prompts.description: Assess a model's governance against banking Model Risk Management principles — robust development/implementation/use, effective validation with independent effective challenge, and sound governance/policies/controls, plus model inventory and ongoing monitoring — without inventing regulatory citations, capital figures, or deadlines.

prompts.title: RAI Model Risk Register
prompts.description: Author and maintain a living model risk register — structured risk entries with severity, likelihood, controls, residual risk, owner, and review cadence — kept current across model and data changes rather than produced once and abandoned.

prompts.title: RAI NIST AI RMF Assessment
prompts.description: Assess an AI system against the NIST AI Risk Management Framework's four functions — GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE — producing a function-by-function maturity gap assessment with evidence, gaps, and prioritized actions, without inventing category identifiers or normative thresholds.

prompts.title: RAI Privacy & PII Assessment
prompts.description: Assess an ML system's privacy risk — PII exposure, membership inference, and memorization — and select proportionate mitigations (minimization, differential privacy) measured against utility, without overclaiming protection.

prompts.title: RAI Red-Teaming Plan
prompts.description: Design a red-teaming plan for an AI system — threat model, attack categories, coverage, and reporting — that measures real failure modes rather than producing anecdotes, and pairs findings with severity and reproducibility.

prompts.title: RAI Sustainability & Carbon Assessment
prompts.description: Estimate and reduce the compute and carbon footprint of training and serving an ML system using measured inputs and stated assumptions, never invented energy or emissions figures.

prompts.title: 3D & Point-Cloud Model Design
prompts.description: Choose a 3D representation (voxel grid, raw point set, mesh, multi-view projection, or range image) and design for permutation and rotation invariance, sensor fusion (LiDAR + camera), and density/sampling — matched to the sensor, task, and compute budget, with scan-overlap-aware evaluation.

prompts.title: CV Annotation Strategy
prompts.description: Design an image/video annotation strategy — label schema, annotation guidelines, edge-case rules, quality control, and tooling — that produces consistent labels matched to the task and metric.

prompts.title: CV Augmentation Strategy Selector
prompts.description: Choose image/video augmentations that genuinely improve robustness to deployment conditions without breaking label validity, distorting class semantics, or creating train/serve mismatch.

prompts.title: CV Object Detection Evaluator
prompts.description: Evaluate an object detector correctly — mAP across IoU thresholds, per-class and per-size breakdowns, confidence/NMS effects, and the small-object and class-imbalance pitfalls that hide behind a single headline number.

prompts.title: CV Segmentation Approach Designer
prompts.description: Choose between semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation for a task and design its evaluation (IoU/Dice/PQ) with boundary precision, class imbalance, and small-region pitfalls accounted for.

prompts.title: CV Task Framing
prompts.description: Translate a fuzzy vision goal into a concrete CV task type (classification / detection / segmentation / keypoint) and derive the label format, metric, and data implications each choice forces.

prompts.title: CV Transfer Learning & Pretrained Backbone Selector
prompts.description: Select a pretrained backbone and adaptation strategy (linear probe / partial fine-tune / full fine-tune) for a vision task with limited data, matching domain gap, data volume, and compute to the right approach.

prompts.title: Computer Vision Video Understanding Design
prompts.description: Design a video-understanding approach — clip/frame sampling, temporal modeling (3D CNN, two-stream, video transformer, or frame-aggregation), task framing (action recognition, temporal action localization, video classification), and leakage-safe evaluation — matched to the data's temporal structure, label granularity, and compute budget.

prompts.title: Medical Imaging Modeling Considerations
prompts.description: Design a medical-imaging modeling approach with DICOM/modality handling, patient-level splits to prevent leakage, class imbalance and external validation strategy, and regulatory / no-diagnostic-claim guardrails — framework-neutral and grounded in the user's data.

prompts.title: OCR Pipeline Design
prompts.description: Design a detect → recognize → post-process OCR pipeline with layout/structure recovery, language/script coverage, and CER/WER-based evaluation — matched to the document types, scripts, and downstream consumers, with template-overfit-aware splits.

prompts.title: Fraud-Graph Modeling Patterns
prompts.description: Model fraud and abuse on heterogeneous graphs (users/devices/transactions) under extreme label scarcity and adversarial drift — with time-respecting features and operating-point evaluation, not just AUC.

prompts.title: GNN Scalability Design
prompts.description: Scale GNN training to large graphs — choose neighbor sampling vs full-graph training, partition and distribute, and reason about memory/throughput tradeoffs and how sampling changes accuracy and the effective receptive field.

prompts.title: Graph Link Prediction Design
prompts.description: Frame a link-prediction task on a graph — define what an edge means, choose a negative-sampling strategy, pick transductive vs inductive (and temporal) splits, and select ranking metrics — without leaking future edges into training.

prompts.title: Graph ML Task Framing
prompts.description: Design a graph machine-learning approach — frame the task (node/edge/graph level), choose a GNN family, plan neighbor sampling for scale, and prevent the leakage that graph splits invite.

prompts.title: Classical NLP Task Framing
prompts.description: Frame a text task before choosing a method — deciding what the unit of prediction is, whether the label set is closed, and whether an LLM or a trained classical model is the right instrument for this volume, latency, and stability profile.

prompts.title: Classical Text Classification Pipeline Designer
prompts.description: Design a non-LLM text classification pipeline — representation, model, evaluation, and class-imbalance handling — with leakage-safe preprocessing and metrics that survive imbalanced, multi-label, or skewed-cost settings.

prompts.title: NER / Span Extraction Design
prompts.description: Design a named-entity / span extraction system — entity schema, annotation and tagging scheme (BIO/BILOU), boundary rules, and span-level evaluation that does not mistake token accuracy for extraction quality.

prompts.title: Robust Text Preprocessing Pipeline Designer
prompts.description: Design a text preprocessing pipeline — normalization, language handling, noise removal — that is reproducible, identical offline and at serving, and free of the silent leakage and information-destruction that quietly degrade NLP models.

prompts.title: Tokenization & Text Representation Strategy
prompts.description: Choose a tokenization scheme and text representation — bag-of-words, TF-IDF, word, or subword embeddings — matched to the task, language, vocabulary behavior, and out-of-vocabulary risk, with a leakage-safe fitting boundary.

prompts.title: Topic Modeling & Unsupervised Text Structure Approach
prompts.description: Approach unsupervised text structure discovery — LDA vs embeddings+clustering — and validate it with coherence, stability, and human interpretability rather than trusting auto-discovered topics at face value.

prompts.title: Anomaly & Outlier Detection Design
prompts.description: Design anomaly/outlier detection under extreme class imbalance — choose unsupervised vs semi-supervised framing, set defensible thresholds, and evaluate with metrics that don't lie when positives are rare.

prompts.title: Audio ML Design (Non-Speech)
prompts.description: Design machine learning on audio that is not speech — sound events, music, machine and bioacoustic signals — choosing the representation against what the signal looks like in time and frequency, and preventing the recording-condition leakage that inflates audio results.

prompts.title: Multimodal Model Architecture Design
prompts.description: Design a multimodal model for a combined-input task — fusion strategy, cross-modal alignment, modality dropout, and missing-modality handling — without assuming a fancy architecture is needed.

prompts.title: Speech Task Framing (ASR / TTS / Diarization)
prompts.description: Frame a speech task — ASR, TTS, or diarization — pinning down its data requirements, the right metrics (WER/CER, MOS, DER), and the acoustic and evaluation pitfalls that fool teams new to audio.

prompts.title: Contextual Bandits & Exploration Design
prompts.description: Decide when and how to use bandits for recommendation — epsilon-greedy / UCB / Thompson sampling, contextual vs non-contextual, off-policy evaluation (IPS / doubly-robust), exploration budget and safety guardrails, and propensity logging that makes future evaluation possible.

prompts.title: Multi-Objective Ranking Design
prompts.description: Balance relevance against diversity, revenue, freshness, and fairness in a single ranker — choose between scalarization (weighted sum), constrained optimization, and Pareto methods, select and validate objective weights, and install guardrail metrics that catch silent degradation.

prompts.title: Recommender Cold-Start Strategy
prompts.description: Design strategies for user, item, and system cold start using content features, popularity priors, onboarding, and exploration — without starving discovery or overfitting to early signal.

prompts.title: Recommender Feedback-Loop & Bias Audit
prompts.description: Audit a recommender for popularity bias, position bias, and self-reinforcing feedback loops — where the system trains on data it generated, entrenching the head and starving discovery — with evidence-backed findings and mitigations.

prompts.title: Recommender Objective ↔ Business Alignment
prompts.description: Align a recommender's training objective with the actual business objective — exposing proxy-metric risk where optimizing the trainable label (clicks, watch-time) quietly degrades the goal it's supposed to serve (retention, revenue, satisfaction).

prompts.title: Recommender Offline Evaluation & the Offline→Online Gap
prompts.description: Evaluate a recommender offline with appropriate ranking metrics and beyond-accuracy measures, and reason rigorously about why offline gains may not translate to online lift due to logged-data bias.

prompts.title: Recommender System Architecture Design
prompts.description: Design an end-to-end recommender (retrieval + ranking, content/collaborative/hybrid) matched to the use case, data, scale, and latency budget.

prompts.title: Sequential & Session-Based Recommendation Design
prompts.description: Model user behavior as an ordered sequence — choose between session-based RNN/transformer/next-item architectures, define session boundaries, balance short- vs long-term intent, handle cold sessions, and design leak-free temporal evaluation.

prompts.title: Two-Stage Candidate Generation & Ranking Design
prompts.description: Design the two-stage retrieval (candidate generation) + ranking pipeline for a recommender — the recall mechanisms, the ranking features and objective, and the handoff between stages — sized to catalog scale and latency.

prompts.title: Multi-Agent RL Design
prompts.description: Design a multi-agent RL setup across cooperative, competitive, or mixed settings — handling non-stationarity from co-adapting agents, centralized-training-decentralized-execution, credit assignment, and evaluation against a population of opponents rather than a single fixed one.

prompts.title: Offline RL Design
prompts.description: Design an offline (batch) RL setup that learns a policy from a fixed logged dataset with no environment interaction — handling distributional shift, out-of-distribution actions, conservative learning methods, and off-policy evaluation before any deployment.

prompts.title: RL Agent Evaluation & Safety
prompts.description: Evaluate an RL agent honestly under high return variance, detect reward hacking and overfitting to the training environment, and build in safety/constraint handling before any deployment claim.

prompts.title: RL Algorithm Family Selection
prompts.description: Choose an RL algorithm family — value-based, policy-gradient, actor-critic, offline, or model-based — by matching it to the action space, data/interaction regime, sample budget, and safety needs of the problem.

prompts.title: RL Environment & Simulator Design
prompts.description: Design or wrap an RL environment/simulator — observation and action spaces, reset/termination semantics, determinism, and the sim-to-real gap — so the thing the agent learns in matches the thing it must act in.

prompts.title: RL Problem Framing & MDP Formulation
prompts.description: Decide whether a problem is genuinely reinforcement learning, and if so formulate it as a well-posed MDP — state, action, reward, transition, horizon — before any algorithm is chosen.

prompts.title: RL Reward Function Design & Hacking Stress-Test
prompts.description: Design a reward function that encodes the true objective, then adversarially stress-test it for reward hacking, unintended optima, and shaping artifacts before training.

prompts.title: RLHF / RLAIF Pipeline Design
prompts.description: Design a preference-optimization pipeline that aligns an LLM or policy from human or AI feedback — preference data collection, reward-model training, the optimization step (PPO vs DPO vs others), and KL/regularization to prevent reward over-optimization.

prompts.title: Hierarchical & Grouped Forecasting
prompts.description: Forecast across an aggregation hierarchy (e.g. SKU → category → region → total) and reconcile the levels into a coherent set, choosing among bottom-up, top-down, middle-out, and optimal (MinT) reconciliation based on where the signal lives in the structure.

prompts.title: Intermittent & Sparse Demand Forecasting
prompts.description: Forecast series dominated by zeros and sporadic demand (spare parts, slow movers) using methods built for intermittency — Croston, SBA, TSB, and zero-inflated approaches — and evaluate them with metrics that don't break on zeros, avoiding MAPE entirely.

prompts.title: Probabilistic Forecasting Design
prompts.description: Design forecasts that output a full distribution or set of quantiles rather than a single point, choosing among quantile regression, conformal prediction, and sampling approaches, scoring with proper rules (pinball / CRPS), and validating that intervals are actually calibrated to their nominal coverage.

prompts.title: Time-Series Anomaly Detection Design
prompts.description: Design a time-series anomaly detector — method, seasonality handling, thresholding, and honest evaluation — that separates real anomalies from seasonal/trend variation and noise, without leaking the future into its baseline.

prompts.title: Time-Series Backtesting Design (Rolling-Origin)
prompts.description: Design rolling-origin / walk-forward backtesting for a forecaster that respects time order — choosing window scheme, gap/horizon alignment, and metrics — so evaluation honestly estimates future performance and never leaks the future.

prompts.title: Time-Series Feature Engineering (Leak-Free)
prompts.description: Engineer time-series features — lags, rolling windows, calendar/event, and exogenous covariates — that capture temporal structure without look-ahead leakage, ensuring every feature uses only information available at prediction time.

prompts.title: Time-Series Forecasting Model Selection
prompts.description: Choose a forecasting approach — classical statistical, ML, or deep learning — matched to the series' structure (trend, seasonality, intermittency), forecast horizon, data volume, and the number of series to forecast.

prompts.title: Time-Series Look-Ahead Leakage Audit
prompts.description: Audit a time-series pipeline specifically for look-ahead / future leakage — features, splits, transforms, and target construction that let information from the future contaminate the past — with evidence-backed findings and fixes.

prompts.title: Time-Series Seasonality & Trend Decomposition
prompts.description: Decompose a series into trend, seasonality, and residual — choosing the right method and period(s), validating the decomposition, and using each component correctly in modeling without introducing look-ahead leakage.

prompts.title: Addressing Alleged Biblical Contradictions — Honest Engagement
prompts.description: Address a specific alleged contradiction in the Bible honestly — presenting the strongest form of the objection, the major harmonization approaches, and acknowledging where genuine tension remains. Not every alleged contradiction has a clean resolution, and that is stated honestly.

prompts.title: Apologetic Conversation Preparation
prompts.description: Prepare for a real apologetic conversation — practice listening, understand the other person's actual position (not a straw man), identify shared values, and plan gracious responses focused on relational and conversational skills, not just arguments.

prompts.title: Biblical Reliability — Evidence and Challenges
prompts.description: Present the evidence for and challenges to biblical reliability — manuscript tradition, archaeological correlation, internal consistency, genre expectations — honestly and with every factual claim verify-required. Not a one-sided defense or attack.

prompts.title: Comparative Worldview Analysis — Biblical and Alternative
prompts.description: Compare the biblical worldview with another worldview (naturalism, Buddhism, Islam, secular humanism, postmodernism, etc.) on a specific question — presenting each from its own best advocates, never caricaturing the alternative, with all philosophical and historical claims verify-required.

prompts.title: Faith and Science Question Framing
prompts.description: Frame a specific faith-and-science question by presenting the range of believing-scholar positions — young earth, old earth, evolutionary creation, etc. — as positions held by identifiable traditions and scholars, never presenting one as THE scientific or THE biblical position.

prompts.title: Intellectual Objection Engagement — Charitable and Honest
prompts.description: Help the user engage charitably with a specific intellectual objection to Christian faith — steelmanning the objection genuinely before presenting multiple Christian response traditions, with all philosophical arguments and historical claims verify-required.

prompts.title: Interfaith Dialogue Preparation — Respectful and Informed
prompts.description: Prepare for interfaith dialogue on a specific topic — presenting the other religion's position from its own best sources, identifying genuine common ground and genuine differences, and preparing for respectful conversation. Never fabricate claims about another religion.

prompts.title: Problem of Evil & Theodicy — Major Positions Presented Fairly
prompts.description: Present the major theodicies (free will, soul-making, greater good, skeptical theism, protest theodicy, etc.) and the strongest objections to each, fairly — including both philosophical and pastoral dimensions, with all philosophical arguments verify-required.

prompts.title: Biblical Author Theology Comparison — Comparing Theological Emphases
prompts.description: Compare two biblical authors' theologies on a user-specified theme (e.g., Paul vs. James on faith/works, John vs. Synoptics on Christology), presenting apparent tensions honestly without harmonizing prematurely or fabricating scholarly positions.

prompts.title: Biblical Theology vs. Systematic Theology — Clarifying the Distinction
prompts.description: Clarify the distinction between biblical theology (attending to individual authors, historical progression, canonical shape) and systematic theology (topical organization, logical coherence, constructive claims) using a user-specified doctrine as a worked example. Show how the same doctrine looks different through each lens.

prompts.title: Center of Biblical Theology Debate — Survey of Proposals
prompts.description: Survey the scholarly debate about whether biblical theology has a 'center' (Mitte) — proposals like covenant, kingdom, God's glory, promise, etc. — presenting each proposal as a position held by identifiable scholars/traditions, with strengths and critiques, all verify-required.

prompts.title: Redemptive-Historical Reading — Passage within the Biblical Storyline
prompts.description: Guide the user to read a specific passage within the creation-fall-redemption-consummation storyline (redemptive-historical hermeneutic), presenting different epoch/era schemes as positions held by identifiable traditions rather than as settled frameworks.

prompts.title: Annual Teaching Calendar — Map Your Church's Preaching & Teaching Year
prompts.description: Map a church's annual preaching and teaching calendar integrating sermon series, holidays, guest speakers, special events, and teaching-ministry rhythms — producing a month-by-month plan with series arcs, open weeks, and coordination notes.

prompts.title: Church Curriculum Scope & Sequence — Multi-Quarter Bible-Teaching Plan
prompts.description: Design a multi-quarter or multi-year scope-and-sequence for a church's Bible-teaching program (kids, youth, adults, or all), ensuring balanced coverage of OT/NT, genres, doctrines, and application areas over time — without fabricating curriculum products, statistics, or publisher claims.

prompts.title: Curriculum Selection & Evaluation — Assess Published Bible-Study Materials
prompts.description: Evaluate published Bible-study curriculum materials against stated criteria — theological alignment, age-appropriateness, pedagogical quality, tradition fit, volunteer-friendliness, and cost — without fabricating product names, authors, reviews, or publisher claims.

prompts.title: Discipleship Pathway Design — Newcomer to Mature Leader
prompts.description: Map a congregation-wide discipleship pathway from newcomer through mature believer to deployed leader — with stage definitions, gate criteria, recommended experiences at each stage, and a plan for people who stall — without fabricating discipleship research or spiritual-maturity metrics.

prompts.title: Midweek Program Design — Bible Study or Prayer Meeting Format
prompts.description: Design a sustainable midweek Bible-study, prayer-meeting, or teaching format that is distinct from Sunday services — covering purpose, format, content cycle, leadership, and sustainability for contexts where volunteer energy and attendance are limited.

prompts.title: Multi-Service Teaching Coordination — Consistent Message Across Communicators
prompts.description: Coordinate consistent teaching across multiple services, campuses, or venues when different communicators deliver the same series — producing a shared outline with non-negotiable anchor points, flexible illustration zones, and communicator-voice guidance.

prompts.title: Sermon Feedback & Debrief — Post-Teaching Review
prompts.description: Run a structured post-sermon or post-teaching debrief — evaluating theological accuracy, textual faithfulness, delivery, audience engagement, and application clarity — producing actionable improvement notes without fabricating audience-response data or communication-science claims.

prompts.title: Small-Group Launch System — Design a Sustainable Group Ministry
prompts.description: Design a small-group system from scratch or restructure an existing one — covering group formation, leader recruitment and training, curriculum cycle, meeting rhythm, reporting and care structures, and launch timeline — without fabricating church-growth statistics or small-group research claims.

prompts.title: Teacher & Volunteer Training Plan — Equip Bible-Study Leaders
prompts.description: Design a training program for Bible-study teachers and volunteers covering hermeneutics basics, age-appropriate teaching methods, handling hard questions, classroom management, and child-safety protocols — producing a session-by-session training plan with objectives and practice activities.

prompts.title: Volunteer Recruitment & Role Design — Teaching Ministry Roles
prompts.description: Design volunteer roles for a Bible-teaching ministry with clear descriptions, time commitments, qualification criteria, onboarding steps, and a recruitment communication plan — without fabricating volunteer statistics or best-practice claims.

prompts.title: Ancient Near Eastern Comparative Context — Parallels Without Fabrication
prompts.description: Identify and analyze parallels between biblical texts and other ancient Near Eastern texts (Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Ugaritic, Hittite, etc.) — classifying each parallel by type and confidence — without inventing text names, fabricating inscriptions, misattributing parallels, or asserting from memory what must be verified in a real critical edition.

prompts.title: Canonical & Intertextual Reading — Trace Echoes, Quotations, and Allusions
prompts.description: Trace how a passage quotes, alludes to, or echoes other parts of Scripture, distinguishing verified textual links (explicit quotations) from probable allusions and from looser thematic association — without fabricating references. Distinguishes what the text demonstrably connects from interpretive construction.

prompts.title: First-Look Passage Observation (Beginner) — What Does the Text Actually Say?
prompts.description: A gentle, beginner-friendly observation prompt that helps a new reader notice what a passage actually says — who, what, where, repeated words, connectors, commands, contrasts — before any interpretation or application. Builds the habit of looking before concluding.

prompts.title: Genre-Aware Reading Guide — Read Each Passage by Its Own Rules
prompts.description: Identify a passage's literary genre (narrative, law, poetry/wisdom, prophecy, gospel, parable, epistle, apocalyptic) and apply the reading conventions that genre requires, so the reader does not, for example, read poetry as legislation or apocalyptic as newspaper. Neutral on contested readings; no fabricated data.

prompts.title: Historical-Cultural Context Reconstruction — Background With Confidence Labels
prompts.description: Assemble the historical and cultural background that bears on a passage — authorship, date, audience, setting, customs, institutions, geography — while labeling each claim by evidentiary confidence and refusing to fabricate archaeological finds, inscriptions, dates, or scholars. Separates background that is well-established from what is debated or speculative.

prompts.title: Literary Context & Discourse Structure — Map a Passage in Its Surroundings
prompts.description: Map a passage's place in its immediate, book-level, and canonical context and analyze its internal structure — argument flow, narrative movement, and structuring devices such as chiasm, inclusio, and parallelism — to show how the shape of the text carries meaning. References by address; no fabricated data.

prompts.title: Multi-View Interpretation Map — Lay Out Competing Readings of a Contested Passage
prompts.description: Map the major competing interpretations of a contested passage or question side by side, each with its strongest textual basis, key assumptions, and the interpretive stream that holds it — taking no side, attributing positions to identifiable streams rather than fabricated scholar names, and marking where the disagreement is genuinely unresolved.

prompts.title: Narrative Analysis — Character, Plot, and Narrator in Biblical Story
prompts.description: Analyze a biblical narrative text using narrative-critical tools — characterization, plot structure and tension, narrator perspective and reliability, gaps and omissions, irony and foreshadowing — showing how narrative technique itself bears theological and literary meaning, while distinguishing what the narrator states from what must be inferred.

prompts.title: Original-Language Word Study (Greek / Hebrew / Aramaic) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Structure a rigorous word study on a Greek, Hebrew, or Aramaic term while refusing to invent lexical data. Presents candidate glosses and semantic range as verify-required, routes the user to named real lexicons and interlinears, labels every claim by confidence, and guards against the etymological and illegitimate-totality-transfer fallacies.

prompts.title: Parable Interpretation — Main Point, Kingdom Context, and the Reversal
prompts.description: Interpret a parable on its own terms — identifying its central point (or limited set of points) without over-allegorizing, reading it in its original audience and kingdom-of-God setting, locating the reversal or 'stinger,' and attributing single-point versus allegorical approaches to identifiable streams. A genre-specific deep-dive that biblical_genre_aware_reading.md routes to.

prompts.title: Reading Hebrew Poetry & the Psalms — Parallelism, Imagery, and Psalm Type
prompts.description: Read a psalm or other Hebrew poetic text by its genre rules — tracing parallelism (synonymous, antithetic, synthetic, and others), weighing imagery and metaphor, respecting poetic terseness, identifying the psalm type (lament, praise, thanksgiving, wisdom, royal, imprecatory), and refusing to read poetry as legislation. A genre-specific deep-dive that biblical_genre_aware_reading.md routes to.

prompts.title: Reading Old Testament Law — Covenant Setting, Law Forms, and Continuity
prompts.description: Read Old Testament law by its genre rules — locating it in its covenant/Sinai setting, distinguishing apodictic from casuistic forms, treating the moral/civil/ceremonial division as an interpretive framework attributed to streams rather than a given, and laying out the continuity/discontinuity debate (how the NT and traditions relate the law to Christians) without ruling. A genre-specific deep-dive that biblical_genre_aware_reading.md routes to.

prompts.title: Reading Prophecy & Apocalyptic Responsibly — Forthtelling, Fulfillment, and Symbol
prompts.description: Interpret prophetic and apocalyptic texts by their genre conventions — distinguishing forthtelling from foretelling, near/already from far/not-yet fulfillment, and symbolic from literal imagery — while attributing eschatological systems (historicist, preterist, futurist, idealist; pre-/a-/post-millennial) to identifiable streams without ruling. A STRONG-GUARD genre-specific deep-dive that biblical_genre_aware_reading.md routes to.

prompts.title: Reading Wisdom Literature — Proverbs, Job, and Ecclesiastes on Their Own Terms
prompts.description: Read wisdom literature by its genre rules — treating a proverb as a general truth rather than an ironclad promise, following the book-level argument of Job and Ecclesiastes, honoring the fear-of-the-LORD frame, and letting the wisdom books converse with one another — while attributing contested readings to identifiable streams. A genre-specific deep-dive that biblical_genre_aware_reading.md routes to.

prompts.title: Rhetorical Analysis — Devices and Persuasive Strategy
prompts.description: Identify and analyze rhetorical devices (chiasm, anaphora, antithesis, inclusio, hyperbole, rhetorical question, irony) and the author's persuasive strategy in a biblical passage — covering Greco-Roman oratorical conventions (for epistles) and Hebrew rhetorical patterns (for prophetic and wisdom texts) — without over-reading structure or claiming devices not supported by the text.

prompts.title: Staged Passage Exegesis Workflow — Observation → Context → Structure → Meaning
prompts.description: Work a single passage through a disciplined exegetical sequence — observation, historical-literary context, structure/flow, key terms, and meaning — attributing every interpretive claim, distinguishing what the text says from what traditions infer, and flagging where readings legitimately diverge. The flagship exegesis prompt of the domain.

prompts.title: Tracing the Argument of an Epistle — Connectors, Logical Flow, and Indicative/Imperative
prompts.description: Trace the argument of a New Testament letter by its genre rules — following logical flow through connectors (therefore, because, but, so that), identifying propositions, grounds, inferences, and exhortations, reading the unit in the letter's occasion and situation, and distinguishing indicative (what is true) from imperative (what to do) — while attributing contested readings to identifiable streams. A genre-specific deep-dive that biblical_genre_aware_reading.md routes to.

prompts.title: Translation Comparison & Variant Notes — Why Renderings Differ
prompts.description: Compare how major translations render a verse and explain the kinds of reasons translations differ — translation philosophy, lexical choice, syntax, and textual-critical variants — without inventing manuscript data, apparatus readings, or specific variant attributions. Routes textual-critical questions to named real resources.

prompts.title: Apprentice Leader Development — Grow the Next Generation of Group Leaders
prompts.description: Design a progressive apprenticeship plan for developing a future Bible-study group leader — with staged responsibilities, observation-to-ownership progression, feedback cadence, and readiness criteria for launch.

prompts.title: Conflict Resolution — Navigate Disagreement and Tension in Groups
prompts.description: Help a Bible-study group leader navigate theological disagreement, personality clashes, or group tension — with strategies for in-the-moment de-escalation, private follow-up, and when to involve church leadership.

prompts.title: Facilitation Dynamics — Manage the Room in Bible-Study Groups
prompts.description: Help a Bible-study group leader manage common facilitation challenges — silence, dominance, tangents, conflict, and emotional disclosure — with specific scripts and strategies, not abstract advice.

prompts.title: Handling Hard Questions — When the Leader Doesn't Know or the Topic Is Controversial
prompts.description: Equip a Bible-study group leader to respond when they can't answer a question, when a topic is theologically controversial, or when someone asks something emotionally charged — with specific response scripts and follow-up plans.

prompts.title: Heretical Claim Response — Gracious Correction in a Group Setting
prompts.description: Help a Bible-study group leader respond graciously and clearly when a participant makes a claim that contradicts ecumenical-creed-level orthodoxy — distinguishing heterodox-but-within-Christianity claims from claims that fall outside historic Christian confession, without adjudicating intra-Christian disputes.

prompts.title: Hybrid & Online Format — Adapt Bible Study for Digital Delivery
prompts.description: Help a Bible-study group leader adapt a study session for hybrid (some in-person, some online) or fully online delivery — covering platform setup, engagement techniques, discussion facilitation, and the unique dynamics of digital groups.

prompts.title: Mixed-Maturity Leveling — Adapt Study for Diverse Spiritual Experience
prompts.description: Help a Bible-study group leader adapt a single study for a group spanning new believers to mature Christians — with layered questions, differentiated engagement, and strategies that challenge the experienced without losing the new.

prompts.title: Bible Reading Habit Builder — Sustainable Daily Practice with Gap Recovery
prompts.description: Help a solo learner build a sustainable daily Bible reading habit — with realistic pacing, a method that makes reading stick, accountability design, and a gap-recovery plan for when life interrupts — so the habit survives beyond the first two weeks.

prompts.title: Book of the Bible Deep Dive — Extended Multi-Week Single-Book Study
prompts.description: Guide a solo learner through an extended, multi-week deep study of a single biblical book — with running questions log, cumulative observation, structured interpretation passes, and a capstone synthesis — building the skill of sustained engagement with one text over time.

prompts.title: Compare Traditions on a Practice — Self-Directed Exploration of How Christians Differ
prompts.description: Guide a solo learner through a self-directed exploration of how different Christian traditions approach a specific practice (baptism, communion, church governance, worship style, Sabbath, spiritual gifts, etc.) — presenting each tradition's biblical reasoning charitably and accurately, without adjudicating which is correct.

prompts.title: Comprehension Self-Check — Explain a Passage Back in Your Own Words (Feynman-Style)
prompts.description: Help a solo learner test their understanding of a passage by explaining it back in their own words and then checking that explanation against the supplied text — surfacing gaps, hidden assumptions, and where understanding is solid vs. shaky. The model checks against the learner's pasted text by address and never supplies verse wording from memory. A personal study tool, not pastoral counseling.

prompts.title: Doctrine Self-Exploration — Explore a Teaching Across Traditions, Descriptively
prompts.description: Help a solo learner explore a doctrine on their own — surveying the relevant passages by address and the range of positions across traditions descriptively, without being catechized toward one view. A personal study tool that maps rather than adjudicates, and is not pastoral counseling or a substitute for one's faith community.

prompts.title: Honest Questions & Doubt Explorer — Work Through a Hard Question Intellectually and Charitably
prompts.description: Help a solo learner work through an honest intellectual question or doubt about a biblical text or topic — laying out the question fairly, the relevant passages by address, and the range of responses across traditions, without dismissing the doubt or forcing a resolution. STRONGLY routes acute faith crisis, mental-health crisis, or distress to a pastor or licensed counselor.

prompts.title: Personal Application Worksheet — Text → Original Point → Timeless Principle → Today
prompts.description: Help a solo learner derive honest personal application from a passage by bridging text → the original audience's point → a timeless principle → today — guarding against eisegesis, moralizing, and turning narrative into a checklist. Works from the learner's supplied text by address; the model never quotes Scripture from memory. A personal study tool, not pastoral counseling.

prompts.title: Reflection Journal Companion — Guided Reflective Journaling Through a Passage or Book
prompts.description: Accompany a solo learner in reflective journaling through a passage or book — generating thoughtful prompts that draw out the learner's own engagement and response, without fabricating Scripture, feelings, or experiences on their behalf. Works from the learner's supplied text by address. A personal study and formation tool, not pastoral counseling.

prompts.title: Self-Directed Study Plan Designer — Pace Your Own Multi-Week Study of a Book or Topic
prompts.description: Help a solo learner design a realistic, paced multi-week plan to study a biblical book or topic on their own — calibrated to available time, prior experience, and goal — with built-in observation/interpretation discipline and anti-fabrication guardrails. A personal study and formation tool, not pastoral counseling.

prompts.title: Self-Guided Character Study — Study a Bible Figure by Address and in Context
prompts.description: Guide a solo learner through studying a biblical figure on their own — gathering the passages by address, reading them in context, and carefully separating what the text actually shows from later tradition, legend, or sermon embellishment. A personal study tool, not pastoral counseling.

prompts.title: Self-Quiz & Recall Drill — Test Your Memory and Comprehension on YOUR Supplied Text
prompts.description: Help a solo learner self-test recall and comprehension of a passage or book — but only on text the learner supplies in a named translation. The model never quotes Scripture from memory and never quizzes on wording it generated; questions are built strictly from the learner's pasted text. A personal study tool, not pastoral counseling.

prompts.title: Study-Tool Skill Builder — Use Concordances, Lexicons, Study Bibles, and Commentaries Responsibly
prompts.description: Teach a solo learner how to use Bible study tools (concordance, lexicon, study Bible, cross-references, commentary) well — with anti-fabrication front and center: how to verify what a tool tells you, how to read it critically, and how not to be misled by glosses, agendas, or the model's own memory. A personal study tool, not pastoral counseling.

prompts.title: Biblical Care Conversation Foundations — Encouragement, Not Counseling
prompts.description: Frame a Scripture-rooted care or encouragement conversation — listening well, choosing passages by address that fit the person's actual situation, and offering honest comfort and hope — while staying firmly inside non-clinical lay-care boundaries and routing mental-health, abuse, self-harm, suicidality, and crises to licensed professionals and emergency services. Tradition-neutral; no proof-texting at suffering people.

prompts.title: College / Young Adult Study Designer — Identity, Vocation, and Doubt for 18-30
prompts.description: Design a Bible study for college students or young adults (18-30) that engages the text seriously while addressing the questions this age group is actually asking — identity, vocation, doubt, deconstruction, relationships, justice, and how faith survives the transition to adulthood.

prompts.title: Family Devotions Designer — Short, Participatory, Sustainable
prompts.description: Design household devotions that work across mixed ages — short, participatory, and sustainable — anchored in a passage referenced by address and built from user-supplied text. Scales one shared moment so a toddler and a teen can both engage, keeps it age-safe, and favors a rhythm a real family can actually keep.

prompts.title: Kids' Bible Lesson Builder — Age-Appropriate, Faithful, Engaging
prompts.description: Design a complete children's Bible lesson — objectives, hook, the story told faithfully and accessibly, a hands-on activity, a simple application, and a take-home — calibrated to a stated age band, with the text referenced by address and built on user-supplied verse text. Keeps the content age-safe, concrete, and active without distorting what the passage actually says.

prompts.title: Marriage Enrichment Bible Study Designer
prompts.description: Design a couples' Bible study that handles patriarchal context and gender-role texts honestly — presenting complementarian, egalitarian, and moderate readings without adjudicating — while engaging real marital themes (communication, conflict, intimacy, roles, forgiveness) with biblical grounding drawn from the full canon, not just Ephesians 5.

prompts.title: Men's / Women's Study Designer — Gender-Specific Depth Without Stereotyping
prompts.description: Design a Bible study for a men's or women's group that takes the text seriously, addresses life concerns common to the group, and handles gender-role passages with tradition-neutral honesty — without stereotyping, flattening the text, or proof-texting.

prompts.title: New Believer Discipleship Path — Staged First Steps and Foundations
prompts.description: Design a staged discipleship path for a new believer — first steps, core practices, foundational passages by address, and a realistic pace — that grounds someone in Scripture and basic Christian practice while staying neutral on contested specifics (baptism mode, spiritual gifts, end times) and attributing differing views to identifiable streams.

prompts.title: Parenting Scripture Guide — Contextualized, Not Proof-Texted
prompts.description: Help a ministry leader select and present parenting-relevant Scripture responsibly — contextualizing Proverbs as wisdom literature (probabilities, not promises), handling discipline texts honestly across traditions, presenting the full range of biblical parenting themes (not just obedience and correction), and grounding the study in what the texts actually say in their literary and historical context.

prompts.title: Scripture Guide for Grief & Loss Ministry
prompts.description: Guide a ministry leader through selecting and presenting Scripture for grief and loss contexts — covering the full range of biblical grief literature (lament, protest, honest despair, and hope) rather than cherry-picking comfort texts — with tradition-neutral presentation, anti-proof-texting discipline, and a firm boundary routing clinical grief counseling, complicated grief, and mental-health crisis to licensed professionals.

prompts.title: Seeker's Introduction to the Bible — Honest, Non-Coercive Orientation
prompts.description: Introduce the Bible to a curious skeptic or seeker in a way that is genuinely informative, non-coercive, and honest about the text's difficulty and diversity — orienting them to what the Bible is, how to start reading, and where to ask hard questions, without pressure tactics, hidden agendas, or pretending the hard parts away.

prompts.title: Seniors Bible Study Designer — Legacy, Loss, Hope, and Faithful Aging
prompts.description: Design a Bible study for older adults (60+) that takes the text seriously while addressing the concerns of this life stage — legacy, loss and grief, declining health, retirement identity, grandparenting, mortality, and sustaining hope — with accessibility considerations for hearing, vision, mobility, and cognitive changes.

prompts.title: Special Program Session Designer — VBS / Camp / Retreat Teaching
prompts.description: Design a teaching session (or a themed multi-session arc) for a special program — VBS, camp, or retreat — with a unifying theme, energy and age scaling across sessions, faithful handling of the passages by address, and clear takeaways. Keeps content age-safe and routes illustrations and care concerns to the right prompts.

prompts.title: Youth Bible Study Designer — Real Depth, Real Relevance, Honest Questions
prompts.description: Design a teen/youth Bible study that takes the text seriously and the students seriously at once — balancing genuine relevance to adolescent life with real exegetical depth, inviting hard questions and answering them honestly, and avoiding preachiness. References Scripture by address from user-supplied text and keeps contested points neutral.

prompts.title: Biblical Aramaic Analysis — Syntax, Grammar & Dialect Context — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Structure a disciplined analysis of a Biblical Aramaic passage the user supplies — verb stems and aspect, noun states (construct/absolute/emphatic), syntax, vocabulary with Hebrew cognates, and the relationship of Biblical Aramaic to Imperial/Official Aramaic and other dialects — treating every grammatical label, vocabulary gloss, and dialect classification as candidate / verify-required against standard Aramaic grammars (flagged verify, no section/page numbers from memory), and attributing interpretation-bearing divergence to streams without ruling.

prompts.title: Canon & Versification Differences Across Traditions — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Map where a user-specified book or passage appears across canonical traditions (Protestant, Catholic, Orthodox, Ethiopian, Jewish Tanakh ordering), note versification differences (Psalm numbering MT vs. LXX, chapter/verse splits), and identify books present in some canons but not others — treating every canon-inclusion claim and versification datum as verify-required against each tradition's own published canon lists and numbered editions.

prompts.title: Comparative Semitics & Cognate Analysis (Hebrew / Aramaic) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Help the user evaluate a comparative-Semitic / cognate argument about a Hebrew or Aramaic word or construction — weighing evidence from Ugaritic, Akkadian, Arabic, and other Semitic languages — while teaching the method's controls (attestation, semantic plausibility, illegitimate totality/cognate transfer) and treating every cognate form, gloss, and attestation claim as candidate / verify-required against the comparative lexica, never asserted from memory.

prompts.title: Discourse / Clause-Flow Analysis — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Structure a methodology-forward discourse analysis of a user-supplied text — prominence/foregrounding, cohesion and connectives, paragraph/episode boundaries, and information structure (topic/focus, given/new) — treating every analytical label as candidate / verify-required, routing competing discourse models to named resources without ruling, and never fabricating original-language data, frequencies, or model citations.

prompts.title: Greek & Hebrew Vocabulary Builder — Frequency-Based Study Plan — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Design a staged, frequency-based vocabulary acquisition plan for Biblical Greek or Biblical Hebrew — organizing words by frequency tiers (most common first), integrating spaced repetition and reading-in-context checkpoints, and calibrating the schedule to the user's time budget — treating every word-list datum (frequency count, gloss, semantic range, principal parts, cognate claim) as candidate / verify-required against standard frequency lists and lexica, and never asserting specific word data from memory.

prompts.title: Greek Syntax & Grammar Analysis (NT / LXX) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Structure a disciplined syntactic analysis of a Greek clause the user supplies — case functions, tense-aspect/Aktionsart, mood, voice, clause types, participles, and conditional structures — treating every syntactic label as candidate / verify-required, routing to standard reference grammars (flagged verify, no page/section numbers from memory), and attributing syntax-dependent interpretive divergence to streams without ruling.

prompts.title: Greek Verbal Aspect & Aktionsart Analysis — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Help the user analyze the verbal aspect of a Greek verb form they supply — distinguishing grammatical aspect (perfective / imperfective / stative) from temporal reference and from lexically-conditioned Aktionsart — while presenting the competing aspect frameworks (Fanning, Porter, Campbell, Olsen) descriptively, never ruling between them, and treating every aspect label and grammar citation as candidate / verify-required.

prompts.title: Greek Voice & Deponency Analysis — Middle, Passive & the Deponency Debate — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Help the user analyze the voice of a Greek verb form they supply — the interpretive contribution of middle and passive, the active/middle/passive distinctions, and the contested category of 'deponency' (and the newer middle-only / lexical-middle analyses that challenge it) — treating every voice label as candidate / verify-required, presenting the deponency debate as a live debate, and flagging grammar citations verify-required, never asserted from memory.

prompts.title: Hebrew Cantillation (Te'amim) & Greek Accentuation Analysis — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Help the user read the supralinear/sublinear marking systems of the biblical text — Hebrew cantillation accents (te'amim) as a reading-and-division tradition (disjunctive vs. conjunctive, major pausal breaks) and Greek accent/breathing marks (acute/grave/circumflex, rough/smooth, enclitics, accent-distinguished homographs) — treating every specific accent reading, disjunctive-rank claim, and pausal-division decision as candidate / verify-required against BHS/BHQ and standard grammars, never asserted from memory.

prompts.title: Hebrew Masorah & Qere/Ketiv Analysis (BHS/BHQ) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Help the user read and interpret the Masoretic apparatus of a Hebrew text they supply — the Masorah parva/magna notes and Qere/Ketiv (written vs. read) divergences — explaining what the system encodes about transmission and reading tradition, while treating every specific Masoretic note, Qere/Ketiv reading, and frequency datum as verify-required against BHS/BHQ and Masoretic reference works, never asserted from memory.

prompts.title: Hebrew Syntax & Grammar Analysis (Biblical Hebrew / Aramaic) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Structure a disciplined syntactic analysis of a Biblical Hebrew (or Aramaic) clause the user supplies — the verbal system and aspect/tense debate, waw-consecutive, construct chains, word order and clause types, and particles — treating every syntactic label as candidate / verify-required, routing to standard reference grammars (flagged verify, no section/page numbers from memory), and attributing syntax-dependent interpretive divergence to streams without ruling.

prompts.title: Koine Register, Papyri & Inscriptions Analysis — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Help the user evaluate how documentary evidence — papyri, inscriptions, and ostraca — bears on the register, dialect, and word usage of a Greek word or construction in the NT/LXX, teaching disciplined use of the documentary record while treating every papyrus/inscription citation, dating, provenance, and parallel-usage claim as candidate / verify-required against the editions and lexica, never asserted from memory.

prompts.title: OT-in-NT Usage Analysis (MT / LXX / NT Citation) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Analyze how a New Testament text uses an Old Testament quotation or allusion: compare the wording across the Masoretic Text, the Septuagint, and the NT citation (all supplied by the user), classify the kind of use, and attribute interpretive approaches to identifiable streams — while NEVER fabricating textual apparatus, versification, or which-textual-tradition claims, and routing every wording and variant question to named real resources.

prompts.title: Original-Language Idiom & Figures-of-Speech Analysis (Greek / Hebrew / Aramaic) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Help the user identify and interpret idioms, fixed expressions, and figures of speech in an original-language phrase they supply — where a wooden, word-by-word reading misleads (e.g., Hebrew 'lifted up his eyes,' 'heart' as mind/will, anthropomorphism; Greek idiom and Semitic-influenced expressions) — treating every claimed idiom, idiomatic gloss, and figure classification as candidate / verify-required against lexica and reference grammars, and never inventing a cultural or idiomatic claim to explain a phrase.

prompts.title: Parsing & Morphology Helper (Greek / Hebrew / Aramaic) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Structure and VERIFY the parsing/morphology of an original-language form the user supplies. The model lays out the checking procedure, explains what each parsing slot means, names real tools, and treats any parse it offers as candidate / verify-required — never asserting morphology, lemmas, or Strong's numbers from memory as authoritative.

prompts.title: Semantic Domains & Componential Analysis (Louw-Nida / BDAG) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Help the user disambiguate a word's sense in its context using the method of semantic-domain analysis — mapping the term's candidate senses to domains (Louw-Nida for Greek, comparable domain tools for Hebrew), comparing it with near-synonyms and antonyms in the same field, and letting context select the component — while treating every domain assignment, sense, and synonym relationship as candidate / verify-required against the actual lexica, never asserted from memory.

prompts.title: Septuagint (LXX) Usage & Masoretic Text Divergences — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Structure a disciplined analysis of where the Septuagint diverges from the Masoretic Text for a user-specified passage — classifying each divergence type (translation technique, Vorlage difference, theological interpretation, scribal), assessing interpretive significance, and noting NT citations — treating every textual claim as candidate / verify-required, requiring the user to supply BOTH texts, and attributing scholarly approaches to streams without ruling.

prompts.title: Textual Criticism Primer (Method + User-Supplied Variant) — Structured, Anti-Fabrication
prompts.description: Walk a user through how textual criticism evaluates a specific variant they supply — external evidence (manuscript families, dates, geographic distribution), internal evidence (lectio difficilior, scribal tendencies, harmonization) — presenting the method and major text-critical positions while treating every manuscript attribution, apparatus datum, and reading as verify-required against NA28/UBS5/BHS apparatus.

prompts.title: Daily Devotional Writer — Text, Reflection, Application, Prayer
prompts.description: Draft a short daily devotional anchored to an accurately quoted passage (supplied by the user): a brief reflection grounded in the text, one honest application, and a closing prayer. Stays neutral on contested doctrine and avoids fabricated facts or quotes.

prompts.title: Evangelistic Message Preparation — Text-Driven, Honest, Non-Manipulative Gospel Presentation
prompts.description: Build a text-driven gospel-presentation message anchored in an actual passage (by address, user-supplied text), clear about the gospel, honest and non-manipulative, sensitive to the audience, and tradition-neutral on contested soteriological specifics — attributing differing framings to streams rather than adjudicating.

prompts.title: Expository Sermon Preparation Workflow — From Exegesis to Text-Driven Outline
prompts.description: Move from exegesis to a preachable expository outline: establish the text's meaning in context, distill the big idea, build points that come from the text's own structure, and bridge to application — without overclaiming what the text says or fabricating support. Neutral on contested doctrine; routes illustrations to the guarded illustration prompt.

prompts.title: Lectionary Sermon Prep — Preach from Assigned Readings
prompts.description: Prepare a sermon from lectionary-assigned readings (user supplies the readings) — weaving multiple texts into a unified message with a shared theological thread, while handling the unique challenges of lectionary preaching: texts chosen for you, multiple readings, and the tension between the lectionary's logic and your congregation's context.

prompts.title: Liturgical Calendar Devotional Series — Seasonal Arc from Advent to Ordinary Time
prompts.description: Design a devotional series following the liturgical calendar — Advent, Christmas, Epiphany, Lent, Holy Week, Easter, Pentecost, and Ordinary Time — with daily or weekly readings, reflections, and practices appropriate to each season, without fabricating liturgical dates, lectionary readings, or tradition-specific claims.

prompts.title: Occasional Message Preparation — Funerals, Weddings, Dedications, and Milestones
prompts.description: Prepare a short message for a life occasion (funeral, wedding, dedication, milestone) anchored to a chosen text, pastorally appropriate to the occasion and audience — including non-religious attendees — honest, with no fabricated facts about the people involved (the user supplies those), and tradition-neutral on contested points.

prompts.title: Prayer & Journaling Prompt Generator — Passage-Linked
prompts.description: Generate prayer and journaling prompts linked to a passage and the user's situation — drawing honest connections between the text and the reader's life, scaled to context — without fabricating content or steering toward a contested doctrine.

prompts.title: Scripture Meditation & Reflection Guide — Slow, Reflective Engagement
prompts.description: Guide a reader in slow, reflective engagement with a passage — read, reflect, respond, rest — using the reader's own supplied text, drawing out the passage's point through gentle questions, without imposing a single interpretive tradition or fabricating content.

prompts.title: Sermon / Teaching Series Planner — Multi-Week Arc Over a Book or Theme
prompts.description: Plan a multi-week sermon or teaching series over a book or theme: divide the material into preachable units (by address), give each week a big idea and focus, sequence them into a coherent arc, and note pacing — without overclaiming or fabricating content. Neutral on contested doctrine.

prompts.title: Sermon Delivery Coaching — Self-Assessment and Improvement
prompts.description: Coach a preacher on delivery skills — pacing, manuscript vs. notes, managing nerves, vocal variety, eye contact, and self-assessment — producing a personal delivery improvement plan based on the preacher's self-reported strengths and struggles.

prompts.title: Sermon Illustration Developer — Fitting Illustrations Without Fabricated Facts
prompts.description: Develop illustrations that genuinely fit a sermon's point — by type and structure — while categorically refusing to invent quotes, statistics, historical anecdotes, news events, scientific claims, or attributions. Every factual claim is marked verify-before-use; the preacher supplies or verifies the facts.

prompts.title: Sermon Manuscript Draft — Convert Outline to Oral-Delivery Manuscript
prompts.description: Convert a sermon outline into a full manuscript formatted for oral delivery — with spoken-language phrasing, transition markers, pace/pause cues, and illustration placement — without fabricating illustrations, statistics, quotes, or story details.

prompts.title: Text-to-Application Bridge Builder — From Original Point to Faithful Today
prompts.description: Derive faithful contemporary application from a passage by first establishing the text's original point, abstracting the timeless principle, and only then transferring it to today's situations — guarding against eisegesis, moralizing, and application the text doesn't support. Neutral on contested readings.

prompts.title: Topical Sermon Preparation — Gather Multiple Texts on a Theme Without Proof-Texting
prompts.description: Prepare a topical (vs. expository) message that gathers multiple passages on a theme, with a strong guard against proof-texting: every text is read in its own context, weighted by how directly it addresses the topic, and contested points are flagged and attributed to streams. Contrasts with single-passage expository prep.

prompts.title: Inductive Bible Study (Observation / Interpretation / Application)
prompts.description: Run the classic inductive (OIA) study method on a chosen passage — disciplined observation, then interpretation grounded in observation, then application grounded in interpretation — keeping the three stages distinct and resisting the jump straight to application. Neutral on contested readings; no fabricated data.

prompts.title: Personalized Reading Plan Designer — Paced and Sustainable
prompts.description: Design a Bible reading plan calibrated to the reader's time budget, experience, and goal — chronological, canonical, thematic, whole-Bible, or single-book — with realistic daily portions, checkpoints, and catch-up strategy. References by address; does not reproduce Scripture text.

prompts.title: SOAP Study Method — Scripture, Observation, Application, Prayer
prompts.description: A short, structured personal-study routine for daily reading: copy the Scripture accurately, note observations, draw a specific application, and respond in prayer. Beginner-friendly, sustainable, and honest — no fabricated quotes, no imposed tradition.

prompts.title: Scripture Memorization & Retention Plan — Spaced, Verse-Accurate
prompts.description: Design a spaced-repetition memorization schedule for a passage or set of verses, using a translation the user names, with exact wording supplied by the user, plus review cadence, chunking strategy, and recall checks. Requires verse-accurate text; never quotes Scripture from memory.

prompts.title: Small-Group Discussion Guide Builder — Open, Text-Grounded Questions
prompts.description: Generate a discussion guide for a small group or Sunday-school class: open, text-grounded questions that move from observation to interpretation to application, scaled to group maturity, presenting multiple readings where a passage is contested rather than steering toward one answer.

prompts.title: Teaching Lesson Plan Builder — Objectives, Flow, Application, Assessment
prompts.description: Produce a timed lesson plan for a Bible class or Sunday-school session: learning objectives, a hook, teaching blocks grounded in the text, discussion and activity, application, and a simple assessment of understanding — scaled to audience age/maturity and neutral on contested interpretation.

prompts.title: Thematic / Topical Study Across Passages — Without Proof-Texting
prompts.description: Gather and organize the passages that bear on a biblical theme or topic, weighing each by how directly it addresses the theme and in what context, while guarding against proof-texting and refusing to invent cross-references. Distinguishes passages that genuinely teach the theme from those merely associated with it.

prompts.title: Whole-Book Overview & Synthesis — Structure, Themes, Purpose, Flow
prompts.description: Build a structured overview of an entire biblical book — its structure, major themes, purpose, argument or narrative flow, and place in the canon — distinguishing well-established features from debated questions (authorship, date, occasion) and attributing contested judgments to streams. No fabricated data.

prompts.title: Biblical Basis for a Worship Practice — Cross-Tradition Survey
prompts.description: Examine the biblical basis for a specific worship practice (baptism mode, communion frequency, liturgical prayer, singing psalms vs. hymns, use of instruments, ordination requirements, head coverings, speaking in tongues in worship, etc.) — presenting how different traditions ground their practice in Scripture, without adjudicating which practice is 'the biblical one.'

prompts.title: Biblical Ethics — Framing a Moral Question Across Scripture and Traditions
prompts.description: Frame a moral or ethical question against the biblical material and the major ethical traditions: gather the relevant texts (by address, in context), separate what the text describes from what it commands, account for cultural distance and genuine diversity in Scripture, and present the competing ethical frameworks descriptively without issuing a verdict or fabricating sources.

prompts.title: Canonical Theme Trajectory Tracer — A Theme's Development Across the Canon
prompts.description: Trace how a theme develops across the canon — its introduction, development, turning points, and culmination — distinguishing development the texts themselves demonstrate (by address) from theological construction a tradition supplies, and noting where the trajectory is read differently across traditions. No fabricated references.

prompts.title: Church Government & Polity — NT Material and Tradition Claims
prompts.description: Examine the New Testament material relevant to church government (elders, deacons, bishops, apostles, congregational authority, etc.) and show how different polity systems (episcopal, presbyterian, congregational, connexional, etc.) claim biblical warrant for their structure — presenting each system's strongest biblical case and the strongest objections it faces, without asserting one polity as 'the NT model.'

prompts.title: Comparing Interpretive Views (Debate Format) — Steelman Each Side
prompts.description: Stage a fair, structured comparison of the major positions on a disputed biblical or theological question — each steelmanned with its best arguments and evidence, its responses to objections, and the points where the evidence is genuinely contested — without declaring a winner or fabricating sources.

prompts.title: Creed & Confession Analysis Against Biblical Texts
prompts.description: Analyze a creed or confession (Nicene, Apostles', Westminster, Augsburg, etc.) against the biblical texts it claims or implies — mapping each claim to supporting and challenging biblical material, and presenting how different traditions read the relationship between creed and Scripture — without adjudicating which reading is correct.

prompts.title: Cross-Reference & Typology Mapper — Verified Links vs. Interpretive Typology
prompts.description: Map cross-references and typological connections for a passage or figure, sharply distinguishing explicit textual links (quotations the text itself makes) from probable allusions and from interpretive typology that traditions construct — referencing everything by address, refusing to fabricate references, and noting where a typological reading is contested.

prompts.title: Doctrine Study (Multi-Tradition, Descriptive) — Examine a Doctrine Fairly
prompts.description: Examine a single doctrine across the major interpretive traditions, presenting each position descriptively — its core claim, biblical basis (by address), internal logic, and main objections — labeling each as a position held by a tradition rather than asserting one as fact, and refusing to fabricate sources.

prompts.title: Evaluating & Comparing Commentaries — By Type, Tradition, and Fit for Your Question
prompts.description: Help a user evaluate or choose among commentaries by type (technical/exegetical, expository/pastoral, devotional, critical/academic, application), by interpretive tradition, and by what questions each kind is good for — without inventing specific titles, authors, publishers, or page references. The user supplies which commentaries they actually have; the model structures the evaluation and flags any specific bibliographic claim as verify-required.

prompts.title: Exegetical Fallacy Detector — Scan an Interpretation for Word-Study, Grammatical, Logical, Historical, and Systemic Errors
prompts.description: Scan an interpretation or argument the user supplies for common exegetical fallacies — word-study fallacies, grammatical misuse, logical errors, historical/background overreach, and theological-system imposition — naming each fallacy descriptively, showing where it occurs, and suggesting the disciplined alternative, without itself fabricating lexical or historical data.

prompts.title: Hard / Difficult Passage Analysis — Apparent Contradictions and Hard Sayings
prompts.description: Work through a 'problem' passage — an apparent contradiction, ethical difficulty, or obscure text — by stating the difficulty precisely, surveying the proposed resolutions across interpretive traditions with their strengths and weaknesses, and being honest about what remains genuinely hard, without forcing a verdict or fabricating sources.

prompts.title: Historical Theology — How a Doctrine Developed Across Church History
prompts.description: Trace how a doctrine developed across church history — patristic, medieval, Reformation, and modern periods — presenting the movement descriptively, attributing every position to identifiable figures and streams, and marking every name, council, work, and date as verify-required. No invented figures, quotations, dates, or sources.

prompts.title: Historical-Cultural Background Research Brief — Sourced and Confidence-Labeled
prompts.description: Produce a structured background research brief for a passage, topic, or period — geography, customs, institutions, chronology, and social context — organized with a source-type catalog, every claim confidence-labeled and routed to named real resources for verification, and no invented archaeological, historical, or bibliographic data.

prompts.title: Stress-Test Your Own Theological Position — The Charitable Adversary
prompts.description: Take a theological or interpretive position the user already holds and stress-test it charitably: surface its load-bearing assumptions, steelman the strongest opposing case, locate its weakest links and the cruxes it turns on, and identify what would strengthen it versus what should give the user pause — without straw-manning the other side, fabricating sources, or imposing a verdict.

prompts.title: Theological Research Source Map — Bibliography by Source-Type, Not Invented Titles
prompts.description: Build a research source map for a doctrine or theological question by describing the KINDS of real resources to consult — standard reference works, journal categories, primary vs. secondary sources, confessional vs. critical literature — and how to find and evaluate them, without ever inventing book titles, authors, or article citations. The user assembles and verifies the real bibliography.

prompts.title: Theology of a Single Biblical Book — Its Distinctive Contribution
prompts.description: Synthesize the distinctive theological contribution of a single biblical book — its portrait of God, its central argument or burden, its recurring emphases, and how those relate to the rest of the canon — grounding every claim in the book's own text (by address, in context), distinguishing the book's emphases from later systematic categories, and attributing contested readings to streams without fabricating sources.

prompts.title: Topical / Systematic Theology Synthesis — Across Scripture and Traditions
prompts.description: Synthesize what Scripture and the major interpretive traditions say on a doctrine or topic: gather the relevant texts (in context, by address), organize the biblical data, and present the positions of identifiable traditions descriptively — attributing claims, preserving disagreement, and refusing to invent citations, scholars, or councils.

prompts.title: AI Agent Build-vs-Buy-vs-Hybrid Decision
prompts.description: Recommends build, buy, or hybrid for an agent capability by testing whether customization creates durable advantage, offloading undifferentiated infrastructure, and judging on business outcomes rather than token cost.

prompts.title: AI Product Moat Narrative & Data Flywheel
prompts.description: Builds a defensibility narrative for an AI product when the model is a commodity — codifying domain expertise into context, compounding accuracy via expert feedback, designing a data flywheel, and mapping integration-depth switching cost.

prompts.title: Agentic AI Use-Case Portfolio Prioritization
prompts.description: Scores and sequences a portfolio of candidate agent use cases against an amplify-or-eliminate screen, a complexity-maturity ladder, and a trust-delegation spectrum, surfacing data/context readiness as the real blocker.

prompts.title: Build an Enterprise AI Platform Strategy Brief
prompts.description: A board/executive brief that frames an enterprise AI platform decision: the problem being solved, the buy-vs-build-vs-partner options, the key trade-offs (lock-in, capability, cost, talent), and a recommendation with its invalidation conditions.

prompts.title: Estimate the Cost of Switching AI Vendors in a Future Window
prompts.description: A structured estimate of what it would cost — in dollars, time, and accumulated-context loss — to switch primary AI model vendors at a future date, so vendor-lock-in decisions are made with real numbers instead of vibes.

prompts.title: Evaluate Whether a Capability Compounds or Stays Flat Over Time
prompts.description: A diagnostic that separates AI-enabled capabilities that compound (each use makes the next use better) from capabilities that stay flat (each use is independent), so investment is directed where compounding actually occurs.

prompts.title: Map Where Organizational Understanding Accumulates
prompts.description: A structured audit of where your organization's working knowledge actually lives — across tools, documents, and individual heads — to identify what AI agents can reach, what they can't, and where context gaps will silently degrade AI leverage.

prompts.title: Expansion vs Pocketing AI Savings: A Board-Ready Brief
prompts.description: A board-ready brief that frames the choice between reinvesting AI-driven productivity gains into expansion (new products, segments, capacity) or pocketing them as cost savings / margin improvement — with the specific numbers, strategic logic, and invalidation conditions on both sides.

prompts.title: Founder Bottleneck & Week-Away Test
prompts.description: Help a founder stop being the operational bottleneck by defining founder-only work, mapping what routes through them, stress-testing each path with the week-away test, and deciding what to automate, delegate, or keep.

prompts.title: Leadership-Team Audit of Ambition Level Given AI Leverage
prompts.description: A structured audit the leadership team runs together to test whether current plans reflect the leverage AI actually provides — or whether the org is still planning as if AI weren't there. Surfaces the gap between stated ambition and revealed ambition.

prompts.title: Roadmap for Turning Domain Experts into Builders
prompts.description: A phased roadmap that turns the organization's non-engineering domain experts (analysts, ops, legal, finance, clinicians, etc.) into first-draft builders using AI — without pretending they become engineers — and specifies what engineering must still own.

prompts.title: Workflow Redesign: Compress Insight-to-Action Lead Time
prompts.description: Redesign a specific decision workflow so the time between a real insight surfacing and a decision or action being taken shrinks materially — by removing handoffs, coupling data to owners, and relocating decisions where context actually lives.

prompts.title: Account Health Assessment & Risk Identification
prompts.description: Assess a customer account's health from usage, support, and relationship signals, classify churn risk, and produce a prioritized retention play with owners and a renewal timeline.

prompts.title: Campaign Brief Development from Business Goals
prompts.description: Translate a business goal into a campaign brief: audience, message hierarchy, channel mix, budget split, success metrics, and the assumptions the plan depends on.

prompts.title: Content Performance Analysis & Gap Identification

prompts.title: Regret Minimization Across Time Horizons

prompts.title: Regulatory Risk Radar

Its central discipline is separating decision-judgment from outcome-judgment — a good decision can yield a bad outcome and vice versa — so that lessons attach to the process, not the luck. Output is a reusable AAR with lessons tagged by domain for retrieval.

prompts.title: Decision Log Entry — Append-Only Running Record

Far lighter than a full options memo — built to accumulate in a markdown file or database as a searchable institutional record. Includes an explicit upgrade rule for when an entry's stakes or contestedness demand a full options memo instead.

prompts.title: Executive One-Pager — Whole Decision in 60 Seconds
