Distinct from the TL;DR of an options memo — this is the standalone artifact for a board, CEO, or principal who needs the entire picture in under a minute, with nothing else to fall back on.

prompts.title: Narrative Decision Memo — Six-Page Amazon-Style Prose Memo
prompts.description: Produce a narrative (prose, not bullets) decision memo in the Amazon six-pager tradition: problem, context, options, recommendation, and a mandatory FAQ. Designed to be read silently in the first minutes of a meeting and then interrogated. The FAQ is where the document does its hardest work — it pre-answers the questions a sharp, skeptical reader would raise. Distinct from the structured options memo: this is narrative-first, optimized for silent reading and live challenge.

prompts.title: Options Memo — Multi-Option Decision Memo with Recommendation
prompts.description: Standard structure for a decision memo that presents 2–4 options against shared criteria, makes a recommendation with reasoning, names the strongest objections to the recommendation, and specifies what would have to be true to revisit. Designed to make decisions auditable and to focus discussion on the load-bearing tradeoffs rather than presentation.

prompts.title: Post-Decision Review — Calibration Against Prior Expectations
prompts.description: Run at a pre-committed checkpoint (e.g., 6 months after a hire, 1 year after a major decision), this review compares the actual outcome to what you predicted at decision time — not merely to 'good vs bad.' Because hindsight makes most outcomes look obvious, the review forces an honest comparison against the original calibrated expectations: predicted vs actual, calibration delta, surprises, and calibration lessons for future decisions of the same type. Counters hindsight bias and outcome bias by anchoring to recorded forecasts.

prompts.title: Select and Apply the Right Prioritization Framework
prompts.description: Given a list of items and the surrounding context, recommend the best-fit prioritization framework (RICE, ICE, WSJF, MoSCoW, Kano, Eisenhower, or value/effort), justify the choice against the situation, then apply it — producing a ranked, tiered list with all scoring math shown and every guessed input flagged.

prompts.title: 2x2 Scenario Matrix — Build Four Futures from Two Critical Uncertainties
prompts.description: Identify the two most critical and uncertain drivers shaping a strategic question, cross them into four scenarios, and develop each scenario as a coherent narrative with implications, signposts, and robust strategy candidates. Designed for medium-to-long-horizon planning under deep uncertainty.

prompts.title: Backcasting — Work Backward from a Desired or Feared Future
prompts.description: Specify a desired or feared end-state at a defined future date, then work backward in time to identify the chain of events, decisions, and conditions that would produce it. Surfaces what would have to be true at each interim milestone, distinguishes load-bearing assumptions from incidental ones, and exposes the earliest decisions that gate the path.

prompts.title: Multi-Horizon Roadmap — Three Horizons of Now, Next, and Later with a Resource-Balance Check
prompts.description: Build a three-horizons roadmap (defend the core / build adjacencies / create future options) that names what gets resourced, what gets monitored, and the kill criterion at each horizon, then forces an honest reconciliation between actual time-and-budget allocation and stated strategy. Counters the failure where organizations over-fund the present and starve the future (or chase the future and neglect the engine paying for it).

prompts.title: Robustness Test — Rate a Strategy Across All Scenarios and Find the Performance-vs-Floor Frontier
prompts.description: Test one strategy against every scenario in a set, rating effectiveness in each as strong / acceptable / weak / catastrophic, then propose modifications that lift weak and catastrophic cells to acceptable even at the cost of peak performance in the favored scenario. Surfaces the robustness frontier: the explicit tradeoff between maximizing performance in the expected future and raising the worst-case floor across all futures.

prompts.title: Signposts and Triggers — Detect Which Scenario Is Unfolding and Pre-Commit the Response
prompts.description: Turn a scenario set into an operational early-warning system: for each scenario, define measurable, trackable, distinguishing signposts; for each signpost, set a monitoring cadence, a source, and the pre-committed response that fires when it triggers. Ends with a monitoring dashboard spec. Counters scenario theater — the failure where scenarios are built, admired, and then never used to drive a decision.

prompts.title: Strategic Pre-Mortem — Imagine the Strategy Failed at Year Three and Trace Back Why
prompts.description: Run a pre-mortem on an entire strategy at its three-year mark: assume it has clearly failed, then work backward to identify the failure modes that produced it — missed market shifts, capacity gaps, competitive responses, execution breakdowns, and false assumptions about team, market, and technology. Outputs ranked failure modes each paired with a prevention or detection move. Distinct from product/prompt pre-mortems and from systems-intervention pre-mortems; this one operates at the strategy level.

prompts.title: Wild Card Injection — Stress-Test a Strategy Against Low-Probability, High-Impact Shocks
prompts.description: Inject a structured set of low-probability, high-impact wild cards into an existing strategy or scenario set, then test each one against three questions: would the strategy survive, how fast would damage arrive, and what early-warning signal exists. Counters the planning failure where strategies are tuned to the expected case and silently fragile to shocks outside the scenario axes.

prompts.title: Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) — Weighted Scoring with Sensitivity Audit
prompts.description: Compare 2–7 options against 4–10 weighted criteria, producing a weighted score per option. Includes a mandatory sensitivity analysis to test whether the result is robust to plausible weight changes — the primary failure mode of MCDA is false precision from arbitrary weights, and the sensitivity step exists to defeat it.

prompts.title: Pugh Matrix — Baseline-Relative Option Comparison
prompts.description: Compare options against a single baseline (often the status quo) by scoring each criterion as better (+1), same (0), or worse (-1) relative to that baseline, then summing and ranking. Deliberately less precise than MCDA's absolute scoring — it trades resolution for speed and for forcing an explicit 'compared to what' frame. Includes a weighted variant and a concordance/discordance read so a high sum built on one criterion doesn't masquerade as broad superiority.

prompts.title: Real Options Framing — Decisions as Optionality, Not One-Shot Bets
prompts.description: Reframe a decision that looks like a single irreversible commit as a sequence of options: an initial bounded commitment that buys the right (not the obligation) to defer, expand, abandon, contract, or switch later. Borrowed from financial real-options analysis but kept qualitative. Forces the questions 'what does today's spend buy me in optionality?', 'what does it foreclose?', and 'what is the value of waiting vs. acting now?' — countering both premature full commitment and indefinite waiting.

prompts.title: Reversibility × Stakes Grid — Decision Sequencing by 2x2
prompts.description: Plot a decision (or set of decisions) on a 2x2 grid: reversibility (one-way / two-way door) × stakes (low / high). Each quadrant has a different rule for how much analysis to invest, who to involve, and how fast to move. Counters the most common decision pathology: applying high-analysis processes to two-way-door decisions and rushing one-way-door decisions.

prompts.title: Blind Spot Analysis and Falsification
prompts.description: Identify cognitive blind spots in your self-assessment and generate falsifiable experiments to test each hypothesis

prompts.title: Crisis Communication Playbook
prompts.description: Complete framework for communicating during a crisis — from initial holding statement through resolution, covering internal and external audiences

prompts.title: Crisis Severity Triage
prompts.description: 5-minute rapid assessment framework to classify crisis severity, determine response urgency, and route to the right action protocol

prompts.title: Escalation Decision Tree
prompts.description: Structured framework for determining when to escalate, who to notify, what information to provide, and how to communicate urgency appropriately

prompts.title: First Principles Problem Decomposition
prompts.description: Break down complex, seemingly intractable problems into fundamental truths and rebuild solutions from the ground up

prompts.title: Logic and Complex Problem Solver
prompts.description: Systematic framework for solving complex logic, reasoning, and analytical problems by applying structured thinking methods

prompts.title: Multi-Constraint Optimizer
prompts.description: Framework for navigating decisions where multiple constraints compete and you can't optimize for everything simultaneously

prompts.title: Rapid Stakeholder Alignment
prompts.description: Framework for quickly getting diverse stakeholders aligned on a course of action during time-sensitive or high-stakes situations

prompts.title: Recovery and Resilience Planning
prompts.description: Post-crisis framework for rebuilding trust, capturing lessons, preventing recurrence, and emerging stronger than before

prompts.title: Resource-Constrained Problem Solver
prompts.description: Framework for solving problems when you have limited time, money, people, or other critical resources — making the most of what you have

prompts.title: Time-Boxed Decision Protocol
prompts.description: Structured framework for making the best possible decision within a fixed time constraint, from 5 minutes to 4 hours

prompts.title: After a Mentor Is Removed — Caring for Everyone Left
prompts.description: Plan the care of the mentees, the mentor cohort, and the wider community after a discipler is removed or a concern about them is substantiated — who is told what, in what order, by whom, and what each group is offered — without investigating, adjudicating, disciplining, characterizing what happened, or running a communications strategy.

prompts.title: Dependency and Over-Attachment — Unwinding a Pair That Has Closed In
prompts.description: Diagnose and unwind unhealthy dependency in a live discipling relationship that is not crossing a safeguarding line — in either direction, including where the mentor is the dependent one — restoring the mentee's own decisions, people, and access to God without shaming either person or treating ending the relationship as the only remedy.

prompts.title: Harmed by a Previous Discipling Relationship — Terms for Trying Again
prompts.description: Set the terms on which someone who was harmed in a previous discipling relationship or high-control setting enters a new one — pace, veto, exit, what is disclosed and to whom, what is never asked — with a safety and clinical screen run before any relationship is designed, and without ever assessing what happened or telling the person they should try again.

prompts.title: When the Mentor Got It Wrong — Owning and Repairing a Rupture
prompts.description: Help a discipler own and repair something they did that hurt the person they were discipling — beginning with a gate that decides whether 'mistake' is the right word at all, then producing an apology that names the thing without explaining it away, a change the mentee can see, and an outcome that does not require them to forgive, continue, or reassure anyone.

prompts.title: Campus Ministry Program Variant — Discipleship Inside an Institution's Rules and a Three-Year Clock
prompts.description: Design a campus discipleship program that operates inside the institution's recognition, access, and non-discrimination rules, protects students whose visa or academic standing could be affected, handles the staff-student power gap, and rebuilds itself annually against near-total turnover.

prompts.title: Prison and Re-Entry Program Variant — Discipleship Inside Rules You Do Not Set
prompts.description: Design a discipleship program for people in custody and people leaving it, where facility rules govern absolutely, the power asymmetry is extreme, no promise may be made that cannot be kept, and the re-entry cliff is planned for before the first inside session runs.

prompts.title: Remote and Diaspora Program Variant — Discipleship Across Distance, Time Zones, and Risk
prompts.description: Design a fully-remote or diaspora discipleship program that works across time zones and bandwidth, holds safeguarding and identity verification at a distance, keeps data and records minimal where participants may be at risk, and connects participants to a local body rather than replacing one.

prompts.title: Workplace and Marketplace Program Variant — Discipleship Where Someone Signs Someone Else's Payslip
prompts.description: Design a workplace or marketplace discipleship group that operates inside the employer's policy, never pairs a manager with their own report, keeps participation demonstrably voluntary and off the record, and protects colleagues who do not participate as carefully as those who do.

prompts.title: Cross-Cultural Discipling — Asking Rather Than Assuming About Someone Else's World
prompts.description: Design a discipling relationship across a culture or language you do not share, built on questions asked of the actual person rather than generalizations about their group — with the mentor's own culture surfaced as a culture, and the power the arrangement carries named honestly.

prompts.title: Oral-Preference Learners — Discipleship That Does Not Require Reading
prompts.description: Design discipleship for people who learn, remember, and reason orally — through story, repetition, dialogue, and community memory — building an oral route that is equal rather than remedial, and never treating literacy as a prerequisite for maturity.

prompts.title: Translated Material Pitfalls — Auditing Discipleship Material That Has Crossed a Language
prompts.description: Audit discipleship material that has been translated or is about to be, finding the metaphors that do not travel, the assumptions embedded in examples, the terms with no equivalent, and the authority a translated text acquires — without ever assessing translation quality the model cannot verify.

prompts.title: Curriculum Balance Audit — Gaps, Imbalance, and Smuggled Distinctives
prompts.description: Audit an existing discipleship curriculum against the five formation domains to surface coverage gaps, over-weighting, missing practice, and tradition-specific distinctives that have entered as unmarked assumptions — reporting findings with evidence from the supplied material rather than impressions.

prompts.title: Discipleship Curriculum Architecture — Multi-Stage Formation Blueprint
prompts.description: Design a complete multi-stage discipleship curriculum — stages, modules, formation outcomes, evidence of growth, pace, and entry and exit points — for a new believer or a believer seeking to mature, staying neutral on contested practices and describing growth as observable practice rather than a measured level.

prompts.title: Discipleship Material Evaluation — Criterion Review Without Fabricated Claims
prompts.description: Evaluate supplied discipleship or formation material against stated criteria — fit, theological transparency, practice formation, accessibility, facilitator demand — with every product, author, availability, and reception claim marked verify-required rather than asserted from memory.

prompts.title: Formation Outcomes Framework — Observable Growth Without a Score
prompts.description: Define observable formation outcomes for a discipleship pathway across Scripture, character, practice, community, and mission — stage by stage, described as recognizable practice rather than measured level — with an explicit account of what the evidence cannot see.

prompts.title: Module Scope and Sequence — Ordering a Formation Curriculum
prompts.description: Sequence discipleship modules across a pathway with explicit prerequisites, deliberate revisits of foundational material, contested-practice flags, and a stated rationale for the ordering — sized to a real participant time budget.

prompts.title: Multiplication Design — Disciples Who Disciple
prompts.description: Design a discipleship pathway for reproduction — what a disciple must be able to hand on, how handing-on is learned rather than assumed, the generational depth test, and the specific ways multiplication designs degrade into recruitment pressure or diluted formation.

prompts.title: Multiplication Governance and Material Drift — Generation Three and What It Teaches
prompts.description: Govern a discipleship program once its third and fourth generations are being formed by people the original designers never met — auditing an accumulated material library nobody can attribute, separating what is core from what is legitimately local, and designing how correction travels without becoming control or a licensing regime.

prompts.title: Baptism Preparation — Preparing Someone Well Inside a Practice This Prompt Does Not Adjudicate
prompts.description: Design baptism preparation that runs inside the community's own practice while showing the candidate honestly where Christian traditions differ on subjects, mode, and meaning — with no deadline, no pressure, no counting, and no use of baptism as a gate to belonging.

prompts.title: Catechesis Design — Structured Instruction That Teaches a Tradition Without Closing a Mind
prompts.description: Design a catechesis — structured instruction in the faith, in a tradition's own terms and often in question-and-answer form — that teaches confidently while keeping questions genuinely open, marks the contested as contested, and never uses memorization or a rite as a pressure point.

prompts.title: Membership Preparation — Preparing Someone to Commit, and Telling Them What They Are Committing To
prompts.description: Design membership preparation that discloses obligations, authority, discipline, giving expectations, and how membership ends before anyone commits — presents the divergence on what membership even is, and never lets belonging or care be conditional on joining.

prompts.title: Growth Self-Assessment — An Honest Picture Without a Score
prompts.description: Help a believer see where they actually are across Scripture, character, practice, community, and mission — as a narrative picture with named next edges, never as a score, level, or rank — while distinguishing formation questions from circumstance and from distress that needs professional help.

prompts.title: Life Constraints Adaptation — Rebuilding a Pathway Around Real Capacity
prompts.description: Rebuild a discipleship pathway around the actual conditions of someone's life — shift work, caregiving, disability, chronic illness, poverty, no private space, limited literacy, unsafe home, or restricted access — preserving formation while removing assumptions the standard pathway silently makes.

prompts.title: Personal Growth Plan — One Focus for the Next Season
prompts.description: Build a believer's own next-season growth plan around a single focus — with practices sized to real capacity, a floor that survives a bad week, named people, a review date, and an explicit account of what was deliberately left out.

prompts.title: Returning Believer Re-engagement — Coming Back Without Being Shamed
prompts.description: Build a re-entry plan for someone returning to faith or church after a long absence — taking the reasons they left seriously first, separating hurt from drift from doubt from circumstance, and pacing return so that nothing requires them to explain or justify themselves to be welcome.

prompts.title: Spiritual Practices Designer — Rhythms That Survive a Real Week
prompts.description: Design a sustainable set of spiritual practices matched to temperament, season, capacity, and tradition — drawing across contemplative, word-centred, charismatic, liturgical, and active streams without ranking them — with a deliberately small floor and an honest account of what each practice does and does not do.

prompts.title: Stalled Growth Diagnostic — Why Nothing Is Moving, and Where It Routes
prompts.description: Differentiate the actual cause when spiritual growth has stopped — plateau, exhaustion, isolation, unresolved doubt, hidden circumstance, unaddressed harm, or clinical distress — and route each to the right response instead of prescribing more effort to all of them.

prompts.title: College and Young Adult Track — Discipleship Built for Transience, Autonomy, and Real Questions
prompts.description: Design a discipleship track for students and young adults that assumes people leave within three or four years, treats deconstruction and hard questions as legitimate intellectual work rather than a threat, respects newly held autonomy, and builds a handoff so formation survives the move.

prompts.title: Married Couples Track — Discipling Two People Who Are Not in the Same Place
prompts.description: Design a discipleship track for married couples that forms two individuals as well as a marriage, screens for abuse before any joint work begins, never imposes one tradition's teaching on marital roles, and stays firmly out of marriage counseling.

prompts.title: Parents Track — Discipling the Parent, Not Grading Them by Their Child's Faith
prompts.description: Design a discipleship track for parents that forms the parent's own faith in the conditions parenting actually creates, refuses to treat a child's belief or behaviour as the measure of the parent's discipleship, and hands parenting technique and child-behaviour questions to the domains that hold them.

prompts.title: Seniors Track — Discipleship for People Still Being Formed, Not Being Wound Down
prompts.description: Design a discipleship track for older adults that treats them as people still being formed and still giving, designs around accumulated loss and changing capacity without patronizing, builds genuine accessibility, and screens for elder abuse and isolation without turning care into surveillance.

prompts.title: Youth and Teen Discipleship Track — STRONG-GUARD Design for Discipling Minors
prompts.description: Design a discipleship track for teenagers where child safeguarding governs every structural decision before any content decision, parents and guardians are inside the design rather than around it, doubt is treated as development rather than rebellion, and no emotional pressure is ever applied to a minor's spiritual decisions.

prompts.title: Mentor Boundaries and Referral — What a Lay Discipler Does Not Do
prompts.description: Build a lay mentor's standing scope-and-referral framework — what falls inside the role, what always routes out, the specific handoff words, the confidentiality limits stated before anyone discloses anything, and the power dynamics a discipling relationship creates whether or not anyone intends them.

prompts.title: Mentor Case Consultation — Taking One Live Situation to a Third Party
prompts.description: Run the conversation in which a lay discipler brings one live, difficult relationship to a supervisor or designated third party — with the confidentiality frame and de-identification settled before anything is disclosed, a standing check that consultation is not standing in for a referral, and a clear line between what helps the mentor and what becomes information about the mentee.

prompts.title: Mentor Conversation Skills — Listening, Asking, and Not Fixing
prompts.description: Develop the specific conversational skills a discipler needs — open questions, silence, reflecting back, resisting the urge to advise, and noticing what is not being said — through targeted diagnosis of a mentor's actual habits and drills that can be practised in real meetings.

prompts.title: Mentor Posture in Doubt and Deconstruction — Staying When You Want to Argue
prompts.description: Prepare a discipler for a mentee whose faith is coming apart — working the mentor's own fear first, fixing the relationship as unconditional on the outcome, refusing apologetic counters, deadlines, and any verdict on whether the person is still a believer, and separating honest doubt from distress that routes to a professional.

prompts.title: Mentor Readiness Assessment — Character, Capacity, and Self-Awareness
prompts.description: Assess whether someone is ready to disciple another person — across character, capacity, self-awareness, and boundary-holding — producing an honest ready / ready-with-support / not-yet verdict with what would change a not-yet, without reducing readiness to a score or gating on credentials.

prompts.title: Mentor Season Debrief — What Happened, and What Was Yours
prompts.description: Debrief a completed discipling season with a mentor — separating what they controlled from what they did not, resisting both self-blame and self-congratulation, extracting the one change worth carrying forward, and refusing to judge the season by the mentee's visible progress.

prompts.title: Mentor Support and Sustainability — Peer Cohort, Capacity Limits, and Early Warning
prompts.description: Design the support structure that keeps lay disciplers going — peer cohort, check-in cadence, honest capacity limits, and early-warning signs of overload — treating mentor attrition as a design failure of the program rather than a commitment failure of the volunteer.

prompts.title: Mentor Training Curriculum — Equipping a Cohort of Disciplers
prompts.description: Design a training curriculum for a cohort of lay disciplers — sessions, practice, feedback, and observable readiness criteria — front-loading boundaries and referral, weighting rehearsal over content, and defining what a trainee must demonstrate rather than merely attend.

prompts.title: Cadence and Rhythm Design — A Meeting Pattern Both People Can Sustain
prompts.description: Set a sustainable meeting frequency, length, format, and channel for a discipling pair — designed against both people's real constraints rather than an assumed weekly hour, with an explicit reduced pattern for hard seasons and a rule for what happens when meetings start slipping.

prompts.title: Ending or Transitioning a Discipling Relationship
prompts.description: Close a discipling relationship well — differentiating completion, mismatch, handoff, withdrawal, and ending-because-of-harm — with the words for each, a handover that does not strand the mentee, and no requirement that anyone justify leaving.

prompts.title: First Meeting Guide — Building Trust and Scope Without Interrogating
prompts.description: Plan the first conversation between a newly paired mentor and mentee — establishing what the relationship is for, stating the confidentiality limits before anything is disclosed, and letting the mentee set the depth, without turning the meeting into an assessment or an interview.

prompts.title: Informal Pairing Without a Program — Two People and No Institution
prompts.description: Set up a discipling relationship where there is no program, no lead, no policy, and no third party — establishing who the third party will be, what the agreement is with nobody to enforce it, what the safeguarding floor is, and where a concern would go — and returning 'not like this' where the arrangement cannot be made safe rather than designing around the gap.

prompts.title: Pairing Criteria Design — Matching, Disqualifiers, and Re-match Triggers
prompts.description: Design the criteria for matching someone seeking discipleship with someone able to offer it — separating hard safety constraints from fit preferences, defining disqualifiers and re-match triggers, and preventing the matching process from encoding bias or leaving people unmatched indefinitely.

prompts.title: Re-contracting a Long Relationship — Renew, Change Shape, or Release
prompts.description: Work a discipling relationship that has run for years past its original purpose to a decided outcome — renew with a new focus, change shape into friendship or peer accountability, or release — by naming the drift out loud, testing what it is still doing, and requiring neither party to justify choosing release.

prompts.title: Relationship Covenant — Mutual Expectations and the Limits of Confidentiality
prompts.description: Write the mutual agreement between a mentor and a mentee — scope, frequency, duration, what each brings, how disagreement is handled, how it ends, and above all the limits of confidentiality stated plainly before anything has been disclosed.

prompts.title: What to Expect as a Mentee — Normal, Never Owed, and What to Do
prompts.description: Give the person being discipled a plain account of what a healthy discipling relationship looks like, what is never owed to a mentor, what to do when something is off, and who to tell — written before any commitment, independent of the mentor and the program, and usable where no covenant or policy exists at all.

prompts.title: Accountability Conversation Structure — The Half Hour, and the Questions That Do Not Interrogate
prompts.description: Structure the actual accountability conversation between two peers — a fixed shape, questions that can be answered without confession, the verbatim response when the answer is no, and the drift checks that catch a partnership turning into inspection.

prompts.title: Accountability Partnership Design — Peer Support Built Against the Surveillance-and-Shame Failure
prompts.description: Design a peer-to-peer accountability partnership that is mutual rather than supervisory, built on commitments the person chose themselves, with no monitoring, no checking of devices or records, no streak-keeping, and an exit that requires no explanation.

prompts.title: Mentor Peer-Cohort Curriculum — What Disciplers Work On Together, Without Discussing Their Mentees
prompts.description: Design the curriculum for a mentors' own peer cohort — the standing group where disciplers are formed, supported, and kept honest — with a confidentiality rule that keeps mentees out of the room and a clear line between peer support and supervision.

prompts.title: Peer-Cohort Facilitation — Running the Meeting Where Disciplers Tell the Truth
prompts.description: Facilitate a mentors' peer cohort meeting: the shape of the hour, the standing questions, the intervention when a mentee enters the conversation, what to do when nobody is struggling, and how to hold a group where members have different power.

prompts.title: Mentor Pipeline and Capacity — Growing Supply Without Lowering the Bar
prompts.description: Plan mentor supply against demand for a discipleship program — modelling the pipeline from invitation through screening and training to pairing, with honest lead times — and holding the readiness bar fixed by naming what the program will do instead when supply cannot meet demand.

prompts.title: Minimum Viable Program — Discipleship With No Staff and No Budget
prompts.description: Work out what a discipleship program genuinely requires at three pairs rather than thirty — separating the non-negotiable floor (a safeguarding baseline, a named second person, a working route for a concern) from the structure that only exists because larger programs have staff to run it, and stating honestly what a solo or bivocational leader should not attempt.

prompts.title: Participant Onboarding Design — Two-Sided Intake for a Pairing Program
prompts.description: Design intake for both sides of a discipleship pairing program — what a seeker is asking for, what a mentor is offering, what matching genuinely needs, and what must not be collected — with consent stated before disclosure and every question justified by a decision it informs.

prompts.title: Program Control Drift Audit — Auditing Your Own Design for Coercion
prompts.description: Audit a discipleship program's own artifacts — covenant, cadence, onboarding, accountability structures, multiplication expectations, leadership accountability — for exit cost, information asymmetry, penalty for dissent, and unaccountable authority, producing design changes rather than a verdict on anyone, and routing the personal question of whether a group is high-control elsewhere.

prompts.title: Program Design Blueprint — Standing Up a Discipleship Pairing Program
prompts.description: Design a discipleship pairing program end to end — roles, intake, screening, matching, cadence, support, and review — sequenced so safeguarding precedes matching, sized to real volunteer capacity, and with the program's own failure modes named before launch.

prompts.title: Program Health Review — Stalled Pairs, Attrition, and What the Data Can't Tell You
prompts.description: Review a discipleship pairing program's health — stalled pairs, attrition patterns, unmatched participants, mentor load — separating measurable signals from what only conversation reveals, and refusing to use activity metrics as proxies for whether anyone is being formed.

prompts.title: Safeguarding and Conduct Policy — Screening, Visibility, and Reporting
prompts.description: Draft a discipleship program's safeguarding and conduct policy — screening, conduct expectations, visibility norms, reporting paths, and response to a concern — with every legal requirement, threshold, and authority marked verify-required and routed to qualified counsel rather than stated from memory.

prompts.title: Conversation Question Bank — Graded by Depth, With a Too-Far Line
prompts.description: Build a mentor's bank of discipling questions organized by depth tier and topic — with an explicit too-far line for each tier, the earned-access rule that governs moving between them, and questions written to be answerable rather than impressive.

prompts.title: Hard Conversation Navigation — When Something Heavy Is Said
prompts.description: Give a lay mentor an in-the-moment plan for a hard disclosure — classifying what was said, responding in the first sixty seconds without alarming or minimizing, routing what is not theirs, and handling what comes after the meeting including what they now carry.

prompts.title: Lesson Builder — Turning a Module Into a Session Two People Can Work Through
prompts.description: Build the teaching content for a single discipleship session — the question it answers, Scripture by address, discussion that is genuinely open, one practice to attempt, and honest handling of where traditions differ — handing all exegesis to domain-biblical-studies rather than attempting it.

prompts.title: Session Accessibility Design — Building It to Work in the First Place
prompts.description: Design discipleship sessions and modules so they work by default for disabled and neurodivergent participants — sensory load, eye contact, unstructured open questions, ambiguous social scripts, processing time, and written versus spoken demand — as design defaults offered to everyone, never as accommodations arranged for an individual and never by assessing whether anyone is disabled.

prompts.title: Session Plan Builder — A Reusable Shape for the One-to-One Meeting
prompts.description: Build a reusable structure for a discipling pair's regular meeting — check-in, Scripture, practice, prayer, and one next step — with realistic time allocation, a shorter version for hard weeks, and enough flexibility that the plan yields when the conversation matters more.

prompts.title: Small Group Discipleship Format — Triads and Groups of Three to Five
prompts.description: Design a triad or small-group discipleship format — distinct from Bible-study group facilitation — with rotating responsibility, confidentiality that actually holds among several people, protection for the quietest member, and a plan for the dynamics that only appear above two.

prompts.title: Anger and Conflict Module — Formation for the Conflicts a Disciple Is Actually In
prompts.description: Design a discipleship module on anger, conflict, and confrontation that treats anger as information rather than a character fault, teaches the conflict passages with their power-imbalance limits flagged, and routes abuse and intimidation out instead of handling them as conflict.

prompts.title: Digital Life Module — Formation for Attention, Platforms, and the Self That Is Performed Online
prompts.description: Design a discipleship module on digital life — attention, feeds, performance, outrage, pornography, and online speech — that forms judgment rather than issuing screen rules, refuses invented statistics about technology, and routes compulsion out to specialist help.

prompts.title: Forgiveness and Reconciliation Module — Separating Three Things That Are Routinely Collapsed Into One
prompts.description: Design a discipleship module that holds forgiveness, reconciliation, and restoration of trust apart as three distinct things, never requires a person who has been harmed to reconcile with the person who harmed them, and treats safety as prior to every other consideration in the module.

prompts.title: Money and Generosity Module — Formation Around What a Disciple Does With Money
prompts.description: Design a discipleship module on money, generosity, debt, and contentment that forms actual practice without adjudicating tithing, without shaming people in financial hardship, and without letting the group that receives the giving be the group that teaches the giving unexamined.

prompts.title: Sexuality and Singleness Module — STRONG-GUARD Formation Design on the Most Divisive Topic in the Curriculum
prompts.description: Design a discipleship module on sexuality, singleness, marriage, and desire that presents genuine tradition disagreement without adjudicating it, never interrogates anyone's sexual history, never treats a person's orientation or identity as a curriculum problem to be solved, and routes abuse, compulsion, and distress out on first contact.

prompts.title: Suffering and Lament Module — Formation That Does Not Explain Anyone's Pain
prompts.description: Design a discipleship module on suffering, lament, and unanswered prayer that teaches the practice of lament rather than a theory of suffering, presents the theodicy positions without adjudicating them, and never offers a participant an explanation for what has happened to them.

prompts.title: Witness in a Hostile Setting Module — Formation Where Speaking Costs Something Real
prompts.description: Design a discipleship module on witness where identifying as a Christian carries social, professional, family, legal, or physical cost — grading the hostility honestly, refusing to generate security advice or manipulative persuasion technique, and leaving every risk decision with the person who bears it.

prompts.title: Work and Vocation Module — Formation Around What a Disciple Does All Day
prompts.description: Design a discipleship module on work, calling, and vocation that takes ordinary jobs seriously, refuses the sacred-secular ranking, includes unpaid and unwanted and unavailable work, and never uses calling language to keep someone in an exploitative situation.

prompts.title: Anchor Paper / Exemplar Generator
prompts.description: Generate a calibration set of anchor papers — one per rubric performance level — with annotated scoring rationale, for norming teacher scoring on constructed-response or performance items.

prompts.title: Feedback Drafting Coach
prompts.description: Draft actionable, evidence-cited feedback for any student assignment — not a template, but a coach that ensures every comment names specific evidence, offers a concrete next step, and passes a tone check before the teacher sends it.

prompts.title: Item Analysis Report
prompts.description: Take class quiz results and produce a diagnostic item analysis — difficulty indices, distractor frequency patterns, items to flag, student error clusters, and a prioritized reteach agenda — designed for classroom teachers, not psychometricians.

prompts.title: Item Difficulty Calibrator
prompts.description: Estimate and adjust the difficulty of a draft item set so the final assessment has an intentional difficulty distribution — flagging items that are too easy (no diagnostic value) or too hard (demoralizing), and suggesting rewrites to hit target difficulty bands.

prompts.title: Quiz-to-Reteach Plan
prompts.description: Convert quiz results directly into a differentiated reteach lesson — grouping students by error pattern (not score), assigning each group a targeted intervention, and producing a 20-minute differentiated sequence.

prompts.title: Standards Alignment Auditor
prompts.description: Audit an existing assessment for alignment to stated standards — identifying misaligned items, over-tested standards, and uncovered standards — and produce a gap-repair list with replacement item suggestions.

prompts.title: Standards-Based Grading Converter
prompts.description: Convert a traditional points-based grading system into standards-based grading: identify priority standards, design proficiency scales, plan reassessment policy, and translate SBG marks back to a transcript grade if required.

prompts.title: Assessment and Rubric Builder
prompts.description: Create aligned assessments with clear rubrics and scoring guides

prompts.title: Common Formative Assessment for PLC
prompts.description: Build a PLC-aligned common formative assessment (CFA): essential standard, item bank, scoring agreement, data-meeting protocol, and tiered instructional response — designed to drive collaborative inquiry, not grading uniformity.

prompts.title: Diagnostic Quiz + Knowledge Map
prompts.description: Build a pre-unit diagnostic quiz that outputs not just items but a knowledge map of prerequisite concepts — and an instructional routing guide that translates score patterns into specific starting points.

prompts.title: Mastery Check Designer
prompts.description: Design a binary pass/retry mini-assessment for a single skill — with a mastery threshold, a parallel retry version, and a teacher note on what 'not yet' means instructionally.

prompts.title: Peer Review Protocol Designer
prompts.description: Design a structured peer review protocol — with a calibration activity, criteria-anchored reviewer checklist, sentence starters, reviewee response guide, and a feedback quality rubric — so peer review produces revision, not just reaction.

prompts.title: Performance Task Designer
prompts.description: Design an authentic performance task with GRASPS framing, multi-day workflow, scaffolded student-facing prompt, analytic rubric, and exemplar response — assessing transfer, not recall.

prompts.title: Portfolio Assessment Designer
prompts.description: Design a portfolio assessment system: criteria for inclusion, curation rationale by the student, reflection scaffolds, calibration anchors, and a defensible scoring approach that rewards growth without losing rigor.

prompts.title: Self-Assessment Checklist Builder
prompts.description: Build student self-assessment tools calibrated to rubric criteria — with observable behavioral indicators at each performance level, a self-rating scale, reflection prompts, and a teacher guide for using them before or after submission.

prompts.title: Test Blueprint / Table of Specifications
prompts.description: Build a test blueprint mapping items to objectives, DOK levels, and weights — producing a defensible content-validity matrix and an item-write order with target counts per cell.

prompts.title: Answer Key Generator with Diagnostic Scoring Guide
prompts.description: Take any existing assessment and produce a complete scoring guide — correct answers, full and partial credit criteria, common error patterns per item, and diagnostic interpretation of wrong answers so grading yields instructional data.

prompts.title: Bloom's Question Stem Bank by Subject
prompts.description: Build a leveled bank of question stems across all six Bloom's revised levels, customized to a specific subject and grade — so teachers can move a class up the cognitive ladder during discussion, exit tickets, or cold-call cycles.

prompts.title: DOK Item Generator (All 4 Levels)
prompts.description: Generate a coordinated set of items at all 4 Depth of Knowledge levels on a single standard — recall, skill/concept, strategic thinking, and extended thinking — with item-design analysis showing why each item lives at its DOK.

prompts.title: Distractor Rationale Designer
prompts.description: Take any MC question and generate distractors where every wrong option is tied to a named, teachable misconception — with a teacher-facing rationale card and a targeted teaching move for each.

prompts.title: Hinge Question Designer
prompts.description: Design a single pivotal diagnostic question with a branching response-distribution decision tree — so the teacher knows whether to advance, regroup, or reteach the moment results come in.

prompts.title: Multiple-Choice Item Writer with Distractor Analysis
prompts.description: Generate psychometrically defensible multiple-choice items — stem, key, and 3 distractors — each anchored to a specific objective, DOK level, and named misconception, with distractor rationale and item card.

prompts.title: Oral Questioning Plan
prompts.description: Design a structured diagnostic oral questioning sequence — with opening questions, follow-up probes, and branching paths for correct and incorrect responses — so classroom questioning reveals thinking in real time.

prompts.title: Short-Answer Item Writer with Response Spectrum
prompts.description: Generate short-answer assessment items with model answers, an annotated response spectrum (strong → misconception), a 0–3 scoring rubric, and feedback templates for each response tier — so wrong answers become diagnostic information.

prompts.title: Classroom Management Plan & Norms Builder
prompts.description: Build a complete classroom management plan — co-constructed norms, response continuum, restorative protocols, communication systems, and a first-30-days rollout — anchored in proactive design rather than reactive consequences.

prompts.title: Classroom Routines & Transitions Designer
prompts.description: Engineer the high-leverage classroom routines and transitions — entry, materials, group switches, exit, technology — with signal, sequence, and re-teach protocol that reclaims minutes per day.

prompts.title: Restorative Conversation Script
prompts.description: Generate a structured restorative conversation script after harm or broken agreement — teacher-student or student-student — using the five restorative questions, with preparation, conversation, and follow-through phases.

prompts.title: AI Literacy Lesson Designer
prompts.description: Design age-appropriate lessons teaching students about AI concepts, critical evaluation, and ethical reasoning

prompts.title: Blended / HyFlex Lesson Designer
prompts.description: Design a single blended or HyFlex lesson where in-person, sync online, and async learners get equivalent experience and outcomes — not 'in-person plus afterthoughts.'

prompts.title: Instructional Slide Deck Designer
prompts.description: Design a class slide deck that supports learning rather than substituting for it: cognitive-load-aware slide structure, segmented activities, and a teacher-facing speaker-note layer.

prompts.title: Instructional Video Script
prompts.description: Write a script for an instructional video (typically 3–10 minutes) with hook, segmented explanation, on-screen text plan, and embedded retrieval cues — designed for replayable learning.

prompts.title: LMS Course Shell Setup Checklist
prompts.description: Stand up an LMS course shell (Canvas / Blackboard / Brightspace / Moodle) end-to-end before the term opens — navigation, modules, gradebook, communication, accessibility, and a student-view test.

prompts.title: Student Choice Board / HyperDoc Designer
prompts.description: Design a student choice board (HyperDoc-style) where learners select from differentiated tasks aligned to a single learning objective — including must-do, may-do, and challenge tiers.

prompts.title: Analogy Engine
prompts.description: Construct precise, testable analogies that make unfamiliar concepts instantly intuitive — with explicit mapping, stated limits, and anti-mislead safeguards

prompts.title: Concept Clarity for Adults
prompts.description: Make complex concepts genuinely intuitive for adults using mental models, structured analogies, and the 'explain it to a smart friend' approach

prompts.title: Concept Decoder for Teenagers (Ages 11-17)
prompts.description: Break down complex concepts into sharp, relatable explanations for teens using real-world parallels, thought experiments, and 'aha moment' engineering

prompts.title: Concept Explorer for Kids (Ages 5-10)
prompts.description: Transform complex concepts into magical, memorable adventures that kids can see, feel, and retell — using characters, sensory imagery, and mini-stories

prompts.title: Reading Level & Text Adapter
prompts.description: Adapt texts to different reading levels while preserving core content and academic rigor

prompts.title: Socratic Discussion Facilitator
prompts.description: Design and facilitate Socratic seminars and discussion-based learning experiences

prompts.title: Story-Based Explainer
prompts.description: Transform any concept into a memorable narrative — allegory, origin story, character journey, or dramatic scenario — that teaches through story structure rather than lecture

prompts.title: Visual Memory Architect
prompts.description: Transform any concept into a spatial, visual memory structure — memory palaces, mental maps, journey pegs, and scene-based encoding — so learners remember by SEEING, not repeating

prompts.title: Vocabulary & Academic Language Builder
prompts.description: Design subject-specific vocabulary instruction with tiered word selection and multi-modal activities

prompts.title: Essay Feedback by Rubric Criterion
prompts.description: Generate criterion-by-criterion essay feedback that quotes specific student evidence, names a single highest-leverage revision, and produces a one-line warm + cool summary — without rewriting the student's work.

prompts.title: Lab Report Feedback (CER-Anchored)
prompts.description: Generate feedback on a student lab report keyed to CER components — claim, evidence, reasoning — plus procedure, data quality, and limitations, naming a single highest-leverage revision rather than rewriting the report.

prompts.title: Math Work Feedback (Process + Answer)
prompts.description: Generate feedback on student math work that addresses the process — strategy choice, representation, reasoning, computation — not just the final answer, while pointing the student to the next move without solving the problem for them.

prompts.title: Reusable Comment Library Generator
prompts.description: Build a personal comment library indexed by rubric criterion and severity tier — so high-leverage feedback can be deployed quickly across a stack while staying specific enough to drive revision.

prompts.title: Speed-Grading Triage
prompts.description: Sort a stack of student work into grade-deeply / grade-lightly / grade-quickly piles based on a triage protocol — protecting feedback quality where it matters and reclaiming hours where it doesn't.

prompts.title: Student Feedback Composer
prompts.description: Create specific, actionable, growth-oriented feedback that motivates improvement

prompts.title: Student Presentation / Video Feedback
prompts.description: Generate timestamped feedback on a student presentation or video — content, structure, delivery, and visual aids — that names a single highest-leverage revision while protecting the relational stakes of giving public-performance feedback.

prompts.title: Whole-Class Feedback Memo
prompts.description: Synthesize a stack of student work into a single class-facing feedback memo — patterns, exemplar moves, common errors, and a next-action menu — saving hours over individual comments.

prompts.title: Async LMS Module Designer
prompts.description: Design a fully asynchronous online module ready to drop into Canvas, Blackboard, Brightspace, or Moodle — with sequenced content, embedded checks, discussion structure, and accessibility baseline.

prompts.title: Compliance Training Module Designer (Generic)
prompts.description: Design a compliance training module that satisfies legal/regulatory documentation requirements (which the user must supply for their jurisdiction) while still producing actual behavior change — not just a click-through.

prompts.title: Corporate Onboarding Program Designer
prompts.description: Design a multi-week onboarding program (typically 30–90 days) covering role readiness, systems access, culture orientation, and milestone checks — with manager and peer roles defined.

prompts.title: Graduate TA Discussion Section Prep
prompts.description: Prepare a graduate teaching assistant to lead a discussion or recitation section: clarify the section's purpose relative to lecture, structure 50–75 minutes with active moves, and run a defensible grading and equity protocol.

prompts.title: In-Person to Online Course Conversion
prompts.description: Convert an existing in-person course (semester or quarter) into an online or hybrid version with realistic faculty workload, assessment-aligned redesign, and a release-ready module sequence.

prompts.title: Lecture to Active Learning Converter
prompts.description: Convert an existing lecture (slides, recording, or transcript) into an active-learning session with interleaved retrieval, application, and discussion structures while preserving the original learning goals.

prompts.title: Microlearning Module Designer (5–15 min)
prompts.description: Design a tight 5–15 minute microlearning module focused on a single skill or decision, with a hook, single concept, one practice rep, and a transfer cue.

prompts.title: Office Hours Prep
prompts.description: Prepare an instructor or TA for office hours: anticipate the questions, pre-build worked examples, structure the room, and end with a one-page recap that benefits students who couldn't attend.

prompts.title: Performance Support Job Aid Designer
prompts.description: Design an at-the-moment-of-need job aid (decision tree, checklist, quick reference card, or embedded helper) that solves a workflow problem in under 60 seconds without requiring training.

prompts.title: Syllabus & Course Designer (Higher Ed)
prompts.description: Design comprehensive course syllabi with learning outcomes, AI policies, and inclusive design for higher education

prompts.title: Train-the-Trainer Guide
prompts.description: Prepare internal subject-matter experts to deliver a training reliably — facilitator skills, content mastery, common-question pre-builds, and a confidence-and-quality calibration plan.

prompts.title: Differentiation Strategy Planner
prompts.description: Design differentiated instruction for diverse learners with varying readiness, interests, and learning profiles

prompts.title: Lesson Plan Generator
prompts.description: Create comprehensive, standards-aligned lesson plans with differentiation and assessment

prompts.title: Project-Based Learning Designer
prompts.description: Design authentic PBL units with driving questions, sustained inquiry, and public products

prompts.title: Standards Alignment & Crosswalk Mapper
prompts.description: Map curriculum to standards, identify coverage gaps, and generate cross-standard alignment documents

prompts.title: Substitute Teacher Plan Generator
prompts.description: Create comprehensive substitute teacher plans for emergency and planned absences

prompts.title: Unit & Curriculum Planner (Backward Design)
prompts.description: Design multi-week instructional units using Understanding by Design framework with scope and sequence

prompts.title: Parent & Family Communication Composer
prompts.description: Create professional, empathetic parent communications including newsletters, conference notes, and progress updates

prompts.title: Report Card Comment Generator
prompts.description: Generate personalized, strengths-based report card comments by subject and development area

prompts.title: Exit Ticket & Formative Check Generator
prompts.description: Create quick formative assessment items aligned to Bloom's taxonomy with data analysis guidance

prompts.title: Misconception Diagnoser
prompts.description: Analyze student work to classify misconceptions and produce targeted reteach priorities

prompts.title: Pre-Assessment Designer
prompts.description: Design objective-aligned pre-assessments that surface misconceptions and drive instructional decisions

prompts.title: Reteach Intervention Planner
prompts.description: Design targeted reteach interventions from diagnostic data with clear success criteria and reassessment gates

prompts.title: Small-Group Rotation Planner
prompts.description: Plan objective-aligned small-group rotations based on misconception data, timing constraints, and reassessment goals

prompts.title: 504 Plan Accommodation Menu
prompts.description: Generate a categorized menu of 504-style classroom accommodations matched to a student's documented impairment, ranked by leverage and feasibility — with implementation specifics and progress-monitoring notes.

prompts.title: Behavior Support & SEL Planner
prompts.description: Design behavior intervention plans, SEL activities, and restorative practice guides for classroom communities

prompts.title: Dyslexia Structured Literacy Plan
prompts.description: Build a structured-literacy intervention plan for a student with dyslexia or characteristics of dyslexia — sequenced phonological, decoding, fluency, and comprehension components, progress monitoring, and classroom accommodations.

prompts.title: ELL Scaffolding by WIDA Proficiency Level
prompts.description: Adapt a content lesson with WIDA-aligned scaffolds at each of six proficiency levels — language objectives, sentence frames, modified output expectations, and assessment accommodations that preserve grade-level content rigor.

prompts.title: High-School Graduation Tracker & Intervention Planner
prompts.description: Track a high-school student's progress toward graduation requirements, surface gaps, and design specific interventions — anchored on the user's jurisdiction's requirements (which the user supplies).

prompts.title: IEP & 504 Plan Goal Writer
prompts.description: Generate measurable, compliant IEP and 504 plan goals with progress monitoring frameworks

prompts.title: Student Course-Selection Advising Conversation
prompts.description: Guide a one-on-one course-selection conversation with a student: clarify goals, surface constraints, weigh options against requirements, and produce a defensible schedule with decision rationale.

prompts.title: UDL Lesson Redesign
prompts.description: Audit and redesign an existing lesson against the three Universal Design for Learning principles — engagement, representation, action & expression — producing a per-component options menu and a learner-variability audit.

prompts.title: ELA Book Club Discussion Guide (4–6 Week)
prompts.description: Design a 4–6 week book-club facilitation plan: pacing, discussion protocols by week, role rotation, accountable-talk moves, and a culminating task that lets students compare across books.

prompts.title: ELA Close Reading Minilesson Designer
prompts.description: Design a 20–30 minute close reading minilesson on a short text passage — text-dependent questions across three reads, evidence-based discussion moves, and a written response prompt.

prompts.title: ELA Grammar Minilesson (10 Minutes, One Concept)
prompts.description: Teach a single grammar concept in a 10-minute minilesson grounded in mentor sentences and student writing — not isolated drill — so students can apply the move in revision today.

prompts.title: ELA K–2 Phonics Scope and Sequence
prompts.description: Build a K–2 phonics scope and sequence aligned with structured-literacy / Science-of-Reading principles — sequencing phonemes, sound-spelling correspondences, and high-frequency words across a year with explicit assessment checkpoints.

prompts.title: ELA Mentor Text Close Read for Craft
prompts.description: Use a mentor text excerpt to teach a single craft move — naming what the author did, why it works, and how students can try it in their own writing — without turning the mentor text into a comprehension test.

prompts.title: ELA Reading Conference Planner
prompts.description: Plan a 5–7 minute 1:1 reading conference: research stance, decide one teaching point, deliver one named strategy, and capture notes the teacher can act on next time.

prompts.title: Writer's Workshop Minilesson Designer
prompts.description: Design a focused 10–15 minute writer's workshop minilesson on a single craft move — connection, teaching point, mentor text demonstration, active engagement, and link to independent writing.

prompts.title: 3-Act Math Task Builder
prompts.description: Design a complete 3-act math task — Act 1 (hook + question), Act 2 (information release), Act 3 (reveal + sequel) — anchored to a specific standard, with anticipated student approaches.

prompts.title: Math Error Analysis Task Designer
prompts.description: Design a task in which students analyze a fictional student's wrong solution — locating the error, classifying the misconception, and writing the correction with reasoning — to convert misconception data into instructional leverage.

prompts.title: Math Manipulatives Lesson — Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract
prompts.description: Design a math lesson that moves students through the concrete → pictorial → abstract (CPA) sequence so the symbolic representation grows out of physical action — not the other way around.

prompts.title: Math Number Talk Designer
prompts.description: Design a 5–15 minute number talk that builds mental computation, reasoning, and discourse around a single computation or visual prompt — with anticipated student strategies and teacher moves.

prompts.title: Math Problem String Designer
prompts.description: Sequence a 4–6 problem string warm-up that uses the first problems as a helper for the later ones — surfacing a target strategy or relationship rather than drilling random computation.

prompts.title: NGSS Phenomenon Selector & Storyline Anchor
prompts.description: Select and frame an anchoring phenomenon for an NGSS unit — vetted against NGSS criteria, mapped to performance expectations and DCI/SEP/CCC, with student-question driver lines and a storyline arc.

prompts.title: Science Claim-Evidence-Reasoning Scaffold
prompts.description: Build CER scaffolds at three tiers (heavy, medium, light) for a specific science task — pushing students from sentence frames to independent argument from evidence over the year.

prompts.title: Science Fair Project Mentor (Student-Facing)
prompts.description: Coach a student through the full science fair arc — question, hypothesis, design, data, analysis, board, presentation — with Socratic guidance that keeps the work the student's, not the AI's.

prompts.title: Science Lab Activity Designer with CER Scaffold
prompts.description: Design a full hands-on science lab — investigation question, procedure, data collection, and Claim-Evidence-Reasoning scaffold — that has students do science rather than verify a known answer.

prompts.title: Document-Based Question (DBQ) Writer
prompts.description: Build a complete DBQ assessment — historical question, 5–7 sourced documents with attribution and context, scaffolded organizer, scoring rubric, and exemplar essay outline.

prompts.title: Social Studies Civic Action Project
prompts.description: Design a multi-week student-led civic action project: issue selection, root-cause research, stakeholder analysis, action planning, execution, and reflection — with explicit non-partisan framing and feasibility constraints.

prompts.title: Social Studies Current Events Connector
prompts.description: Connect a current news event to a unit of study via a structured analysis: source vetting, parallel framing, evidence-based connection, and a discussion protocol that protects classroom climate around politically charged topics.

prompts.title: Social Studies Primary Source Analysis
prompts.description: Design a deep single-source analysis lesson using sourcing, contextualization, close reading, and corroboration moves — building students' capacity to read sources like historians, not summarize them.

prompts.title: World Language Communicative Task Designer
prompts.description: Design a task-based world-language activity built around a real communicative purpose — information gap, decision-making, problem-solving, or opinion exchange — with proficiency-targeted scaffolds and outcome-based assessment.

prompts.title: World Language Comprehensible Input Scaffold (TPRS-Style)
prompts.description: Plan a comprehensible-input lesson — TPRS, story-listening, or PQA — that delivers compelling, contextualized target-language input at students' i+1 level, with circling, comprehension checks, and gradual production.

prompts.title: Andragogy-Aware Study Workflow for Adult Learners
prompts.description: A general study workflow tuned for how adult learners actually learn — problem-centered, experience-anchored, autonomy-respecting. Different from traditional study guides; assumes the learner can self-direct and brings prior context. Works across subjects.

prompts.title: Cold Start: Returning to School After a Break
prompts.description: Structured ramp for adults returning to formal education after years away. Handles syllabus decoding, time-on-task recalibration, academic-tone rehearsal, and what to expect in the first 4 weeks. Andragogy-aware; respects the learner's experience.

prompts.title: Credential Pathway Decision: Degree, Cert, Bootcamp, MOOC, OJT, or Self-Study
prompts.description: Help an adult learner decide which credentialing pathway fits their target role, time horizon, financial situation, and existing skill base. Honest about cost, time, opportunity cost, and signal value per field. Not a sales pitch for any pathway.

prompts.title: Imposter Calibration for Adults in Age-Mixed Classrooms
prompts.description: Calibrate impostor feelings or out-of-place feelings for adult learners in classrooms dominated by younger students. Distinguishes real signal (gaps to close) from age-anchored false signal (you don't belong here). Andragogy-aware.

prompts.title: Portfolio While Learning: Ship Public Artifacts Before Mastery
prompts.description: Design a portfolio strategy for an adult learner pivoting careers: which artifacts to build while you're still learning, how to ship public work that signals correctly without misrepresenting your level, and how each artifact compounds into the next.

prompts.title: Prior Learning Articulation: From Career Experience to Academic Currency
prompts.description: Turn an adult learner's career experience into academic currency: credit-for-prior-learning (CPL) portfolios, graduate-school SOP language, application essays, or course-by-course petition narratives. Treats experience as a resource without inflating it.

prompts.title: Skill-Pivot Self-Study Plan Designer
prompts.description: Design a 3, 6, or 12-month self-study plan for an adult learner pivoting careers or building a new skill domain — with milestones, evals, evidence artifacts, and an explicit definition of 'ready.' Anchored on real target roles, not aspirational learning.

prompts.title: Working Learner: Time Architecture Under Real Constraints
prompts.description: Weekly time architecture for an adult enrolled in school while working full-time, often with family responsibilities. Honest about tradeoffs; designs around the actual week, not the idealized one. Outputs a defensible weekly block plan.

prompts.title: Writing Rust Recovery for Returning Adult Learners
prompts.description: Diagnose which specific academic writing skills have rusted during years of professional writing, then rehearse the rusty ones with low-stakes exercises before the first graded paper. Andragogy-aware; treats professional writing experience as a resource.

prompts.title: Exam Review Planner
prompts.description: Creates a prioritized, content-based exam review plan: classifies topics by yield, assigns daily coverage based on available days and mastery gaps, and builds a contingency buffer.

prompts.title: Finals Week Study Planner
prompts.description: Help a student build a realistic, prioritized finals week study schedule — mapping exams to available hours, sequencing subjects by date and difficulty, and building in buffer and recovery time.

prompts.title: Practice Test Generator
prompts.description: Produces a full-format, standalone practice test: mixed question types, point values, timing guidance, answer key, and a post-test self-score rubric — suitable for printing or independent use.

prompts.title: Professional Licensing Exam MCQ Drill
prompts.description: Exam-style multiple-choice question drill for professional licensing exams (CPA, CFA, LSAT, GMAT, GRE, MCAT): generates questions in the house style of the target exam, collects confidence ratings per question, tracks over- and under-confidence, and produces a targeted review agenda weighted by both performance and confidence calibration.

prompts.title: Study Next Advisor
prompts.description: Answers 'what should I study next?' by integrating exam date, current mastery estimates, topic dependencies, and available time to output a prioritized session agenda.

prompts.title: Technical Certification Domain Drill
prompts.description: Domain-weighted retrieval drill for IT/cloud/professional certifications: generates question sets proportional to actual exam domain percentages, tracks performance by domain, flags knowledge gaps, and produces a targeted re-study agenda aligned to exam weighting.

prompts.title: Test Day Strategy Coach
prompts.description: Coach a student through pre-test preparation and during-test strategy — question prioritization, time allocation, and anxiety management — for a specific upcoming test.

prompts.title: Weak Area Diagnosis and Drill Plan
prompts.description: Systematically diagnoses knowledge gaps from quiz scores, self-ratings, or error logs and outputs a ranked weakness map with a targeted drill plan for each gap.

prompts.title: Adult Returning to School: Cross-Domain Prompt Kit
prompts.description: Curated index of non-education prompts that returning adult learners need: deep work and time management, identity calibration, bottleneck diagnosis, agency / execution, and career-transformation prompts when the return is pivot-related.

prompts.title: Workflow: Cold Start Return to School
prompts.description: First-four-weeks ramp for adults returning to school after years away: syllabus decoding, time-on-task calibration, what's changed in higher ed, weekly tasks, questions to ask instructors. Anchors the rest of the semester.

prompts.title: Workflow: Imposter Calibration in Age-Mixed Classrooms
prompts.description: Separate real skill-gap signal from age-anchored impostor noise. Use when 'I don't belong here' shows up for an adult learner surrounded by younger peers. Produces an action plan for real gaps and a reframe for the noise.

prompts.title: Workflow: Prior Learning Articulation
prompts.description: Translate career and life experience into academic currency — CPL portfolios, graduate-school SOPs, application essays, course-equivalency petitions. Treats experience as a resource without inflating it.

prompts.title: Workflow: Working-Learner Time Architecture
prompts.description: Design a defensible weekly time architecture for working adults in school — accounting for actual work hours, family floor, sleep, maintenance, and the higher per-credit-hour estimates that apply to returning learners. Forces explicit tradeoffs.

prompts.title: Workflow: Writing Rust Recovery
prompts.description: Diagnose which specific academic-writing skills have rusted during years of professional writing, then rehearse the rusty ones before the first graded paper. Treats professional writing experience as a resource.

prompts.title: Career Changers: Cross-Domain Prompt Kit
prompts.description: Curated index of non-education prompts a career changer will need: career strategy, agency / execution, identity calibration, time management, and decision-making.

prompts.title: Workflow: Credential Pathway Decision
prompts.description: Decide between degree, certificate, bootcamp, MOOC, on-the-job training, and self-study for a career pivot. Anchors on the target field's actual hiring signals, not the field's discourse. Output: a defensible recommendation with reasoning shown.

prompts.title: Workflow: Portfolio While Learning
prompts.description: Ship public artifacts that signal your skill at the level it actually is, while you're still building. Compounds into a portfolio that lands the destination role without misrepresenting your level.

prompts.title: Workflow: Proof-of-Work for the Pivot
prompts.description: Position your portfolio and accumulated work for the target role's application context. Adapts the general proof-of-work portfolio prompt for the pivot-specific case where you need to make career-change make sense to a hiring manager.

prompts.title: Workflow: Skill-Pivot Self-Study Plan
prompts.description: Design a 3, 6, or 12-month self-study plan calibrated to the target role's actual hiring bar. Chains the pivot plan prompt with time architecture, portfolio strategy, and checkpoint design. Output: an end-to-end pivot plan you can defend.

prompts.title: College Students: Cross-Domain Prompt Kit
prompts.description: Curated index of non-education-domain prompts that traditional college students will find useful: time management, focus, procrastination, perfectionism, confidence, stuckness, and weekly review.

prompts.title: Workflow: Essay — Draft to Submit
prompts.description: Full chain for writing a college essay (3–10 pages): topic to thesis to outline to draft to revision to integrity self-check. Uses existing Socratic prompts only — AI does not write the essay.

prompts.title: Workflow: Exam Prep & Finals Week
prompts.description: Triage, spaced retrieval, mistake review, and test-day strategy for finals or a major exam. Chains study-skills and time-management prompts. Works for one exam or a full finals week.

prompts.title: Workflow: Office Hours & Class Discussion Prep
prompts.description: Turn vague confusion into specific productive questions for office hours; prepare a defensible claim and textual evidence for class discussion. Two short related workflows that share the underlying skill — converting fuzzy thinking into something you can act on.

prompts.title: Workflow: Research Paper — Full Arc
prompts.description: Full chain for a college research paper (10+ pages, multiple sources, 2–4 week timeline): question to search to source synthesis to outline to draft to bibliography. Socratic stance throughout — AI does not write.

prompts.title: Workflow: STEM Problem Solving
prompts.description: Per-problem chain for math, physics, chemistry, engineering: decode the problem, Socratic step-by-step (no final answer given by AI), error analysis on your work, concept map for the unit. Builds skill instead of getting the answer.

prompts.title: AI as Study Partner: Academic Integrity for Self-Directed Adult Learners
prompts.description: How to use AI as a learning partner without producing submittable work. Aimed at college students, returning adults, and self-directed career changers. Covers what integrity policies mean for each audience, how the learner-facing prompts are designed to comply, and practical patterns for using AI ethically across coursework.

prompts.title: Andragogy Principles for Adult Learners
prompts.description: Adult learning theory (Knowles, Mezirow, Brookfield) applied to prompt design. Why prompts for adults differ from prompts for traditional students, and what the difference looks like in practice.

prompts.title: Prompt Index for Learners (Cross-Domain)
prompts.description: Curated cross-domain index of ~115 prompts relevant to college students, adult returning learners, and career changers. Organized by job-to-be-done. The human-browsable companion to PROMPT_INDEX.json's audience-tag enrichment.

prompts.title: Socratic vs. Direct: When to Use Which Mode
prompts.description: Decision rule for when AI should coach Socratically (refuse to answer, ask diagnostic questions) and when it should answer directly. Resolves the live tension adult learners feel under time pressure.

prompts.title: Daily L2 Conversation Drill (Partner Mode)
prompts.description: Run a scenario-based conversation drill with an L2 learner — acting as a natural conversation partner at calibrated difficulty, then delivering structured per-exchange feedback without interrupting flow.

prompts.title: Idiom Decoder (Context-First)
prompts.description: Decode idioms an L2 learner has encountered — guiding inference from context before explaining literal vs. figurative meaning, usage contexts, and register — then coaching production.

prompts.title: L2 Grammar Concept Explainer
prompts.description: Explain an L2 grammar concept clearly — rule, examples, common errors, and comprehension check — then coach the student through targeted production practice.

prompts.title: Pronunciation Coach (Text Mode)
prompts.description: Coach an L2 learner through specific pronunciation challenges using phonetic notation, placement descriptions, minimal pairs, stress patterns, and connected-speech rules — entirely in text.

prompts.title: Topical Vocabulary Builder (L2, Context-First)
prompts.description: Help an L2 learner acquire and produce vocabulary around a specific topic — using contextual presentation, meaning inference, production practice, and spaced recall — without simply handing them a word list.

prompts.title: Error Analyzer (Student's Own Math Work)
prompts.description: Help a student analyze their own returned math work — locate where the error happened, name the error type, understand why it happened, and plan how to avoid it next time — without re-solving the problem for them.

prompts.title: Experimental Design Helper (Socratic, Student Designs)
prompts.description: Guide a student through designing their own experiment — question, hypothesis, variables, procedure, controls — through diagnostic questions, without designing the experiment for them.

prompts.title: Lab Report Scaffold (Student-Driven, Section by Section)
prompts.description: Coach a student through writing their own lab report — purpose, hypothesis, methods, data, analysis (CER), conclusion, and sources of error — with structural scaffolds and diagnostic questions, never substituting student content.

prompts.title: Math Problem Coach (Socratic, No Final Answer)
prompts.description: Guide a student through solving a math problem they're stuck on — through diagnostic questions, partial reveals, and stepping-stone prompts — without giving the final answer or computing the result for them.

prompts.title: Science Concept Map Builder (Student Builds, AI Coaches)
