prompts.description: Design a realistic, math-anchored spaced repetition schedule for a stated deck size, time budget, and target retention. Produces a day-by-day workload forecast, an SM-2 / FSRS-aligned interval table, and explicit triggers for when to thin the deck, suspend cards, or reset. Output includes a daily-load curve and abort criteria.

prompts.title: Study Plan Designer for Health-Professions Learners
prompts.description: Given exam date, target score, available hours/week, and current knowledge gaps, generate a week-by-week study plan with resource mix, interleaving, retrieval blocks, qbank cadence, and rest days. Discipline- and exam-tailored.

prompts.title: Study-Load Triage (Burnout-Aware Workload Audit)
prompts.description: Audit a learner's current study/work/sleep/recovery load against a 7-axis rubric, identify the 1–2 binding constraints, and produce a 14-day triage plan that cuts load before adding more study time. Refuses to add hours when sleep, exercise, or recovery are below threshold. Names burnout-warning patterns explicitly.

prompts.title: Textbook Chapter → Anki Deck (Atomic Card Extraction)
prompts.description: Convert a textbook chapter or board-review section into an Anki deck using element-by-element extraction. Each testable element is converted into exactly one atomic card scored on a six-criterion rubric. Output is a tab-separated Anki import block plus a per-element coverage map and a rejected-cards block. Refuses to fabricate facts not in the source.

prompts.title: Weekly Study Review for Health-Professions Learners
prompts.description: End-of-week reflective review of study progress. Coach surfaces what was studied vs what was retained (retrieval check), reasoning vs content gaps, what to re-block next week, and energy/sleep notes that shape the upcoming plan.

prompts.title: Perianesthesia Board-Style Vignette Author (CPAN / CAPA / NCSBN / ASPAN Pattern-Locked)
prompts.description: Author a single clinically defensible perianesthesia nursing vignette for CPAN-, CAPA-, NCSBN-, or ASPAN-aligned assessment. Produces a phase-specific stem, one best lead-in, 4–5 parallel options, a discriminating-fact rationale, a distractor walk tagged to named perianesthesia failure modes, a clinical-validity audit, a cue-artifact audit, and a teaching note. Refuses to ship items with unsafe sequencing, scope violations, phase mismatch, unsupported thresholds, or cueing artifacts.

prompts.title: Allied-Health Scope & Reasoning Drill for Allied-Health Learners
prompts.description: Parameterized drill for allied-health learners (PT, OT, SLP, RT, RD, MSW, audiology): assessment frame → SMART/COAST goals → intervention plan → outcome measures → scope boundaries and referral triggers.

prompts.title: NBCOT Drill — Multi-Step Clinical-Simulation or Three-Four Option Item Anchored to OTPF Domains and Process
prompts.description: Drill a single NBCOT-OTR item — either a multi-step Clinical Simulation Test (CST) opening scene with branching information requests, or a 3- or 4-option item anchored to the Occupational Therapy Practice Framework (OTPF-4) domains (occupations, performance skills, performance patterns, contexts, client factors) and process (evaluation, intervention, outcomes). Build with a defining feature: occupation-based intervention selection over impairment-based reflex. Output is one item + per-option teardown with explicit naming of the OTPF-4 domain tested.

prompts.title: NPTE Drill — FSBPT-Blueprint Anchored Item with Patient Vignette + Clinical-Reasoning Teardown
prompts.description: Drill a single NPTE (National Physical Therapy Examination) item rooted in the FSBPT content outline (musculoskeletal, neuromuscular & nervous, cardiovascular & pulmonary, integumentary, other systems) crossed with practice-area task (patient examination, evaluation/diagnosis/prognosis, interventions, equipment/devices, safety/protection, professional responsibilities). Output is one stem + 4 options + per-option teardown that names the specific clinical-reasoning failure each distractor catches.

prompts.title: Respiratory Therapist Clinical Competency Evaluation — NBRC-Aligned Scenario with ABG, Vent, and Airway Action
prompts.description: Run an RT clinical-competency station: deliver a structured patient scenario testing ABG interpretation, ventilator management, airway intervention, or aerosol/oxygen-delivery selection. Modeled on NBRC's Therapist Multiple-Choice (TMC) and Clinical Simulation Examination (CSE) section formats. Output is scenario + decision sequence + per-step scorecard mapped to NBRC content areas (patient data evaluation, troubleshooting, initiation/modification of therapeutic procedures) and to safe-practice critical actions.

prompts.title: Dental Treatment Planning Practice for Dental Learners
prompts.description: Comprehensive dental exam → caries/perio chart interpretation → phased treatment plan (Phase I emergency/disease control → II definitive → III restorative → IV maintenance) with alternatives, sequencing rationale, medical considerations, and informed-consent talking points.

prompts.title: INBDE Drill — Integrated Clinical Scenario Linking Foundation Knowledge to Clinical Content via Patient Box
prompts.description: Drill a single INBDE-format integrated case. Each item begins with a patient box (demographics, chief complaint, medical hx, dental hx, medications) and an item testing the link between a foundation-knowledge area (anatomy, biochemistry, physiology, microbiology, pharmacology, pathology, biomaterials) and a clinical content area (diagnosis & treatment planning, oral health management, practice and profession). Build the patient box once, then ask one clinical-decision item, with a per-option teardown that names the integration tested.

prompts.title: EMS Field Scenario Drill — Full-Shift Run Progression with Scene Safety, Scope-Locked Action, and Handoff
prompts.description: Drill a full-progression EMS field run from dispatch through hospital handoff. Differs from `boards_nremt_scenario_drill.md` by emphasizing the *full operational arc* (response → scene → assessment → treatment → packaging → transport → handoff → PCR draft → debrief) rather than the psychomotor exam shape. Used for ride-along debrief, after-action review, or teaching simulation. Output is run-transcript + handoff radio call + PCR-draft skeleton + scorecard with scope/safety/timing/communication anchors.

prompts.title: EMS Protocol Decision Drill for EMS Learners
prompts.description: EMS scene-call drill: vignette → protocol selection → standing orders vs medical control contact → procedural sequence → transport decision. Coach surfaces the tension between protocol literalism and clinical judgment, scene safety, and crew resource management.

prompts.title: EMS Run Call Critique — Structured PCR + Run Review for Protocol Adherence, Documentation Defensibility, and Quality-of-Care Audit
prompts.description: Critique a completed EMS run using the patient care report (PCR) and any run-related artifacts (radio recording transcript, monitor strip, OLMC consult log). Score on protocol adherence, scene management, clinical decision-making, transport decision, documentation defensibility, and crew-resource management. Output is structured critique tied to specific PCR quotes + audit of the most common failure modes (chart vs reality drift, retrospective rationalization, missing critical action documentation).

prompts.title: NREMT Scenario Author — Build Examiner-Ready Psychomotor Scenario with Critical Criteria, Distractor Plants, and Scoring Sheet
prompts.description: Author an NREMT-style psychomotor evaluation scenario suitable for an EMT, AEMT, or paramedic course practical exam. Includes scenario stem, examiner script, vital-sign trajectory under correct vs incorrect treatment, planted distractors (information that sounds important but isn't or red herrings), critical-criteria pass/fail items mapped to NREMT skill sheets, and post-scenario debrief framework. Output is a one-page examiner packet + candidate-facing dispatch + scoring sheet.

prompts.title: NGN Clinical Judgment Drill — NCSBN Six-Step CJMM Across NGN Item Formats
prompts.description: Drill a Next-Generation NCLEX (NGN) clinical-judgment item in one of the new item formats — bowtie, matrix multiple-response, drag-and-drop ordering, highlight, cloze drop-down, or trend / case-study sequence. Each item is anchored to one of the six NCSBN Clinical Judgment Measurement Model (CJMM) layer-3 cognitive skills (recognize cues, analyze cues, prioritize hypotheses, generate solutions, take action, evaluate outcomes). Build the unfolding case, deliver, wait, then teardown using the polytomous (partial-credit) NGN scoring rules.

prompts.title: New-Graduate Nurse Preceptor Orientation Plan — Week-by-Week Competency Build with Caseload Progression
prompts.description: Build a unit-specific 8–16 week new-grad preceptor orientation plan. Each week names: caseload (number of patients + acuity), unit-specific competencies to demonstrate, learning resources, scheduled didactic, milestone assessment (with go/no-go criteria), preceptor:orientee ratio, and explicit escalation criteria. Output is a week-by-week table + competency checklist + go/no-go gate definitions + a separate struggling-orientee branch.

prompts.title: Nursing Care Plan Practice for Nursing Learners
prompts.description: NANDA-I / NIC / NOC nursing care plan rehearsal. Generate or critique a care plan with nursing diagnosis, defining characteristics, related factors, expected outcomes, interventions with rationales, and evaluation criteria. NCLEX-style reasoning emphasis on priority, safety, and delegation.

prompts.title: Nursing Clinical Evaluation Tool — Bondy-Style Anchored Behavioral Rubric for Pre-Licensure Clinical Rotation
prompts.description: Author a clinical evaluation tool (CET) for a pre-licensure nursing rotation using the Bondy-derived 5-level rating scale (Independent / Supervised / Assisted / Marginal / Dependent) anchored with observable behaviors per QSEN competency domain (patient-centered care, teamwork, EBP, QI, safety, informatics) plus profession-specific domains (clinical judgment, professionalism, communication, technical skills). Output is a one-page tool with anchor descriptors per cell + scoring guide + faculty commentary blocks.

prompts.title: Nursing Concept Map Designer — Patient-Centered Map Linking Med Dx, Nursing Dx, Assessments, Interventions, and Outcomes
prompts.description: Build (or critique) a single-patient nursing concept map. Center node = patient + chief medical diagnosis. Spokes = NANDA nursing diagnoses (PES format), each with linked assessments, interventions (independent / collaborative / dependent), and measurable outcome criteria (SMART, NOC-style). Cross-link nodes to expose system interactions. Output is a structured map (text-renderable) + critique grid scoring linkage quality, prioritization, and SMART-outcome rigor.

prompts.title: PA Clinical Year Rotation Evaluation Tool — PAEA Competencies + EOR Blueprint + Procedural Logbook Audit
prompts.description: Author a clinical-year preceptor evaluation tool for a PA student rotation (family medicine, internal medicine, surgery, peds, OB/GYN, emergency medicine, behavioral health, elective). Cover PAEA core competencies (medical knowledge, interpersonal skills, clinical and technical, professionalism, practice-based learning, systems-based practice), EOR-exam-aligned topic exposure, procedural logbook audit, and entrustment ratings tied to PA-CAT and ARC-PA-required learning outcomes. Output is preceptor-facing one-page tool + rotation-specific competency rubric.

prompts.title: PANCE Blueprint Drill — Targeted Vignette Item Anchored to Specific Task × Organ-System Cell
prompts.description: Drill a single PANCE-style vignette anchored to a named cell of the NCCPA blueprint (one of the medical content categories crossed with one of the task areas: history-taking & PE, diagnostic studies, formulating most likely dx, health maintenance/patient education, clinical intervention, pharmaceutical therapeutics, applying basic science concepts, professional practice). Build the stem with the specific task in the lead-in, deliver, wait for answer, then teach by walking each distractor through a named condition for which it would be correct.

prompts.title: APPE Rotation Evaluation Tool — PPCP Anchored to ACPE/EPA Outcomes for PharmD Final Year
prompts.description: Author a preceptor evaluation tool for an Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience (APPE) rotation. Anchored in the Pharmacist's Patient Care Process (PPCP: collect / assess / plan / implement / follow-up monitor & evaluate) crossed with ACPE Standards 2016 educational outcomes (foundational knowledge, essentials for practice and care, approach to practice and care, personal and professional development) and AACP/PharmD-EPA expectations. Output is a one-page tool + rotation-specific competency matrix + entrustment ratings.

prompts.title: PGY1 Pharmacy Residency Evaluation — ASHP Outcomes/Goals/Objectives Quarterly Rating with NI/SP/ACH/ACHR
prompts.description: Author a quarterly preceptor evaluation for a PGY1 pharmacy resident, anchored to ASHP PGY1 educational outcomes (R1 patient-centered care, R2 advancing practice, R3 leadership and management, R4 teaching/education/dissemination, E5 elective). Rate each ASHP-defined goal and objective on the ASHP four-level scale: NI (needs improvement), SP (satisfactory progress), ACH (achieved for residency), ACHR (achieved for residency, repeat needed for sustained competency). Output is a quarterly tool + customized objective set for the rotation + ResiTrak-shape narrative blocks.

prompts.title: Pharmacy Journal Club Critique Rubric — PICOTS, Internal/External Validity, Statistical Literacy, Clinical Applicability, Presentation
prompts.description: Author a rubric for a pharmacy resident or APPE student journal club presentation. Score on five anchored axes: PICOTS articulation, internal validity (study-design appropriateness), external validity & applicability, statistical literacy & interpretation, and presentation/discussion facilitation. Each axis has 0–4 anchors. Output is a one-page rubric + per-axis exemplar phrases + an audit block for the most common journal-club failure modes (e.g., reciting methods without critiquing them, misinterpreting NNT, ignoring fragility index).

prompts.title: Pharmacy Therapeutics SOAP Practice for Pharmacy Learners
prompts.description: Pharmacist-style therapeutic SOAP / SBAR for a medication-therapy problem. Coach against the pharmacotherapy reasoning frame: indication → drug → dose adjustment principle → response → adverse effects → adherence → monitoring → recommendation. NAPLEX / BCPS prep emphasis.

prompts.title: Implementation and Relationship — The Deal Is Signed and Nothing Has Happened
prompts.description: Convert signed terms into executed obligations. Extracts every commitment from the agreement with an owner and a date on each side, identifies the terms most likely to quietly lapse, sets early-warning signals for drift, and designs the relationship maintenance that makes the next negotiation cheaper. Includes the first-breach response ladder — the reaction to the first small failure sets the standard for the whole term. Counters the failure that wastes good negotiating: treating signature as the finish line when it is the point at which the obligations start.

prompts.title: No-Deal Recovery — Preserve the Option, Extract the Learning, Execute the Alternative
prompts.description: A negotiation ended without agreement. This prompt handles the three things that follow: closing the conversation so it can be reopened later without anyone losing face, extracting what the failure revealed about your assumptions and their constraints, and actually executing the BATNA you priced — which is where most no-deal outcomes fail, because the alternative was a bargaining device nobody planned to implement. Includes the reopening protocol and the honest test of whether no deal was the right outcome. Counters the reflex that destroys the option: leaving badly.

prompts.title: Post-Negotiation Debrief — What the Outcome and Their Behaviour Actually Revealed
prompts.description: Debrief a concluded negotiation as a negotiation. Compares the outcome against the reservation point and target, identifies which specific moves moved the number and which merely felt productive, reads what the counterpart's behaviour revealed about their true BATNA now that concealment no longer serves them, and extracts one change to how you prepare next time. Separates decision quality from outcome quality, since a good result from a bad process is not a repeatable success. Counters the two debrief failures: the highlight reel, and the retrospective in which everything that happened was inevitable.

prompts.title: Renegotiating a Live Agreement — Reopen Terms Without Burning the Relationship
prompts.description: Reopen an agreement already in force. Builds the change-of-circumstance case that makes the ask legitimate rather than opportunistic, prices the relationship cost honestly, tests amend-versus-exit before committing to either, and sequences the approach so the counterpart is not ambushed. Includes the reciprocity question — what you offer for the change — and the response when they use the reopening to reopen everything. Counters the failure that turns a workable amendment into a dispute: asking to change terms without a reason the other side would accept as fair.

prompts.title: Authority and Mandate Limits — Set Yours, Probe Theirs, Survive Ratification
prompts.description: Establish what you can agree to before you walk in, determine what the counterpart can actually agree to, and design the deal so it survives whoever must approve it. Covers probing authority without insulting anyone, responding to a late 'I'll have to check with my boss,' deciding whether to claim limited authority yourself, and pre-empting the ratification renegotiation where an approver reopens settled terms. Counters the failure that voids more agreements than any tactic: negotiating to a signature with someone who was never able to give one.

prompts.title: Closing and the Final Concession — Recognize the Close, Structure the Last Move, Refuse the Nibble
prompts.description: Handle the endgame, where more value is lost than anywhere else. Identifies the signals that a deal is actually closeable (as distinct from a counterpart who wants one more round), structures the final concession so it buys closure rather than continuation, locks the agreement before anyone leaves the room, and refuses the post-agreement nibble by reopening the package rather than conceding the increment. Counters the endgame failure that undoes good negotiating: treating the close as a formality and giving away the reserve to a deal that had already closed.

prompts.title: Emotional Flooding at the Table — De-escalate Without Conceding on Substance
prompts.description: Anger, walkouts, tears, and your own reactivity, handled without paying for calm. Distinguishes tactical displays from genuine flooding — the response differs — and supplies a de-escalation sequence that separates acknowledgement from agreement, so the person is heard while the position stays exactly where it was. Includes the self-regulation protocol for when you are the one flooded, the rule for calling a break, and repair after an escalation you caused. Counters the reflex that costs the most in the moment: buying calm with a concession.

prompts.title: Hard Bargainer Defense — Name and Neutralize Coercive Tactics Without Escalating
prompts.description: Identify the coercive tactic being used on you and respond without either capitulating or escalating. Covers the extreme anchor, the exploding offer, the nibble, good-cop/bad-cop, the manufactured deadline, take-it-or-leave-it, the personal attack, and the late-stage authority reveal. For each: how to recognize it, why it works, and three graduated responses — absorb, name, or exit. Counters the two reflexive failures that hard bargainers rely on: conceding to restore comfort, and matching aggression in a way that converts a tactical problem into a relationship one.

prompts.title: Impasse Breaker — Diagnose the Deadlock Type, Then Apply the Matched Unlock
prompts.description: A negotiation has stopped moving. This prompt diagnoses which of five impasses you are in — positional, informational, emotional, structural, or authority — because the unlock for each is different and applying the wrong one entrenches the deadlock. Positional impasses need reframing; informational ones need a contingent term; emotional ones need process, not substance; structural ones need a changed deal shape; authority ones need a different room. Counters the reflex that deepens most deadlocks: applying more of whatever already failed.

prompts.title: Live Question Sequencing — Surface Interests in the Room Without Signalling Need
prompts.description: Build the question sequence you will actually use during a negotiation. Orders questions from low-threat to diagnostic so disclosure builds rather than shuts down, converts extractive questions into ones a counterpart wants to answer, and pairs each with the follow-up that gets past the first answer. Includes the four question types by function, what to do with silence, and how to ask about budget, timeline, and alternatives without revealing that those are what you need. Counters the failure that closes counterparts down: interrogating for leverage instead of inquiring for understanding.

prompts.title: Reading Signals and Testing Bluffs — What Their Behaviour Actually Tells You
prompts.description: Interpret what the counterpart's behaviour reveals, and test a claimed constraint without calling anyone a liar. Separates high-information signals (what they negotiate hardest for, response latency, which MESO they pick, what they concede without being asked) from low-information ones body-language folklore over-reads. Provides four bluff tests that work by making a claim costly to maintain rather than by challenging it. Counters the two symmetric errors: taking every stated constraint at face value, and confidently reading tells that carry no information.

prompts.title: Counter-Offer Message — Structure the Written Counter So It Advances Rather Than Resets
prompts.description: Draft the written counter-offer: the message that accepts what is agreed, moves what is not, and justifies the movement in a form the recipient can forward to their approver. Structures it as acknowledge, accept-and-lock, counter-with-basis, and close-with-a-step, so the settled terms are ringfenced instead of reopening every round. Includes the one-counter-per-issue rule and what never to put in a counter. Counters the failure that stalls written negotiations: a counter that restates the whole position and invites the counterpart to do the same.

prompts.title: Cross-Cultural Negotiation — Surface the Dimensions That Vary, Then Ask Rather Than Assume
prompts.description: Prepare for a negotiation across cultural or organizational contexts without substituting stereotypes for information. Rather than supplying claims about how people from a country negotiate, this prompt names the dimensions on which negotiating norms genuinely vary — directness, decision structure, relationship sequencing, time orientation, contract meaning, disagreement expression — and builds observation and questions to establish where this specific counterpart sits. Counters the failure that does the most damage in cross-border deals: acting on a confident national generalization that the individual across the table does not match.

prompts.title: Remote and Video Negotiation — Recover What the Channel Takes Away
prompts.description: Negotiate over video or phone with the channel's losses accounted for. Video strips overlapping turn-taking, makes silence ambiguous, flattens the side conversations where deals often move, and removes the shared physical artifacts that structure a room. This prompt supplies the compensations: an explicit turn-taking protocol, a stated meaning for pauses, a deliberate caucus mechanism, screen-share used as a controlled anchor, and a pre-agreed process for the moment the connection fails mid-concession. Counters the default failure: running a remote negotiation as though it were an in-person one held further away.

prompts.title: Written and Async Negotiation — What Belongs in Writing, and What It Costs You
prompts.description: Negotiate in email, messages, and documents without the losses the channel imposes. Decides what belongs in writing versus live, calibrates tone for a medium that reads colder than intended, sequences a message so the ask is not buried, and accounts for the permanent record every written position creates — including its use in the next negotiation. Includes the response-timing rule and the escalate-to-live trigger. Counters the failure specific to the channel: writing a position you would have phrased carefully aloud, into a document that will outlive the negotiation.

prompts.title: Customer Escalation Concession — What to Give, What It Sets, and When to Hold
prompts.description: An unhappy customer wants something. Separates the legitimate remedy from the escalation premium, prices the precedent every concession creates across the customer base, distinguishes a genuine service failure from a renegotiation using dissatisfaction as leverage, and supplies the hold script for when the answer is no. Includes the goodwill-versus-entitlement distinction that determines whether a concession ends the escalation or starts a pattern. Counters the reflex that trains customers to escalate: giving whatever stops the complaint, without naming what it was for.

prompts.title: Freelance and Consulting Rate Conversation — Defend the Number, Trade Scope, Raise on Existing Clients
prompts.description: Hold a rate live, once it is set. Covers stating the number without apologizing, responding to the discount request by trading scope rather than price, handling 'we can get it cheaper' and the exposure offer, and the hardest case — raising rates on a client you already have and value. Includes the scope-creep response that reprices without souring the relationship, and the rate-floor rule that makes declining possible. Counters the failure that keeps independents underpaid: setting a defensible rate and then discounting it the first time someone pauses.

prompts.title: Internal Resource Negotiation — Budget and Headcount Against Peers With Equal Claim
prompts.description: Negotiate for budget, headcount, or capacity inside your own organization, where the counterpart is a colleague, the resource is fixed, and you will work with everyone who loses. Builds the case in the currency the decision-maker actually uses, finds the trades peers will make, times the ask to the allocation cycle, and handles the zero-sum reality without converting a colleague into an opponent. Counters the failure that loses internal asks: arguing that your team needs it, in a process that allocates by organizational priority rather than by need.

prompts.title: Major Purchase Bargaining — Vehicles, Property, and One-Off Buys Against a Repeat Seller
prompts.description: Buy a large one-off item from someone who sells them daily. Closes the information gap with pre-negotiation research, negotiates the total rather than the monthly payment or the headline, handles the finance-and-extras stage where the margin actually is, and makes the walk-away real — the only genuine lever a one-time buyer holds. Includes the response to the manager-approval routine and the deposit-taken pressure. Counters the buyer failure this asymmetry produces: negotiating hard on the sticker and losing more than that back in a stage nobody prepared for.

prompts.title: Partnership and Equity Split — The Conversation Nobody Wants to Have Early
prompts.description: Negotiate an equity or profit split between founders and partners, at the point when the relationship is good and the discussion feels unnecessary — which is the only point at which it is cheap. Separates past contribution from future commitment, prices roles and risk asymmetrically, and insists on vesting, departure terms, and a decision rule for deadlock before any number is agreed. Counters the failure that kills partnerships: an equal split agreed quickly to avoid an uncomfortable conversation, with no vesting and no exit terms, revisited eighteen months later under maximum acrimony.

prompts.title: Salary, Raise, and Promotion Negotiation — Evidence, the Ask, and the Budget Response
prompts.description: Negotiate compensation with the specifics this context demands: how bands and approval cycles actually constrain your counterpart, how to assemble market and contribution evidence that survives scrutiny, when to raise it relative to review timing, what to do with 'there's no budget,' and which non-salary dimensions are genuinely available when the number is fixed. Applies the domain's general machinery to the case where the counterpart is also your manager and the relationship continues afterward. Counters the failure specific to comp: asking for a number with no basis, in a month when nothing can move.

prompts.title: Sales Objection Handling — Diagnose the Objection Behind the Objection
prompts.description: Handle price, timing, authority, and competitor objections by finding what they actually signal. Most stated objections are proxies — 'too expensive' usually means unproven value, unclear budget ownership, or a comparison you have not seen; 'not right now' usually means no compelling reason to act rather than a genuine calendar constraint. Provides a diagnostic sequence per objection type and the response matched to the real one, plus the rule against discounting a value objection. Counters the reflex that loses deals and margin together: answering the stated objection rather than the actual one.

prompts.title: Vendor and Procurement Negotiation, Buyer-Side — Competitive Tension and the Renewal Cliff
prompts.description: Negotiate with a vendor as the buyer, without a procurement function or legal team. Builds and maintains genuine competitive tension, prices total cost rather than headline cost, treats switching cost as the leverage that decays fastest, and plans the renewal from the day of signature — because the second negotiation is always harder than the first. Includes the sales-cycle timing that actually moves vendor pricing, and the terms that matter more than the discount. Counters the buyer failure that recurs annually: negotiating hard on year-one price and inheriting a renewal with no alternatives left.

prompts.title: Negotiation Practice Loop — Drill One Sub-Skill Against Real Feedback
prompts.description: Build a practice loop for one negotiation sub-skill, in a domain where ordinary experience does not produce improvement — the feedback is slow, noisy, and confounded by luck. Selects a sub-skill narrow enough to drill, finds low-stakes repetitions that occur weekly rather than annually, defines the observable that indicates success independent of outcome, and sets the review cadence. Counters the reason experienced negotiators frequently stop improving: they accumulate reps without ever isolating a skill or receiving feedback the outcome did not contaminate.

prompts.title: Negotiation Style Self-Assessment — Your Default Under Pressure and What It Costs
prompts.description: Identify how you actually negotiate under pressure, as distinct from how you intend to. Works from evidence — past outcomes, the moves you reach for first, what you avoid — rather than from self-description, because stated style and revealed style diverge reliably. Maps your default across five dimensions, identifies the specific situations where it costs you, and produces one adjustment worth drilling. Counters the failure that makes negotiation training useless: identifying a style from a questionnaire about how you'd like to behave rather than from what you did last time it was hard.

prompts.title: Pattern Library Builder — Turn Accumulated Debriefs Into Situation → Move → Outcome
prompts.description: Convert a pile of individual negotiation debriefs into a personal library that answers 'what works in situations like this.' Defines a record format terse enough to maintain, a situation taxonomy that groups usefully rather than by topic, the extraction pass that finds patterns across records, and the calibration check that catches your systematic errors — the ones that recur because they feel like judgment. Counters the reason careful debriefing still produces no compounding: individual retrospectives are read once and never compared.

prompts.title: The Ethics Line — Where Persuasion Becomes Manipulation, Decided in Advance
prompts.description: Decide what you will and will not do in a negotiation, before the pressure arrives. Separates the settled cases from the genuinely contested middle — silence about a known defect, manufactured urgency, exploiting a counterpart's error, strategic ambiguity — and supplies three tests that resolve most of them. Sets pre-committed limits that survive the moment, and prepares the response when the other side crosses theirs. Counters the failure that produces most negotiating regret: deciding what is acceptable while inside a situation that rewards deciding it favourably.

prompts.title: Delivering Bad News You Did Not Decide — Layoffs, Cancellations, and Denied Requests
prompts.description: Deliver a decision you are carrying but did not make. Leads with the news rather than the context, refuses the false comfort of implying the decision is still open, distinguishes what you can honestly own from what you cannot defend, and handles the two hardest moments — 'is this final?' and 'do you agree with this?' — without either lying or abandoning the organization. Includes the practical support that matters more than the words. Counters the failure that makes bad news worse: burying it in preamble so that the person hears the softening and then the blow.

prompts.title: Difficult Conversation Post-Review — Debrief What Just Happened
prompts.description: Debrief a difficult conversation that just happened. Separates what factually happened from your interpretation, surfaces what surprised you, what you said well, what you'd say differently, and the gap between what you said and what the other person seemed to actually hear. Names what you owe them now (follow-up, context, repair) and what you owe yourself (decompression, pattern-noticing). Ends by extracting the recurring pattern this conversation reveals and one change to how you prepare next time.

prompts.title: Difficult Conversation Pre-Brief — One-Page Prep Before You Walk In
prompts.description: Prepare for a difficult conversation — firing, ending a relationship, naming a relationship problem, hard feedback, declining a major request, or raising an uncomfortable boundary. Forces clarity on the conversation's actual goal (not just to get-it-over-with), what the other person needs to hear and why, what you'd regret not saying, your response to the worst reply you could get, the venue and timing, and the commitments you make to yourself regardless of how it goes. Output: a one-page brief with the opening line, key points, and post-conversation commitments.

prompts.title: Receiving Hard Feedback — Stay in the Conversation and Separate Signal From Delivery
prompts.description: Take difficult feedback without defending, deflecting, or collapsing. Handles the physiological reaction that arrives before any judgment does, supplies the questions that extract specifics from vague criticism, separates the content from a delivery that may have been poor, and sets the rule for deciding what to act on — since accepting all feedback and accepting none are both failures. Includes what to do when the feedback is unfair, and the follow-up that converts a hard conversation into a changed relationship. Counters the reflex that ends the conversation early: explaining.

prompts.title: Saying No Upward — Declining a Request From Someone With Power Over You
prompts.description: Decline a request from a manager, client, or anyone with authority over you, without damage. Distinguishes the four things 'no' can mean — not possible, not without a trade, not by me, not without changing something else — because three of them are not refusals at all. Supplies the trade-off framing that hands the decision back with its costs made visible, the escalation-safe wording, and the rule for when compliance is the right answer. Counters the two failures that follow an unprepared ask: the agreement you cannot deliver, and the flat refusal that reads as unwillingness rather than capacity.

prompts.title: Coalition Defense — When the Other Parties Have Aligned Against You
prompts.description: You are one against a bloc. This prompt assesses whether the coalition is genuine or presentational, finds the seams — divergent interests, unequal stakes, members who joined for access rather than agreement — and chooses between three strategies: split it legitimately, negotiate with it as a unit, or restructure the negotiation so the coalition is no longer the relevant frame. Includes what makes splitting legitimate rather than corrosive, and the test for when accepting the bloc is the better outcome. Counters the reflex that hardens a soft coalition: treating it as monolithic and negotiating against all of it at once.

prompts.title: Facilitating a Negotiation You Are Not a Party To — The Neutral Role
prompts.description: Run a negotiation between other people without becoming a party to it. Establishes the mandate and its limits, sets the process the parties agree to before substance begins, separates the facilitator's control of process from the parties' control of outcome, and supplies the moves that unlock a stalled exchange — caucusing, reframing, reality-testing each side privately, and the single-text procedure. Includes the neutrality-loss warning signs and what to do when you are not actually neutral. Counters the failure that ends a facilitation: drifting from running the process to advocating an outcome.

prompts.title: Multi-Party Alignment — Coalition Mapping and Concession Sequencing
prompts.description: For negotiations with three or more parties, design the sequence of bilateral conversations and the all-parties moment that gets to a deal. Maps every party's interests and BATNA, enumerates feasible coalitions, separates must-include parties (no deal without them) from swing parties, and sequences whom to align with first to influence the rest — with an explicit coalition-collapse risk attached to each step. Counters the bilateral-thinking failure: treating a 4-party deal as four separate 2-party deals.

prompts.title: Team Negotiation Roles — Who Speaks, Who Watches, and How Not to Be Split
prompts.description: Assign roles before your side walks in together. Separates the speaker, the observer, the technical authority, and the decider; sets the internal signals and caucus rules; and closes the seams a counterpart will probe — the colleague who answers a question outside their lane, the sympathetic side conversation, the visible disagreement between teammates. Includes the pre-brief, the no-solo-concession rule, and the debrief that catches what the speaker missed. Counters the failure that costs teams their advantage: arriving with more people than the counterpart and less coordination.

prompts.title: BATNA Analysis — Best Alternative, Reservation Point, ZOPA Mapping
prompts.description: Before a negotiation, develop your BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement), estimate the counterpart's BATNA, derive your reservation point and theirs, and map the Zone of Possible Agreement (ZOPA). Surfaces whether a deal is possible and where in the bargaining range your strongest moves live. Counters the most common negotiation mistake: entering without knowing your walkaway.

prompts.title: Concession Plan — The Ladder, the Decay Curve, and the Reciprocity Rule
prompts.description: Design every concession before the negotiation instead of inventing them under pressure. Builds a ladder with decreasing step sizes (the decay curve that signals you are approaching a limit), attaches a required return to each step so no concession is unilateral, sets the reciprocity rule and what happens when it is broken, and pre-commits the floor. Ends with the pattern the ladder will teach the counterpart, since concession sizes communicate more than words do. Counters the failure the domain's own BATNA prompt flags: entering with a walkaway but no plan for the ground between the opening and it.

prompts.title: Counterpart Simulation — Reconstruct Their Brief, Their Pressure, and Their Next Three Moves
prompts.description: Build a model of the person across the table as an analysis artifact: the brief they were given, the constraints they cannot move, the person they report to, how their success is measured, and the three moves they are most likely to make — each with your prepared response. Produces a written counterpart profile with confidence-tagged inferences and the two questions that would confirm or overturn the load-bearing ones. Counters the failure that makes preparation brittle: preparing your own case thoroughly and treating the counterpart as a generic obstacle who reacts to it.

prompts.title: Information Plan — What to Ask, What to Reveal, What to Protect
prompts.description: Plan the information side of a negotiation deliberately. Inventories what you need to learn, what you hold that they don't, and what would damage you if disclosed; then sequences disclosure so that reciprocal sharing builds without exposing your reservation point. Includes the pre-negotiation research list, the ask-order, prepared answers to the three questions you least want, and the rule for what you will never volunteer. Counters two symmetric failures: negotiating on assumptions you never tested, and answering every question truthfully in an order that gives away the range.

prompts.title: Interest Mapping — Positions vs. Underlying Interests for Both Sides
prompts.description: Before or during a negotiation, separate what each party SAYS they want (positions) from WHY they want it (interests). Drives a why-laddering procedure 3–5 levels deep per side, finds where interests overlap (value-creation territory) and where they genuinely diverge (value-claiming territory), and designs a question sequence to surface the counterpart's interests live. Counters the most common value-destroying mistake: negotiating positions when the deal lives in interests.

prompts.title: Leverage Audit — Inventory Every Source of Leverage, Not Just Your BATNA
prompts.description: Inventory and rank every source of leverage on both sides of a negotiation — alternatives, time pressure, information, legitimacy, relationship, scarcity, coalition, and cost of no-deal — then assess each for durability and whether the counterpart knows you hold it. BATNA is one source among eight, and negotiators who track only their alternative routinely concede from a position that was stronger than they knew. Counters the most common self-inflicted failure: bargaining as though the only leverage in the room is your willingness to walk.

prompts.title: Negotiation Prep Depth Triage — How Much Preparation This One Deserves
prompts.description: Decide how much preparation a specific negotiation warrants before spending hours on it, and which prompts to run in which order. Scores the negotiation on stakes, reversibility, relationship horizon, counterpart sophistication, and information asymmetry, then assigns one of four prep tiers — from a five-minute walkaway check to a full multi-session workup — with a named prompt sequence per tier. Counters the two symmetric failures: over-preparing a low-stakes ask until the window closes, and walking into a consequential negotiation with nothing but a number in your head.

prompts.title: Opening Offer Design — Whether to Move First, Where to Anchor, and How to Justify It
prompts.description: Decide whether to make the first offer, then design it. Tests the four conditions under which moving first is correct, sets the anchor from your target rather than your floor, and — the part most negotiators skip — builds the justification that makes the anchor survive contact. An unjustified anchor is a number the counterpart discounts; a justified one reframes the whole range. Ends with the response to an extreme counter-anchor. Counters the two default errors: conceding the first move reflexively out of politeness, and anchoring aggressively with nothing behind the number.

prompts.title: Package and Trade Design — Log-Rolling, MESOs, and Contingent Terms
prompts.description: Convert a mapped set of interests into actual offers. Scores every negotiable issue by how much each side values it, finds the asymmetries that make log-rolling profitable, assembles two to four packages of equivalent value to you but different shape to them (MESOs), and designs contingent terms that bridge disagreements about the future rather than splitting the difference on them. Counters the failure that wastes most of the value in multi-issue deals: negotiating issues one at a time in sequence, which converts every trade into a concession.

prompts.title: Pre-Meeting Rehearsal — Scripting the High-Stakes Negotiation Conversation
prompts.description: Rehearse a high-stakes negotiation conversation before it happens. Not a brief — the actual run-through. Scripts the load-bearing moments (opening line, early questions, the ask, the response to their counter, the walkaway/exit, the close), rehearses 2–3 likely surprises with a response to each, and runs a tone and body-language check for in-person or video. Output is a set of scripted moments plus a decision tree of branches so the user has a prepared move at every fork.

prompts.title: Attachment Repair After a Long Absence (0–3 years)
prompts.description: Reconnect with an infant or toddler after a sustained absence (hospitalization, work travel, military deployment, custody schedule, separation due to illness or relocation) — repair the attachment relationship without forcing closeness too fast.

prompts.title: Daycare or Childcare Transition Plan (3 months–3 years)
prompts.description: Plan an infant or toddler's transition into a new daycare, in-home provider, or kinship care setting — covering placement-fit assessment, staggered ramp, communication protocol with the provider, illness expectations, and adjustment monitoring.

prompts.title: Developmental Red Flags 0–3 — Screening and Routing
prompts.description: Identify developmental signals that warrant pediatric evaluation, early intervention referral, or specialist routing in infants and toddlers — across motor, language, social-communication, sensory, and feeding domains.

prompts.title: Infant Feeding Troubleshooter (0–12 months)
prompts.description: Diagnose an infant feeding concern across breast, bottle, and combo feeding by mapping symptom pattern to mechanism (latch, supply, transfer, oral structure, gut, behavior) and produce a stepped intervention plan.

prompts.title: Newborn & Infant Sleep Pattern Decoder (0–12 months)
prompts.description: Decode an infant's sleep pattern by age, distinguish developmentally typical sleep variability from intervention-worthy patterns, and produce an evidence-based response plan for the next 14 days.

prompts.title: Postpartum Parent Capacity Check (0–12 months postpartum)
prompts.description: Help a caregiver in the postpartum year self-assess capacity, distinguish baby blues from PPD/PPA/PP-OCD/postpartum psychosis/PTSD, and route to appropriate support — for birthing parents, non-birthing parents, and adoptive caregivers.

prompts.title: Screen Time for Under 3 — Decision and Plan
prompts.description: Make a values-and-evidence-based plan for screen exposure for an infant or toddler — distinguishing video chat, co-viewed content, passive background TV, and solo device use; addressing real-world caregiver constraints rather than ideal-world rules.

prompts.title: Separation Anxiety Protocol (6 months–3 years)
prompts.description: Differentiate developmentally typical separation anxiety from clinically significant separation distress, design predictable goodbye rituals and reunification scripts, and produce a 2–4 week protocol for daycare drop-off, sleep separation, or caregiver work transitions.

prompts.title: Sleep Regression Decoder (4 months–2 years)
prompts.description: Decode whether a sudden sleep disruption in an infant or toddler is a developmental regression, an environmental disruption, or a medical issue — and produce a stage-matched response plan.

prompts.title: Speech & Language Milestone Check (0–36 months)
prompts.description: Compare a child's communication development to evidence-based milestones, distinguish typical variation from intervention-worthy delay, and produce a concrete next-step recommendation including SLP referral thresholds.

prompts.title: Starting Solids Planner (4–12 months)
prompts.description: Plan an infant's introduction to solids — readiness assessment, approach selection (purée-led, baby-led weaning, hybrid), allergen introduction sequence, choking-hazard guardrails, and a 12-week ramp.

prompts.title: Toddler Biting and Hitting Response Plan (12–36 months)
prompts.description: Decode the function of toddler biting, hitting, kicking, and pushing; respond in the moment without escalating; teach replacement skills; and produce a daycare-coordinated plan with a 4-week reduction target.

prompts.title: Toddler Tantrum Response Script (12–36 months)
prompts.description: Phase-by-phase script for responding to a toddler tantrum (12–36 months) with developmental physiology in mind — distinct from a 4–8-year-old meltdown, with adjustments for limited language, peak frustration tolerance, and emerging autonomy.

prompts.title: Toilet Training Readiness and Plan (18 months–4 years)
prompts.description: Assess a child's toilet training readiness across physiological, cognitive, motor, and social-emotional axes; choose an approach (parent-led, child-led, intensive 3-day, gradual); produce a 4–8 week plan with troubleshooting for refusal, regression, and constipation.

prompts.title: When to Call the Pediatrician (0–3 years)
prompts.description: Decision guide for caregivers about whether a symptom or concern in an infant or toddler warrants emergency response, same-day call, next-business-day call, well-visit mention, or home monitoring.

prompts.title: College or Not — The Post-Secondary Pathway Conversation
prompts.description: Have the post-secondary pathway conversation honestly across 4-year college, community college, trade or apprenticeship, gap year, military, work, or undecided — accounting for family pressure, financial reality, neurodivergent and 2e considerations, and first-gen-college context.

prompts.title: Developmental Expectations 13–18 (Adolescence)
prompts.description: Map cognitive, emotional, social, physical, and identity development across ages 13–18, distinguishing typical adolescent reorganization from intervention-worthy patterns and orienting caregivers to the renegotiation of the parent–child relationship.

prompts.title: Teen Autonomy, Curfew, and Calibrated-Step Negotiation
prompts.description: Design and renegotiate calibrated autonomy steps with a teen — mobility, time, money, social, and decision-making — including curfew, transportation, sleepovers, parties, and the protocol for tightening when steps fail.

prompts.title: Teen Dating, Consent, and Relationship Health Conversations
prompts.description: Equip caregivers with conversation scripts on healthy relationships, enthusiastic and ongoing consent, dating-violence red flags, safer sex, breakups, online dating, sexting and nudes pre-loading, and sextortion response — across orientations and gender identities.

prompts.title: Teen Driving Readiness Assessment and Family Driving Contract
prompts.description: Assess driving readiness beyond chronological age, design a family driving contract using graduated-licensing principles, decide on telematics use, and provide an after-crash response protocol.

prompts.title: Teen Eating Disorder Signal Response
prompts.description: Recognize and respond to signs of anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder, ARFID, OSFED, or orthorexia in a teen — body-size-neutral assessment, Maudsley FBT-informed framing, adolescent-medicine routing, and adaptations for athletes and male-typical body presentations.

prompts.title: Teen Friend Group Concerns
prompts.description: Address concerns about a teen's friend group — substance use, risk-taking, exclusion patterns, identity-shift, perceived radicalization — using influence-boundary thinking, the rare-cases of when to forbid, and how to keep communication open across disagreement.

prompts.title: Teen Mental Health Signal Check (13–18)
prompts.description: Distinguish typical adolescent mood lability from signal patterns suggesting depression, anxiety, OCD, panic, bipolar onset, or first-episode psychosis — with adolescent-specific presentations, screening-instrument framing, and clinical routing pathways.

prompts.title: Teen Repair After Blowup (Adolescent Rupture and Repair)
prompts.description: Repair the parent–teen relationship after a blowup, slammed-door dynamic, post-fight silence, or sustained estrangement — the late-adolescent analog to early-childhood repair, with respect for autonomy, slower pacing, and explicit accountability when the caregiver overreached.

prompts.title: Teen School Disengagement Decoder
prompts.description: Differentiate adolescent school disengagement from school refusal, learning disability, depression, anxiety, identity-context (LGBTQ+ unsafe school), peer dynamics, substance use, or family stress — and design a re-engagement pathway that includes alternative-school, GED, and late-graduation options.

prompts.title: Teen Self-Harm Signal Response (NSSI)
prompts.description: Respond to non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) in a teen — differentiate from suicidality, conduct the in-the-moment response, address function, build a safety plan using the Stanley-Brown framework, restrict means, and route clinically.

prompts.title: Teen Social Media Renegotiation (Reopening the Agreement at 13+)
prompts.description: Reopen and restructure the social-media agreement at age 13+ across TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat, Discord, Reddit, and X — addressing algorithm exposure, body image, radicalization vectors, AI image and deepfake risk, sextortion, and parasocial dynamics.

prompts.title: Teen Substance Conversation Scripts (Pre-Loaded and Post-Discovery)
prompts.description: Provide pre-loaded substance conversations and post-discovery response scripts for alcohol, cannabis, vaping (nicotine and THC), prescription misuse, and polysubstance use — using harm-reduction-informed framing, SBIRT-light approach, and CRAFFT-based escalation criteria.

prompts.title: Body Image Early Intervention (Tween)
prompts.description: Catch and respond to early body-image concerns in a tween — distinguish body comments from disordered eating signals, audit family environment for harm vectors, build affirming everyday language, and route to clinical support when warranted.

prompts.title: Bullying Perpetrator Response Protocol (Tween)
prompts.description: Respond when a tween is the one bullying — interrupt the behavior, run accountability without shame, address the underlying drivers (status, modeling, exclusion, mental health, identity), and prevent the long-term trajectory.

prompts.title: Bullying Target Response Protocol (Tween)
prompts.description: Respond when a tween is the target of bullying — distinguish bullying from typical conflict, run a documented response (school engagement, evidence collection, safety plan, mental health support), and address the long-term emotional impact.

prompts.title: Developmental Expectations 9–12 (The Tween Years)
prompts.description: Map cognitive, emotional, social, and physical development across ages 9–12 — the 'tween' window — distinguishing typical from intervention-worthy patterns and orienting caregivers to the major shifts (puberty onset, identity formation, peer primacy, abstract reasoning emergence).

prompts.title: First Phone Decision Framework (Tween)
prompts.description: Help a caregiver decide whether to give a tween a phone (and which type — dumb phone, kid phone, locked smartphone, full smartphone), build a contract, set up safeguards, and plan iterative trust-building.

prompts.title: Homework Autonomy Handoff (Ages 9–12)
prompts.description: Move a tween from caregiver-led homework support to tween-led with appropriate scaffolding — distinguish executive function from motivation, build a system that supports without micromanaging, and address the most common failure modes (avoidance, perfectionism, too-late discovery).

prompts.title: Period Prep for Any Caregiver
prompts.description: Prepare a tween for menarche regardless of who's the caregiver — including dads, foster parents, grandparents, stepparents, and any caregiver who didn't experience menstruation themselves — with practical product knowledge, body framing, and emergency-on-the-go protocols.

prompts.title: Puberty Prep Conversation Scripts (Ages 8–12)
prompts.description: Scripts and structure for talking with a tween about puberty — body changes, hygiene, emotional shifts, sexuality, gender, consent — across multiple short conversations rather than one big talk.

prompts.title: School Refusal Decoder (Tween)
prompts.description: Decode tween school refusal across the four function categories (avoidance of distress, escape of social situations, attention-seeking, tangible reward), distinguish from truancy, and produce a structured re-engagement plan with school, family, and clinical coordination.

prompts.title: Social Media First Account Protocol (Tween / Adolescent Onset)
prompts.description: Decide whether to allow a tween's first social media account, set the protocol if yes (platform choice, account type, who follows whom, content monitoring, regular review), and address the most common pitfalls (algorithm exposure, social comparison, unmoderated DMs, AI image manipulation).

prompts.title: Tween Emerging Independence Negotiation
prompts.description: Help caregivers expand a tween's autonomy in calibrated steps — across mobility, time use, money, social access, and decision authority — with built-in repair when steps fail and tightening conditions when needed.

prompts.title: Tween Friendship Drama Coaching
prompts.description: Coach a tween through a specific friendship rupture, exclusion event, or social drama — by validating without solving, helping name dynamics, scaffolding the tween's own response choices, and knowing when to escalate to school or clinical support.

prompts.title: Tween Lying Pattern Function Analysis
prompts.description: Decode why a tween is lying — distinguishing developmentally typical lies from concerning patterns, identifying the function (avoidance, image management, autonomy, peer pressure, fear, mental health), and building a response that doesn't drive the lying further underground.

prompts.title: Tween Money / Allowance / Chores System Designer
prompts.description: Design an integrated system for a tween's allowance, chores, and money management — separating chores-for-membership from earned-income, building category budgeting (spend/save/give), and teaching real financial decision-making.

prompts.title: Video Game Agreement Designer (Tween)
prompts.description: Design a video-game agreement with a tween covering time, content, communication features, monetization, and exit ramps — replacing arbitrary 'screen time' caps with content- and context-aware rules.

prompts.title: Sensory Profile and At-Home Regulation Toolkit
prompts.description: Help a caregiver map a 4–8 year old's sensory profile across eight sensory systems, identify seeking vs. avoiding patterns, and build a house-specific regulation menu the child can use before, during, and after sensory load — without medicalizing typical preferences.

prompts.title: Strong-Willed Child Power Struggle Defuser
prompts.description: Reframe defiance in 4–8 year olds as developmentally healthy autonomy-seeking, then apply choice architecture, collaborative problem-solving, and register-matched scripts to resolve the specific power struggle without breaking the child's spirit or the parent's authority.

prompts.title: Meltdown Response Script (Ages 4-8)
prompts.description: In-the-moment co-regulation script for a child's meltdown — what to say, what to do, and what to avoid, from the first signal through recovery and later repair.

prompts.title: Co-Parent Information Handoff Brief
prompts.description: A clean, factual template for passing the information that matters between homes at a handoff — school events, homework, medical updates, social happenings, mood, sleep — so the receiving parent isn't blindsided. Keeps it child-focused and useful, never surveillance of the other parent. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Co-Parent Message Composer (BIFF Method)
prompts.description: Draft or rewrite a message to a co-parent using the BIFF method — Brief, Informative, Friendly, Firm — stripping out emotion, blame, and JADE (justify-argue-defend-explain), de-escalating the exchange, and keeping it businesslike and child-focused. Includes before/after examples.

prompts.title: Co-Parenting Relationship Reset Proposal
prompts.description: Help a parent propose an improved working relationship to a co-parent after a rough period — a conversation or message that acknowledges your own part, focuses forward on the kids, and sets new working agreements. Non-defensive and child-centered; not legal advice.

prompts.title: Co-Parenting Self-Audit: Am I the Problem?
prompts.description: An honest, non-defensive self-audit for a co-parent — checking for badmouthing, gatekeeping, using the kids as messengers or spies, inflexibility, and other ways you might be contributing to the conflict. Growth-oriented, with specific behaviors to check and concrete changes to make. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Co-Parenting With an Unsafe or Absent Parent
prompts.description: Navigate co-parenting — or its absence — when the other parent is unsafe, struggling with addiction, in a destabilizing mental-health crisis, incarcerated, or absent. Covers supervised/limited-contact contexts, what to tell the kids honestly and age-appropriately, holding the door open vs. protecting the child, and the child's grief about an absent parent. Safety-first; not legal advice.

prompts.title: Consistency Across Two Homes
prompts.description: Help a parent align the rules, routines, bedtimes, screen time, discipline, and homework that genuinely benefit from consistency across two homes — and identify, accept, and normalize the differences they cannot change so the child can hold 'two homes, two sets of rules' without distress. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: De-Escalation in Front of the Kids
prompts.description: An in-the-moment script for handling a flare-up at an exchange or in front of the children — disengaging from a provocation, protecting the child from the conflict, and resetting — including what to do when the other parent provokes you in front of the child. Child-protective and de-escalation-first; not legal advice.

prompts.title: High-Conflict Co-Parent Response Strategy (Parallel Parenting)
prompts.description: Build a sustainable strategy for co-parenting with a high-conflict or chronically difficult co-parent — choosing parallel vs. cooperative parenting, using gray-rock and disengagement, refusing bait, keeping documentation discipline, routing communication through a parenting app, and protecting the children from the conflict. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Long-Distance Co-Parenting Protocol
prompts.description: Maintain the parent-child relationship across distance (virtual visits, scheduled calls, async connection) and coordinate long-distance co-parenting — travel, time zones, and the child's experience of distance. Builds a workable contact rhythm and travel/logistics plan; child-centered, not legal advice.

prompts.title: New Partners & Blended-Family Coordination
prompts.description: Coordinate when one or both parents have new partners or stepfamily — clarifying the role and boundaries of a step/bonus parent, what the new partner does and doesn't do regarding discipline and decisions, how to communicate about new partners with the co-parent, and how to support the child's adjustment. Child-centered; not legal advice.

prompts.title: Shared Decision Framework for Co-Parents
prompts.description: Build a framework for making joint co-parenting decisions — medical, school, activities, religion, big purchases — and for resolving disagreements: what needs joint sign-off vs. day-to-day discretion, how to propose and decide, and what to do at impasse (mediation before court). Organizes the parents' own choices; not legal advice.

prompts.title: Autistic Child (ASD Level 1) Social Situation Decoder
prompts.description: Help a caregiver pre-teach, live-coach, and debrief confusing social situations for a 4–8 year old on the autism spectrum (Level 1 support needs / 'high-functioning'). Decode unwritten social rules, build hidden-curriculum scripts, and respond to friendship confusion without masking-pressure.

prompts.title: Hard Topics — Age-Appropriate Scripts for 4–8 Year Olds
prompts.description: Generate age-tiered (4–5 / 6–7 / 8) parent scripts for hard conversations — death of a loved one or pet, divorce or separation, bodies and consent, big feelings (fear, jealousy, shame), scary news (violence, accidents, loss), a diagnosis in the family, or the child's own diagnosis — using honest, concrete language without overload.

prompts.title: Parent-Initiated Repair Conversation After Rupture
prompts.description: Script a brief, non-shaming, developmentally-appropriate repair conversation when a caregiver has overreacted, yelled, pulled away, broken a promise, or otherwise ruptured connection with a 4–8 year old — while modeling accountability, preserving parental authority, and protecting against over-apologizing or over-explaining.

prompts.title: Apology Modeling for Kids (How Caregivers Apologize)
prompts.description: Help a caregiver apologize to a kid in a way that models real apology — clean apology vs. over-apology vs. fake apology vs. JADE (Justify, Argue, Defend, Explain) — including when to apologize, when not, and the principle that repair-rich beats perfect.

prompts.title: Boundary Holding Script Library (Across Ages and Domains)
prompts.description: Provide caregiver scripts for holding limits across ages and domains — physical safety, screen time, food, sleep, social, money — calmly, firmly, with repair after, and adapted to strong-willed temperament, anxiety, autism, and ADHD.

prompts.title: Chore System by Age (2–18)
prompts.description: Design a household-contributions system across ages 2–18 — distinguishing membership chores from earned-income chores, adapted to family structure, neurodivergent profiles, and household size, and avoiding common allowance-and-chore design failures.

prompts.title: Developmental Expectations Index (Router Across Age Bands)
prompts.description: Router prompt that links to all four age-band developmental-expectations prompts (0-3, 4-8, 9-12, 13-18), identifies which is needed for a given concern, and provides cross-cutting context for when a behavior is 'off-tier' or when looking across age bands is necessary.

prompts.title: Emotion Vocabulary Builder by Age
prompts.description: Build age-appropriate emotion vocabulary across 2–18 — naming nuanced feelings (frustrated vs. angry vs. disappointed; ashamed vs. embarrassed vs. guilty), family practices that build emotional literacy, and adaptation for autistic / alexithymic kids.

prompts.title: Family Meeting Facilitator (Weekly or Monthly)
prompts.description: Design, run, and adapt a weekly or monthly family meeting — agenda, rotating roles, decision-making norms, conflict handling, age-mix considerations, and the question of when kids stop attending — across ages 4–18 households.

prompts.title: Growth Mindset Language Audit (Family-Wide)
prompts.description: Audit the family's language for fixed vs. growth framing, conduct caregiver self-audit, and address common pitfalls (smart-talk, comparison, only-praise-effort which can land hollow) — including Dweck's later corrections to the early oversimplifications.

prompts.title: Household Constitution Designer
prompts.description: Articulate the family's values, household rules, and shared agreements — how we treat each other, how we handle conflict, what's negotiable, what's not — adapted to family structure (single, blended, multigenerational, foster / kinship) and revisited as kids age.

prompts.title: Natural and Logical Consequence Designer
prompts.description: Distinguish natural / logical / imposed consequences, identify when natural works and when it doesn't (developmental incapacity, safety, asymmetric harm), and tie consequence to behavior without escalating to punishment-spiral.

prompts.title: Praise and Encouragement Calibrator
prompts.description: Calibrate praise and encouragement across effort vs. fixed-trait, process vs. outcome, intermittent reinforcement, and neurodivergent profiles (autistic kids and 'good job' landing differently; ADHD and praise dependence) — with age-tiered application and Dweck's later corrections to the growth-mindset oversimplifications.

prompts.title: Sibling Spacing Dynamics (Patterns by Age Gap)
prompts.description: Map common sibling dynamics by age gap (under 2, 2–4, 4+, large gap with much older sibling, half / step / blended siblings), conduct functional analysis of recurring conflict, and address developmental-stage jealousy patterns.

prompts.title: When to Seek Professional Help (All Ages)
prompts.description: Decide when and which professional to engage across ages 0–18 — pediatrician, mental health, OT, SLP, PT, neurology, developmental pediatrics, adolescent medicine, therapist subtypes — with self-referral pathways and language for pushing past dismissive providers.

prompts.title: Changed-Circumstances Documentation Organizer (Court-Presentable)
prompts.description: Help a parent ORGANIZE and compile a factual record when circumstances have changed — a move, job change, school change, safety concern, or the child's needs changing. Structures and compiles the parent's own documentation into a clean, dated, neutral record. Explicitly NOT advice on whether or how to seek a legal modification — that is routed to an attorney. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Child-Centered Proposal Articulator for Mediation (Court-Presentable)
prompts.description: Help a parent translate 'what I want' into 'what serves the child' — articulating a position or proposal for mediation in best-interests, child-centered language focused on the child's needs, stability, and relationships, not a legal argument. Produces a calm, factual proposal a parent can present to a mediator, GAL, or court. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Co-Parenting Communication & Incident Log Template (Court-Presentable)
prompts.description: A template and method for keeping a factual, neutral, dated log of co-parenting communication, exchanges, missed or late pickups, and incidents — organized so it reads as a contemporaneous record, not an argument. Emphasizes facts only, no editorializing, neutral language. A record a parent can keep day-to-day and present to a mediator, GAL, or court. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Common Parenting-Plan Provisions — Plain-Language Explainer (Literacy, Not Advice)
prompts.description: A plain-language literacy explainer of common parenting-plan provisions — right of first refusal, relocation/move-away notice, travel notice and consent, access to school/medical records, decision-making (legal vs. physical custody terminology), introducing new partners, communication, and dispute resolution. For each: what it means in plain words, why parents include it, what to think about — each flagged confirm with counsel for your jurisdiction. Literacy only, not legal advice.

prompts.title: Eliciting a Child's Voice Without Putting Them in the Middle (Age-Appropriate)
prompts.description: How to elicit and represent a child's preferences by age — for a GAL interview, mediation, or custody-evaluation context — without putting the child in the middle, coaching them, interrogating them, or making them choose between parents. Heavy emphasis on age-appropriate, non-coaching methods. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Holiday, Break & Vacation Schedule Builder (Court-Presentable)
prompts.description: Build a holiday, school-break, and summer rotation schedule document — alternating vs. fixed holidays, splitting vs. alternating days, summer blocks, birthdays, and religious observances — as a clean rotation table that supersedes the regular residential schedule, written in factual, neutral language a parent can use day-to-day and present to a mediator, GAL, or court. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Low-Conflict Exchange & Transition Protocol (Court-Presentable)
prompts.description: Design a predictable, low-conflict exchange/handoff protocol document — location, timing, who's present, what travels with the child (clothes, meds, devices, comfort items, homework), curbside vs. neutral-location exchanges — written to reduce conflict at the handoff. A parent-authored protocol usable day-to-day and presentable to a mediator, GAL, or court. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Parenting Plan Builder (Court-Presentable)
prompts.description: Build a complete, child-centered parenting plan document — residential schedule, holiday and vacation rotation, decision-making authority, communication rules, transportation and exchanges, and standard provisions — written in factual, neutral language a parent can use day-to-day and present to a mediator, guardian ad litem, or court. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Residential Schedule Designer by Age (Court-Presentable)
prompts.description: Design a developmentally appropriate residential (timesharing) schedule — explain common patterns (alternating weekends, 2-2-3, 2-2-5-5, week-on/week-off, and others) in plain language, match a pattern to the child's age and needs, and produce a specific weekly schedule with days, exchange times, and a child-centered rationale a parent can use day-to-day and present to a mediator, GAL, or court. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Shared Child Expense & Logistics Tracker (Court-Presentable)
prompts.description: A template and method to track shared child expenses (medical, childcare, extracurriculars, school) and reimbursements transparently — a clean, dated record that supports cost-sharing discussions and can be presented to a mediator, GAL, or court. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Special-Needs Parenting-Plan Addendum (Court-Presentable)
prompts.description: A parenting-plan addendum for a child with disability, medical, ADHD, autism, or mental-health needs — medication continuity across homes, therapy and appointment coordination, IEP/504 coordination, shared documentation, consistency of routines and accommodations, who attends appointments, and emergency protocols. A parent-authored addendum usable day-to-day and presentable to a mediator, GAL, or court. Not legal advice.

prompts.title: Child Reactions to Divorce — A By-Age Guide
prompts.description: Help a parent anticipate and interpret how children of different ages react to a separation — the normal grief responses by developmental stage, the typical adjustment timeline, what regression and acting-out actually mean, and the specific signs that move a reaction from 'normal hard' into 'needs more support.' Emotional support, not diagnosis.

prompts.title: Divorce Hard-Questions Answer Bank
prompts.description: A ready bank of honest, age-appropriate answers to the questions children ask during a separation — 'Why?', 'Is it my fault?', 'Will you get back together?', 'Do you still love each other?', 'Who will I live with?', 'Did Daddy do something bad?' — answered without badmouthing, false promises, or oversharing adult detail. Emotional support, not legal advice.

prompts.title: Holidays & Milestones Across Two Homes — The Emotional Plan
prompts.description: Help a parent handle the EMOTIONAL side of birthdays, holidays, graduations, and religious events across two homes after divorce — managing the child's grief about a 'split' holiday, building new traditions, easing the empty-chair feeling, and navigating both parents at one event. The scheduling/logistics live in the custody set; this is the feelings plan.

prompts.title: Introducing a New Partner to the Kids — Timing & How
prompts.description: Help a divorced or separated parent decide when and how to introduce dating and a new partner to their children — reading readiness signs, pacing the disclosure and first meeting, handling the child's resistance or rapid attachment, and coordinating the disclosure with the co-parent. Child-centered emotional support, not relationship advice.

prompts.title: Shielding Kids From Adult Conflict
prompts.description: Help a parent keep children out of the middle of adult conflict during and after a divorce — avoiding loyalty binds, never disparaging the other parent, not interrogating the child about the other home, and responding well when the OTHER parent badmouths you. Child-centered emotional support, not legal strategy.

prompts.title: Telling Others & Protecting the Child's Privacy
prompts.description: Help a parent decide what to tell teachers, coaches, extended family, and friends about a separation — and how — while helping the child keep control of their own narrative and privacy: what's the child's to share versus the parent's, and how to give the child language and permission. Emotional support, not legal advice.

prompts.title: Telling the Kids: The Separation Conversation Script
prompts.description: Build the joint 'we're separating' conversation — ideally delivered by both parents together — with age-tiered language, the core reassurances every child needs to hear, what NOT to say, and how to hold the first reactions (crying, anger, silence, 'why').

prompts.title: The Parent's Own Grief — Keeping It Off the Kids
prompts.description: Help the parenting parent manage their own grief, anger, and anxiety during a divorce so it doesn't leak onto the children — protecting kids from being used as confidant, messenger, spy, or emotional caretaker, handling the urge to vent about the ex in front of the child, and getting the parent their own real support. Emotional support, not therapy.

prompts.title: Two Homes — Helping Kids Move Between Them
prompts.description: Help a child adjust emotionally to living in and moving between two homes — building transition rituals, handling the 'I miss the other parent' moment, easing the reentry friction after exchanges, and making each home genuinely feel like home. Emotional support, not custody scheduling.

prompts.title: When a Child Needs More Than Time — Warning Signs & Getting Help
