prompts.description: Help a parent tell normal divorce adjustment from clinical concern — the behavioral and emotional warning signs that a child isn't coping and needs a therapist or more help, how to distinguish ordinary grief from red flags, how to bring in a child therapist, and a clear escalation pathway. Heavy safety framing; not a diagnostic tool.

prompts.title: Behavior Function Decoder (Ages 4-8)
prompts.description: Figure out what a child's challenging behavior is actually communicating using a parent-friendly ABC (antecedent-behavior-consequence) analysis.

prompts.title: Developmental Expectations: Ages 4 to 8
prompts.description: Age-tiered map (4-5, 6-7, 8) of what's typical, what's intense-but-typical, and what's worth mentioning to a pediatrician — across behavior, emotion, cognition, social, self-care, and neurodivergence-adjacent signals.

prompts.title: Parenting Style Self-Assessment and Leverage-Point Finder
prompts.description: Help a caregiver of a 4–8 year old map their default parenting style across warmth and structure axes, compare it against their actual values and their child's temperament, and identify 1–3 specific leverage points where a small change would produce the largest improvement — without shame, diagnosis, or generic advice.

prompts.title: When to Seek Professional Help (Parenting 4-8)
prompts.description: Decision guide to help parents of 4- to 8-year-olds figure out whether a behavior, mood, developmental, or family concern warrants a pediatrician, developmental specialist, mental health clinician, OT, SLP — and how urgently.

prompts.title: ADHD Executive Function Scaffold (Ages 4-8)
prompts.description: Build home scaffolds for a 4-8-year-old with ADHD (diagnosed or suspected): task initiation, working memory, transitions, time awareness, and emotional regulation — externalized so the child can actually use them.

prompts.title: Parent Co-Regulation Reset
prompts.description: Help a parent recognize when their own nervous system is flooded, reset it in under 5 minutes, and respond to their child from a regulated state — because no strategy works from a dysregulated parent.

prompts.title: Parenting Scenario Simulator — Rehearse Tough Moments
prompts.description: Run a structured roleplay where the AI plays the 4–8 year old child in a specific tough scenario (meltdown, defiance, friendship confusion, a hard question) so the parent can rehearse responses, get feedback on what landed and what didn't, and iterate scripts before the real moment.

prompts.title: Sibling Conflict Coach — Fairness, Jealousy, and Tattling
prompts.description: Help a caregiver coach 4–8 year old siblings through recurring conflict — fairness fights, jealousy, tattling, physical aggression, dominance-play — without taking sides, shaming either child, or trying to enforce equal treatment. Includes scripts, household-rule frameworks, and adaptations by age gap and neurodivergence.

prompts.title: Daily Routine Designer — Morning, After-School, Bedtime
prompts.description: Design three house-specific daily routines for a 4–8 year old (morning, after-school, bedtime) with visual schedule specs, realistic time budgets, friction-point eliminations, and clear adaptations for ADHD, autism (ASD Level 1), strong-willed, and sensory-sensitive profiles.

prompts.title: Transitions and Warnings Protocol
prompts.description: Reduce daily friction around transitions (leaving the park, screen-off, stopping play, coming to dinner, leaving a friend's house) for 4–8 year olds using timed warnings, previews, first/then framing, and state-matched scripts — with adaptations for ADHD, autistic, strong-willed, and sensory-sensitive kids.

prompts.title: Parent-to-Teacher Email Composer — Concerns, Requests, and Celebrations
prompts.description: Helps a parent draft a short, respectful, collaborative email to their 4–8 year old's teacher — for raising a concern, requesting a change or meeting, sharing useful context about their child (including ADHD / autism / strong-willed temperament), or offering a thank-you — without sounding accusatory, vague, or overbearing.

prompts.title: School Accommodation Conversation Prep — For Kids Who Excel Academically but Struggle Behaviorally or Socially
prompts.description: Prepares a parent for a 504 / informal accommodation / teacher-team conversation about a 4–8 year old whose academic performance is fine (or advanced) but whose ADHD, autism, anxiety, or executive-function profile is creating behavioral, social, or regulatory friction the school may be dismissing as 'not a real problem because grades are fine.' Produces a 1-page parent brief: concerns, supporting evidence, specific asks, anticipated objections, and fallback positions.

prompts.title: Reward System Pre-Mortem (Sticker Charts, Allowance, Behavior Contracts)
prompts.description: Stress-tests a planned reward, sticker chart, allowance, or behavior contract before rolling it out — surfaces the five ways your kid (or the family system) will warp around it, and what to track instead.

prompts.title: Explain-Like-I'm-Nine Converter — Plain-Language Rewrite That Keeps the Truth Intact
prompts.description: Rewrite a technical or jargon-heavy passage so a smart nine-year-old could follow it, without dumbing down the actual claims, then prove nothing true was lost or distorted.

prompts.title: Fresh Perspective Generator
prompts.description: Break out of conventional thinking by generating 3 unconventional perspectives on any challenge — from practical reframes to radical rethinks, each with a vivid story, memorable metaphor, and actionable next step

prompts.title: Goal Setting and Reflection Loop
prompts.description: Regular goal review and adjustment — honestly assess progress, identify what's working and what isn't, celebrate wins, adjust goals based on new information, and produce an updated action plan

prompts.title: Goal System Designer
prompts.description: Transform vague aspirations into SMART goals with tracking systems, weekly review rituals, and accountability structures — produces a complete goal system you can implement this quarter

prompts.title: Interrogative Exploration Mode
prompts.description: Surface unknowns before analysis by generating strategic open-ended questions — forces question-first thinking to reveal hidden assumptions, blind spots, and unexplored dimensions of any topic

prompts.title: Learning Task Decomposition
prompts.description: Break a vague learning goal into 7-9 atomic sub-skills with deliberate practice drills, dependency mapping, and a progressive practice schedule

prompts.title: Limiting Belief Reframer
prompts.description: Transform limiting beliefs into empowering perspectives — using empirical counter-evidence, cognitive reframing techniques, and small experiments to test new beliefs in practice

prompts.title: Memory Palace Generator
prompts.description: Transform abstract information into vivid, spatial memory structures — builds a complete memory palace with room-by-room associations, sensory anchors, and walkthrough instructions for reliable recall

prompts.title: Personal Blind Spot Identifier
prompts.description: Identify plausible blind spots in your thinking, assumptions, or behavior — with falsifiable experiments to test each one and concrete steps to address what you find

prompts.title: Regret Minimization Decision Framework
prompts.description: Consult your future self on major decisions — structured perspective shift using time-horizon analysis, trade-off mapping, and regret forecasting to make choices you can live with long-term

prompts.title: Skill Breakdown Blueprint
prompts.description: Decompose any complex skill into 7-9 atomic sub-skills with practice drills, learning path visualization, 8-week practice schedule, and common pitfall prevention

prompts.title: Solo Developer Automation Audit
prompts.description: Identify what to automate in your solo dev workflow — repetitive tasks audit, tool recommendations, ROI calculation for automation investment, and prioritized automation plan

prompts.title: Solo Developer Burnout Prevention
prompts.description: Burnout detection and prevention for solo developers — workload assessment, boundary-setting strategies, sustainable pace definition, delegation opportunities, and recovery protocols

prompts.title: Solo Developer Context Switching Reducer
prompts.description: Reduce context-switching overhead — analyze typical task switches, batch similar activities, design notification boundaries, and create focused work blocks for different roles

prompts.title: Solo Developer Network Building
prompts.description: Build a professional network as a solo developer — online communities, conferences, mentorship, accountability partners, and leveraging your app for opportunities

prompts.title: Solo Developer Skill Gap Assessment
prompts.description: Assess skill gaps as a solo developer — map required skills across development, backend, design, marketing, business, and legal against current abilities, identify the most impactful skill to develop next, and find efficient learning paths

prompts.title: Stakeholder Navigation Guide
prompts.description: Analyze complex stakeholder dynamics and develop strategic influence plans — maps power, incentives, and relationships to identify the best path through organizational politics

prompts.title: Stakeholder Politics Navigator
prompts.description: Analyze organizational politics, map stakeholder power dynamics and incentives, and develop strategic options for navigating complex multi-party decisions

prompts.title: Strategic Question Generator
prompts.description: Surface hidden assumptions and critical information through structured questioning — generates 10-12 strategic open-ended questions across multiple dimensions, then synthesizes patterns from your answers

prompts.title: Tight Constraint Topic Analyzer
prompts.description: Deep analysis of any topic under strict constraints — word limits, required perspectives, mandatory frameworks, and source requirements force rigorous, focused thinking

prompts.title: Build a Proof-of-Work Portfolio Over a Defined Horizon
prompts.description: Plan a portfolio of shippable artifacts over a 3–12 month horizon, chosen so each one is defensible on its own, accumulates into a coherent track record, and forces the user into repeated shipping rather than repeated planning.

prompts.title: Convert a Vague Goal into a Project You Fully Own
prompts.description: Turn a diffuse aspiration into a concrete project with named scope, a first deliverable, an owner of record, and a definition of done — so the work stops drifting and starts moving.

prompts.title: Cut Scope Creep on a Personal Project Back to a Shippable Core
prompts.description: Reconstruct the original commitment for a stalled personal project, tag every element that got added since, classify each addition against a fixed taxonomy of creep sources, and re-cut to a shippable core with one next action.

prompts.title: Define the Next Concrete Action for the Day
prompts.description: Force a single, unambiguous next physical action out of a mental pile of todos, intentions, and open loops — the kind of action a tired person can start within 60 seconds.

prompts.title: Design a Ship-Within-a-Short-Window Exercise
prompts.description: Design a 2–10 day sprint where the user ships something substantial and real to an external audience, with bounded scope, forced deadline, and a definition of done that survives contact with reality.

prompts.title: Design an Accountability Structure Matched to What the User Responds To
prompts.description: Pick the one accountability mechanism — partner, cadence, stakes, and commitment format — that fits the user's actual track record of what makes them follow through, then produce the exact first message to set it up today.

prompts.title: Detect Planning That Masquerades as Execution
prompts.description: Audit a user's recent work sessions to find activity that feels like execution but is actually sophisticated procrastination — research binges, tool shopping, framework shopping, endless outlining — and name the underlying avoidance.

prompts.title: Diagnose Stage of Burnout and Choose a Recovery Path
prompts.description: Differentiate depletion vs. burnout vs. boredom-burnout vs. mismatch-burnout from observed signals, and prescribe a stage-appropriate recovery — rest design, not productivity tweaks.

prompts.title: Diagnose Stuckness Across a Fixed Taxonomy of Blockers
prompts.description: When the user is 'stuck' on a project, classify the stuckness into one of a small fixed set of blocker types — each with a different unblock move — so the user stops searching and starts doing the right unblock action.

prompts.title: End-of-Session Review to Capture Momentum and Lessons
prompts.description: A 5–10 minute review at the end of a work session that captures what was produced, what was learned, where momentum was lost, and what the first action of the next session will be — so the next session starts in motion, not in orientation.

prompts.title: Extract Useful Feedback from People Who've Seen the Work
prompts.description: Convert informal reactions and polite compliments from people who've encountered the user's shipped work into concrete, usable signal — what actually landed, what didn't, and what to change, without depending on them to be expert critics.

prompts.title: Post-Decision Regret Analysis Without Hindsight Bias
prompts.description: Examine a decision the user now regrets, separate process quality from outcome quality, and extract a transferable update — not a verdict on the past self.

prompts.title: Rapid-Start Mode: Begin Meaningful Work Within a Minute
prompts.description: A 60-second protocol for moving from 'sitting at the desk' to 'producing an artifact' — designed for days when warm-up rituals have expanded to fill the session, and for low-energy moments when the only move is to start.

prompts.title: Reframe Skill Gaps as Separate from Project Goals
prompts.description: Separate a stated skill gap from the project the user is trying to ship, so learning doesn't silently become a substitute for shipping — and the real minimum needed is isolated and bounded.

prompts.title: Repair Broken Consistency in a Personal Habit Loop
prompts.description: Diagnose why a personal habit the user had been keeping has broken down, choose a repair action sized to the break, and restart without requiring a motivational speech or a new tracking app.

prompts.title: Run a Time-Boxed Foundation-Building Session with Full Context Capture
prompts.description: A 2–4 hour focused session for laying the foundation of a new project — the kind of session where decisions, structure, and context get made once so later sessions don't have to rediscover them — with explicit capture so the foundation is durable.

prompts.title: Weekly Review That Compounds Effort into a System
prompts.description: A 20–40 minute weekly review that turns individual sessions into a durable system: what shipped, what didn't and why, what the next week's single most important move is, and one repeatable pattern harvested from the week's data.

prompts.title: Assess a Role's Structural Vulnerability (Not Just Task Automation)
prompts.description: Evaluate a specific role's structural vulnerability by analyzing the economic function it performs, the coordination costs it absorbs, and the scarce inputs it controls — not by listing which tasks AI can do. Produces a vulnerability grade with evidence, not a binary 'safe/not safe' verdict.

prompts.title: Audit a Work Week Against Coordination-Tax Categories
prompts.description: Classify each recurring block on a real calendar week into coordination-tax categories (status, alignment, approval, translation, rework, triage) so the user can see how much of their week is coordination rather than production work — and which categories are automatable, delegatable, or structurally load-bearing.

prompts.title: Build a 90-Day Repositioning Plan Toward Surviving / Adjacent Roles
prompts.description: Translate a vulnerability assessment and residual-skills inventory into a concrete 90-day plan: which adjacent role(s) to bridge into, what evidence the user will produce, what signals they'll send, and which weekly checkpoints catch drift. Plans, not wish-lists.

prompts.title: Build a Positioning Statement From Evidence of Past Wins
prompts.description: Derive a sharp professional positioning statement — who you help, with what specific problem, and why you over alternatives — from evidence of the user's actual past wins and the pattern in who sought them out. Refuses generic personal-brand language and adjective soup.

prompts.title: Decide Whether Your Next Move Is Internal or External
prompts.description: Compare an internal move (new role or expanded scope at the current employer) against an external move (new employer) on growth, leverage, risk, and time-to-impact, using the user's real situation, and issue one recommendation with the disconfirming evidence that would flip it.

prompts.title: Inventory Residual Skills That Survive Automation
prompts.description: Catalog the judgment, taste, and context the user actually holds — separating real residual skills (scarce, transferable, defensible) from skills they wish they had, tasks they happen to do, or credentials that aren't skills. Produces a ranked inventory keyed to evidence.

prompts.title: Separate Your Durable Skill Moat From Your Automatable Surface Area
prompts.description: Split the user's working skillset into a durable moat (judgment, taste, relationships, deep context) versus automatable surface area, using evidence of where their skills actually hold value, then concentrate future investment on the one moat component with the most leverage.

prompts.title: Turn a Position-to-Position Skill Gap Into a Sequenced Reskilling Roadmap
prompts.description: Convert the specific skill gap between the user's current position and a named target position into an evidence-checked, sequenced reskilling roadmap — ordered by dependency and proof-value, with a checkpoint per skill — while deferring generic curriculum design to domain-learning/.

prompts.title: After a Mistake, Separate the Fact From the Self-Attack From the Fair Correction
prompts.description: Take a specific mistake you're beating yourself up over and split it into the factual error, the disproportionate self-attack layered on top, and the fair correction that's actually warranted — ending with the one corrective action, minus the punishment.

prompts.title: Debrief a Specific Emotionally Charged Event and Extract One Pattern
prompts.description: After a heated or emotional event has passed, walk through what happened, what you felt, and what you did, separate the parts to keep from the parts to change, and extract the single repeatable pattern worth carrying forward.

prompts.title: Design a Personal Cooldown Ritual for After a Charged Moment
prompts.description: Build a short, repeatable cooldown ritual tailored to what actually settles you — combining a physiological down-regulation step with a re-entry cue — so a charged moment doesn't bleed into the rest of your day.

prompts.title: Hold Two Opposed True Feelings Without Collapsing to One
prompts.description: Take a situation where you feel two contradictory things at once (relief and grief, love and anger, excitement and dread) and name both fully, identify what each is protecting, and let both stand instead of forcing a single 'real' feeling.

prompts.title: Map a Recurring Over-Reaction to Its Trigger and the Interpretation In Between
prompts.description: Take a reaction that keeps coming out bigger than the situation warrants, trace it to its specific trigger and the split-second interpretation that sits between trigger and reaction, and pre-plan one intercept for the next time.

prompts.title: Process a Specific Disappointment by Separating the Gap, the Story, and the Adjustment
prompts.description: Take one concrete disappointment and split it into the measurable gap (expected vs. actual), the interpretation added on top, and a single realistic adjustment — so the letdown lands cleanly instead of spiraling.

prompts.title: Read In-the-Moment Jealousy as a Pointer and Convert It Into One Pursuit
prompts.description: Take a specific flash of jealousy or envy and decode it into the precise thing you actually want, then convert that want into one concrete pursuit — turning a corrosive feeling into a direction.

prompts.title: Separate Guilt (I Did a Bad Thing) From Shame (I Am Bad) and Route Each Correctly
prompts.description: Take a heavy self-directed feeling after something you did and sort it into guilt (an action, points to repair) versus shame (a global self-verdict, a distortion to disarm), then route each to its correct response.

prompts.title: Sort a Swirl of Worries Into One Action Each or a Deliberate Park
prompts.description: Take an anxious swirl of many worries, split each into controllable (one concrete action) versus not-controllable (a deliberate park with a review date), and end with the single first action to take now.

prompts.title: Turn a Vague 'Bad' Feeling Into Named Emotions and the Need Underneath
prompts.description: Take one undifferentiated 'off' or 'bad' feeling and resolve it into precisely named emotions plus the specific unmet need each points at, so the feeling becomes workable instead of a fog.

prompts.title: Define Anti-Goals and Failure States to Protect the Real Goals
prompts.description: Define what the user will deliberately NOT pursue this period and the concrete failure states to avoid, then convert each into a guardrail that protects the keystone goals. Outputs an anti-goal list, the failure states, and one tripwire per failure state.

prompts.title: Derive One or Two Goals From Your Operating Values
prompts.description: Take the user's already-surfaced operating values and derive 1–2 concrete, observable goals that close the gap between what they value and what they're actually doing. Defers the values-surfacing itself to identity_values_clarification.md; this prompt only builds the values→action bridge.

prompts.title: Diagnose Why a Goal Isn't Moving and Prescribe One Unblock
prompts.description: For a goal that has stopped moving, classify the stall against a fixed 6-cause taxonomy (wrong goal / wrong size / no next action / capacity / motivation / hidden conflict) using the user's evidence, then prescribe the single unblock move that fits the diagnosed cause.

prompts.title: Plan a Year or Quarter From Evidence, Not Resolutions
prompts.description: Turn a year or quarter into a small set of themes plus 2–3 keystone goals derived from evidence of what the last period actually produced, tolerated, and dropped — instead of from aspiration. Outputs the themes, the keystone goals, and the one anti-resolution guardrail.

prompts.title: Resolve Two Goals Competing for the Same Finite Resource
prompts.description: When two or more real goals compete for the same finite resource (time, money, energy, or attention), surface the true conflict, quantify the shared scarce resource, and force a decision: rank one above the other or sequence them — not a fantasy of doing both.

prompts.title: Right-Size a Goal That's Too Big to Start or Too Small to Pull
prompts.description: Calibrate a goal that never gets started (too big) or generates no traction (too small) to the right size for the user's real weekly capacity and horizon. Diagnoses the sizing fault, then rewrites the goal to a size the user will actually start and sustain.

prompts.title: Anchor a New Habit Onto an Existing Routine (Habit Stacking)
prompts.description: Find a reliable existing routine to use as an anchor and bolt a small new habit directly onto it, producing a stable 'after X, I will Y' chain that fires without needing a separate reminder or fresh motivation.

prompts.title: Break an Unwanted Habit Through Friction Analysis and Substitution
prompts.description: Remove an unwanted habit by mapping its actual cue-routine-reward loop, identifying the real reward it delivers, raising friction on the routine, and substituting a behavior that satisfies the same reward — instead of relying on suppression and willpower.

prompts.title: Convert a Vague Intention Into Precise If-Then Implementation Intentions
prompts.description: Take a fuzzy intention ('I'll exercise more', 'I should reply faster') and translate it into one or more precise if-then implementation intentions anchored to a specific cue, time, and location, plus coping if-thens for the predictable obstacles.

prompts.title: Design a Habit From the Identity It Votes For, Not the Outcome It Chases
prompts.description: Take an identity the user wants to become ('someone who X') and design the smallest repeatable behavior that counts as a vote for it, so each rep is evidence of the identity rather than a step toward a distant outcome.

prompts.title: Design a Habit-Tracking System Matched to Your Actual Tolerance
prompts.description: Design the lightest habit-tracking system the user will actually keep — sized to their real tolerance for logging, not an aspirational 30-metric dashboard they'll abandon in a week — by fixing what gets tracked, in what medium, at what moment, and what happens on a miss.

prompts.title: Design a New Habit From Cue, Routine, Reward, and Implementation Intention
prompts.description: Turn a vague intention ('I want to exercise more') into a concretely engineered habit loop — a specific cue, a floor-sized routine, an honest reward, and an if-then implementation intention — that can actually run on a low-motivation day.

prompts.title: Engineer the Environment So a Specific Habit Runs (or Doesn't)
prompts.description: Redesign the immediate surroundings of a single target habit — making the cue obvious and the floor routine frictionless for a wanted habit, or burying the cue and adding friction for an unwanted one — so the behavior follows the environment instead of willpower.

prompts.title: Identify the Keystone Habit Whose Change Cascades Into Others
prompts.description: When a user wants to change many things at once, find the single keystone habit whose change reliably triggers downstream improvements — so they invest in one high-leverage behavior instead of spreading effort across ten.

prompts.title: Pair a Want-To-Do With a Should-Do So the Habit Pulls Itself
prompts.description: Find honest temptation bundles that fit the user's real life — pairing a genuinely wanted activity with a should-do habit so the reward makes the habit self-pulling — and reject the fake bundles that either dilute the pleasure or don't survive contact with a bad day.

prompts.title: Recover a Missed Streak Without an All-or-Nothing Spiral
prompts.description: After breaking a streak, interrupt the all-or-nothing thinking that turns one missed day into total abandonment, set a same-/next-day re-entry rule, and rebuild momentum from the floor — distinct from full habit-loop repair.

prompts.title: Audit the Inner Critic's Specific Sentences
prompts.description: Capture the user's actual recurring self-critical sentences verbatim, classify each by distortion type, and produce a counter-sentence grounded in evidence — not affirmations.

prompts.title: Audit the Limiting Self-Story and Reframe It on the Same Facts
prompts.description: Extract the throughline of the story the user tells about themselves, classify its limiting shape, test it against the full fact set including omitted counter-facts, and rewrite it into a truer, more usable narrative that the old story's own evidence supports.

prompts.title: Calibrate Confidence Against Evidence in Both Directions
prompts.description: Two-mode self-assessment: impostor-syndrome correction (where evidence is being ignored) and overconfidence audit (where evidence is being inflated). Same calibration scaffolding, different direction.

prompts.title: Develop Discernment in a Specific Domain
prompts.description: Build a structured taste-training loop in a chosen domain — exposure schedule, judgment exercises, feedback loop, reference-class library — rather than passive consumption. Distinct from technical skill-gap reframing.

prompts.title: Diagnose What Your Envy Is Pointing At
prompts.description: Given a specific person or outcome the user envies, separate the signal (a real desire worth acting on) from the noise (status mimicry, near-miss grief, reflex comparison) using a fixed envy-pattern taxonomy.

prompts.title: Diagnose Why the 'Why' Has Gone Quiet
prompts.description: When the user has lost the felt sense of purpose on a project, role, or life arc, classify the loss as depletion / mismatch / completion / drift / or unmet hidden goal — each has a different move. Closes the referral gap from agency_stuck_diagnosis category 12.

prompts.title: Map Performed-Role Versus Acting-From-Self, and Close One Gap
prompts.description: Across the user's real contexts, classify each as aligned self, chosen adaptation, or costly performance; score the cost of each performance; distinguish healthy code-switching from identity-eroding suppression; and produce one bounded, safe move to close the single most expensive gap.

prompts.title: Scope a Realistic Remaining Horizon and Stop Deferring One Thing
prompts.description: Set a sober realistic time horizon, classify the user's deferred 'someday' items by whether their window is closing, open, perpetual, or already foreclosed, cross-check against how weeks are actually spent, and produce one first step to stop deferring the highest-regret closing-window item.

prompts.title: Structured Audit at a Major Life Inflection
prompts.description: At a transition (midlife, post-launch, post-loss, post-promotion, after a long arc closes), produce a structured reckoning across dimensions — identity, relationships, work, health, time-left — without prescribing a generic answer.

prompts.title: Surface Operating Values From Past Decisions, Not Aspirations
prompts.description: Extract the user's revealed values from a list of recent real decisions and trade-offs they actually made, then contrast with their stated values to expose specific mismatches and propose one realignment move.

prompts.title: Surface Signature Strengths From Evidence, Not a Strengths Quiz
prompts.description: Derive the user's real strengths from evidence of what they do well and reach for, separate them from draining competencies, name the top few, and place one underused signature strength into an arena where it is currently missing.

prompts.title: Do the 'Who Am I Now' Work When a Defining Role Has Ended or Changed
prompts.description: When a role that defined you has ended, separate the parts of self that were role-dependent from the parts that were always yours, name what genuinely died versus what merely lost its container, and reclaim one durable thread through a concrete act.

prompts.title: Locate Yourself on the Ending → Neutral-Zone → New-Beginning Map and Name What This Phase Needs
prompts.description: A generic transition navigator: place the user in Bridges' three-phase model (ending, neutral zone, new beginning), name what the current phase actually requires, and give the one move that phase needs — plus the signal for advancing.

prompts.title: Navigate the First 90 Days in a New Role Without Running the Old Playbook
prompts.description: Map what actually changed in a new job or promotion, locate where old habits now misfire, and commit to the one relationship and one competence to invest in first — instead of coasting on prior-role instincts.

prompts.title: Protect One Thread of Pre-Parent Self Without Guilt in New Parenthood
prompts.description: Reconcile pre-parent identity with new reality by naming what actually changed, distinguishing genuine loss from temporary compression, and protecting one non-negotiable thread of self while renegotiating time and partnership.

prompts.title: Re-Enter Work After Parental, Medical, or Sabbatical Leave Without Pretending Nothing Changed
prompts.description: Recalibrate realistic capacity, reset boundaries, and structure a deliberate re-onboarding after extended leave — instead of snapping back to the pre-leave pace that the leave itself made impossible.

prompts.title: Rebuild Routine, Belonging, and Place-Attachment After a Move You Already Made
prompts.description: Diagnose which layer of settling-in has stalled after a completed relocation — logistics, routine, social fabric, or place-attachment — and commit to the one deliberate re-rooting action that unblocks the rest.

prompts.title: Rebuild Routine, Social Fabric, and Self-Concept After a Relationship Ends
prompts.description: After a breakup or divorce, diagnose which structures the relationship silently held — daily routine, social network, shared identity, physical home, future story — and commit to one rebuilding move for the most collapsed one.

prompts.title: Reclaim Purpose, Structure, and Couple Identity After the Children Leave
prompts.description: Reorient after children leave home by auditing what the parenting role occupied — time, purpose, structure, couple identity, daily contact — and committing to one deliberate move to fill the highest-cost vacated space.

prompts.title: Replace Work-Derived Identity, Structure, and Social Contact After Retirement
prompts.description: Redesign the four functions a career quietly provided — identity, daily structure, social contact, and purpose — after stopping work, and commit to one recurring anchor that rebuilds the highest-cost one.

prompts.title: Run a Staged Recovery Arc After a Layoff or Firing — Separating the Event From Self-Worth
prompts.description: Locate which phase of job-loss recovery you're in — stabilize, process, reframe, re-enter — and produce the single phase-appropriate move, refusing to skip grief into a frantic job hunt or to stall in rumination.

prompts.title: Aging-Parent Care Decision — Care Level, Capacity, Finances, Siblings, the Parent's Wishes, and Reversibility
prompts.description: Structure the decision of how to care for an aging parent across a fixed set of arrangements (stay-at-home with support, move-in, assisted living, memory/skilled care, sibling-shared, professional home care). Matches the parent's actual care needs and trajectory against your capacity, the finances, the sibling split, and — decisively — the parent's own wishes and autonomy. Ends with a recommended primary arrangement plus a tripwire for when it must escalate, and routes every legal, financial, and medical specific to the right professional.

prompts.title: Career Offer Evaluation — Beyond Compensation to Growth, Network, Optionality, and BATNA
prompts.description: Evaluate a job offer across the dimensions that predict long-run career satisfaction and trajectory, not just the compensation line. Walks through cash, equity, and benefits, then extends to the dimensions most commonly under-weighted: skill growth, network quality, optionality (what doors this opens or closes), reputation carry-forward, manager and team fit, and lifestyle. Compares against BATNA and ends with a clear accept / counter / decline / defer recommendation with reasoning.

prompts.title: Cofounder and Business Partner Selection — Failure Mode Audit with Pre-Mortem
prompts.description: Evaluate a prospective cofounder or business partner against the failure modes that most commonly destroy co-founded companies. Covers skill complementarity, observed work ethic, values alignment on hard cases (not easy ones), conflict-resolution patterns, financial alignment, vesting and equity terms, exit-trigger clarity, and behavior under stress. Forces a pre-mortem: imagine the partnership has failed in 3 years, then reason backward to what the cause was. Counters the bias toward partnering with people you like rather than people you can work with through the hard parts.

prompts.title: Difficult Relationship Audit — Before Acting, Structure What's Actually Happening
prompts.description: Structured audit of a difficult relationship (partner, family member, close friend, colleague) before taking consequential action. Walks through what's specifically happening, the concrete impact on the user, the user's own contribution, what's been tried, what hasn't, what the relationship offers that makes it worth working on, and what a clean exit looks like at what cost. Distinguishes 'hard but worth working on' from 'harmful and the cost of staying exceeds the cost of leaving.' Direct without prescribing.

prompts.title: Education Program Choice — Outcome Track Record, Signaling vs. Skill, and No-Program Alternative
prompts.description: Compare degree programs, bootcamps, certifications, and alternative paths against a specific goal. Forces evaluation of each program's actual outcome track record (not marketing claims), cost including opportunity cost, signaling vs. skill-building ratio, and when no-program is the correct answer. Designed to counter the default bias toward formal credentials when the goal may be achievable through cheaper, faster, or more direct paths.

prompts.title: Family Planning Tradeoffs — Timing, Geography, Career, Support Systems, and Partner Alignment
prompts.description: Structure the tradeoffs involved in family planning decisions: timing of children, whether to have more children, geographic moves with family implications, balancing partner careers, and supporting aging parents. Walks through biological and health considerations, career timing, financial readiness, geography of support, partner alignment, and optionality across life stages. Surfaces what each option costs and what it gives, and identifies the conversations that need to happen with whom. Direct about tradeoffs without prescribing.

prompts.title: Health Decision Research — Evidence Structure, Source Quality, Question Preparation, and Decision Documentation
prompts.description: Support the research process for a non-emergency health decision: treatment options, surgical decisions, screening choices, lifestyle interventions, or second-opinion strategy. Clarifies the underlying question (often not what it first appears), structures the evidence available (study quality, comparable cases, base rates), identifies what to bring to appointments, frames the risk-benefit analysis per option, and documents the reasoning for auditability. This is research scaffolding — the user makes the decision with their clinician.

prompts.title: Major Commitment Decision — Load-Bearing Compatibility, Dealbreakers, and What More Data You Need
prompts.description: Structure a major relationship-commitment decision — marriage, long-term partnership, or moving in together. Scores compatibility on a fixed set of load-bearing dimensions using observed evidence rather than feeling, isolates true dealbreakers from workable differences, names what you still don't know and how to find out, and ends with one of three calls: commit, not-yet (with the specific data to gather), or don't-commit. Replaces 'is this the one' mysticism with a structured read of what's actually known.

prompts.title: Major Purchase Research — Job Clarity, TCO, Attribute Matrix, and Walk-Away Criteria
prompts.description: Structure the research process for a major purchase (house, vehicle, appliance, equipment worth months of savings) before committing. Forces clarification of the actual job the purchase is solving, establishes true total cost of ownership beyond sticker price, builds a defensible attribute comparison, and ends with walk-away criteria and a target offer. Counters the dominant failure modes: anchoring on the first option seen, confusing wants with jobs, and ignoring costs that accumulate after purchase.

prompts.title: Personal Financial Decision Framework — What It Optimizes, Tail Risk, Irreversibility, and Fee-Only Smell Test
prompts.description: Framework for evaluating a major personal financial decision: mortgage sizing, leverage, asset allocation shift, large purchase financing, early retirement feasibility, business loan, equity vs. cash compensation, investment concentration. Forces clarity on what the decision actually optimizes (not just return), the time horizon, tax implications, tail-risk scenarios, and irreversibility. Ends with the fee-only advisor smell test: would a fiduciary with no stake in the outcome make this same recommendation?

prompts.title: Quit or Persist — Optionality, Sunk Cost, Tripwires, and Calibration Anchor
prompts.description: Structure the quit-or-persist decision for a job, project, relationship, business, or education path. Forces clarity on the goal being pursued, viability of the current path, cost of one more period vs. cost of quitting, where sunk cost is distorting the analysis, what a fresh observer would recommend, and what tripwires should force a quit if persistence is chosen. Ends with one of three recommendations: persist with tripwire, quit, or pause — plus a calibration anchor written down today.

prompts.title: Relocation Decision — Multi-Criteria Analysis with Identity, Network, and Optionality Layers
prompts.description: Structure a relocation decision (city, country, neighborhood, hybrid) across financial, career, family, social, identity, and optionality dimensions. Includes the often-skipped layers: what the move signals about identity, what social capital is forfeited, what optionality is gained or lost, and what's hard to reverse. Designed for individuals or couples making one of the most consequential and personally distorting decisions in their lives.

prompts.title: Sabbatical / Career-Break Decision — Purpose, Runway, Re-Entry Risk, and Opportunity Cost
prompts.description: Evaluate taking a sabbatical or extended career break. Forces a clear answer to what the break is actually for (a fixed purpose taxonomy), computes the real runway including re-entry, sizes the re-entry risk by field and gap length, weighs the opportunity cost against the base case of not taking it, and designs the least-irreversible version. Ends with one of three calls: take it, don't take it, or restructure it (shorter, partial, or a negotiated leave) — plus a re-entry plan and a tripwire.

prompts.title: Start a Business vs. Stay Employed — Risk Tolerance, Runway, Real Tradeoffs, and the Staged Option
prompts.description: Structure the choice between starting a business and taking or keeping employment. Separates the real tradeoffs (income variance, runway, autonomy, downside floor, identity) from the imagined ones (romanticized freedom, imagined riches, fear of the leap), tests genuine risk tolerance against the actual downside, and looks hard at the staged/reversible middle — building on the side to a validation milestone before leaving a paycheck. Ends with one of three calls: start now, stay employed, or stage it, with a tripwire and a re-employment fallback.

prompts.title: Weekly Reflection Session for AI-Augmented Work
prompts.description: Runs a focused 30-minute weekly reflection that detects patterns across the week's AI-augmented sessions — what worked, what didn't, what's recurring, what deserves a rule or a capture. Converts in-the-moment frustration into system-level improvement before the pattern fades.

prompts.title: AI Change Management Specialist — Role-Readiness Assessment

prompts.title: AI Coach / Enablement Educator — Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Interactive 8-question interview that assesses a candidate's readiness to become an AI Coach who teaches teams to use AI tools productively, then delivers a tiered verdict, personalized roadmap, tailored resources, and a verification-first earning reality check.

prompts.title: AI Compliance Manager Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Run an 8-question structured interview to assess readiness for an AI Compliance Manager role, then deliver a tiered verdict, a phased roadmap, tailored resources, and a verify-first salary reality check.

prompts.title: AI Content Creator — Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Interactive 8-question interview that assesses a candidate's readiness for AI-assisted content creation work, then delivers a tiered verdict, personalized roadmap, tailored resources, and a verification-first earning reality check.

prompts.title: AI Conversation Designer — Role Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: An interactive 8-question interview that assesses readiness for an AI Conversation / UX Designer role and returns a tiered verdict, a personalized roadmap, tailored resources, and an honestly-labeled salary estimate.

prompts.title: AI Customer Success Manager — Role Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: An interactive 8-question interview that assesses readiness for an AI Customer Success Manager role and returns a tiered verdict, a personalized roadmap, tailored resources, and an honestly-labeled salary estimate.

prompts.title: AI Data Annotator / Trainer — Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Interactive 8-question interview that assesses a candidate's readiness for entry-level AI data annotation / AI trainer work, then delivers a tiered verdict, personalized roadmap, tailored resources, an advancement path, and a verification-first earning reality check.

prompts.title: AI Ethics Officer — Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Interactive 8-question interview that assesses a candidate's readiness for an AI Ethics & Governance role, then delivers a tiered verdict, personalized roadmap, tailored resources, and a verification-first salary reality check.

prompts.title: AI Governance Specialist Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Run an 8-question structured interview to assess readiness for an AI Governance Specialist role, then deliver a tiered verdict, a phased roadmap, tailored resources, and a verify-first salary reality check.

prompts.title: AI Product Manager Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Run an 8-question structured interview to assess readiness for an AI Product Manager role, then deliver a tiered verdict, a phased roadmap, tailored resources, and a verify-first salary reality check.

prompts.title: AI Prompt Engineer Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Run an 8-question structured interview to assess readiness for a Prompt Engineer role, then deliver a tiered verdict, a phased roadmap, tailored resources, and a verify-first earning reality check.

prompts.title: AI Research Scientist Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Run an 8-question structured interview to assess readiness for an AI Research Scientist role, then deliver a tiered verdict, a phased roadmap, tailored resources, and a verify-first salary reality check.

prompts.title: AI Strategist Role-Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: Run an 8-question structured interview to assess readiness for an AI Strategist role, then deliver a tiered verdict, a phased roadmap, tailored resources, and a verify-first salary reality check.

prompts.title: Computer Vision Engineer — Role Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: An interactive 8-question interview that assesses readiness for a Computer Vision Engineer role and returns a tiered verdict, a personalized roadmap, tailored resources, and an honestly-labeled salary estimate.

prompts.title: Deep Learning Engineer — Role Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: An interactive 8-question interview that assesses readiness for a Deep Learning Engineer role and returns a tiered verdict, a personalized roadmap, tailored resources, and an honestly-labeled salary estimate.

prompts.title: Machine Learning Engineer — Role Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: An interactive 8-question interview that assesses readiness for a Machine Learning Engineer role and returns a tiered verdict, a personalized roadmap, tailored resources, and an honestly-labeled salary estimate.

prompts.title: NLP Engineer — Role Readiness Assessment
prompts.description: An interactive 8-question interview that assesses readiness for a Natural Language Processing Engineer role and returns a tiered verdict, a personalized roadmap, tailored resources, and an honestly-labeled salary estimate.

prompts.title: Engineering Manager Stance for AI-Augmented Development
prompts.description: Reorients a developer from writing code to managing AI-generated output — defines the stance, the shifted time allocation, the new skills that matter, and the failure modes of clinging to the old identity.

prompts.title: Build a Concrete Plan to Make New Friends as an Adult
prompts.description: Turn 'I want more friends' into a working plan: identify venues that supply repeated proximity, pick the specific acquaintances worth converting, and script the exact low-stakes first invitations that move a stranger toward a friend.

prompts.title: Build a Durable Strategy for One Difficult Family Relationship
prompts.description: For one specific difficult family relationship, build a strategy you can sustain for years: classify the difficulty, decide what to stop trying to change, set the contact design and boundaries that protect you, and prepare for the predictable patterns — with abuse and safety routed out, not coached around.

prompts.title: Build a Plan to Cultivate and Maintain Personal Relationships
prompts.description: Design a realistic, low-guilt system for keeping personal relationships alive over time — inventory the people who matter, classify them by closeness and current health, set a sustainable contact cadence per tier, and turn 'I should reach out' into specific scheduled gestures. Distinct from professional networking.

prompts.title: Construct a Real Apology That Actually Lands
prompts.description: Build a genuine apology for one specific rupture: name the actual harm in the other person's terms, strip every 'if / but / because', and attach a concrete repair action — producing the exact words to say, stress-tested against the fake-apology patterns that make people feel worse.

prompts.title: Deepen One Pleasant-but-Shallow Friendship Without Forcing It
prompts.description: Take one specific friendship that is warm but stuck at surface level and move it toward depth through graduated self-disclosure and shared experience — matched to the other person's reciprocation so it deepens rather than lurches or scares them off.

prompts.title: Design a Deliberate-Practice Loop for One Social Skill
prompts.description: Pick one specific, observable social skill (starting conversations, listening without fixing, exiting gracefully, being warm with strangers, holding a silence) and build a deliberate-practice loop: a concrete behavioral definition, graduated low-stakes reps, an after-action review, and a way to tell real improvement from a lucky day.

prompts.title: Design and Rehearse a Boundary-Setting Conversation
prompts.description: Turn a vague resentment or recurring frustration into a clear, specific, deliverable boundary — with a script the user can actually say out loud, a plan for the predictable pushback, and a follow-through commitment that makes the boundary real rather than aspirational.

prompts.title: Diagnose the Type of Loneliness and Build a Targeted Connection Plan
prompts.description: Identify which kind of loneliness the user is actually experiencing — intimate, relational, or collective — because each has a different fix, then build a targeted plan matched to the diagnosed type, with clinical depression and situational grief routed out rather than mistaken for a social problem.

prompts.title: Lightweight Health-Check of a Personal Relationship
prompts.description: A quick, low-stakes health-check on a single personal relationship — what's working, what's draining, the give/take balance, and one small move to strengthen it. Designed for maintenance and early-signal catching, not for deciding whether to stay or leave (that's the decision-grade audit it cross-links to).

prompts.title: Prepare for a Hard Personal Conversation
prompts.description: Prepare for an emotionally difficult conversation with someone in your personal life — clarify the one outcome you actually want, separate facts from stories, draft a non-blaming opening, anticipate the other person's perspective, and plan how to stay regulated when it gets tense. Personal-relationship counterpart to the professional difficult-conversations prep.

prompts.title: Repair After a Rupture in a Personal Relationship
prompts.description: After a fight, a hurt, or a breach with someone you care about, structure a genuine repair: get clear on what actually happened and your part in it, decide what to own without over-apologizing or under-apologizing, draft a real repair attempt, and plan for the response you don't control — including when repair isn't currently possible.

prompts.title: Audit Where You Gain vs. Break Under Stress
prompts.description: Map a person's domains (work, finances, skills, relationships, health, identity) against how each responds to stress and volatility — fragile (breaks), robust (endures), or antifragile (gains) — and prescribe targeted moves to reduce fragility and add upside.

prompts.title: Build Tolerance for One Unresolved High-Uncertainty Situation
prompts.description: For a specific unresolved, high-stakes situation, sort the open questions into knowable-now, knowable-later, and unknowable, resolve what an action can resolve, define what stays controllable across outcomes, and park the rest with a concrete mechanism — building tolerance rather than forcing false certainty.

prompts.title: Build a Discipline System That Doesn't Rely on Willpower
prompts.description: Design a personal discipline system that produces consistent action through structure — defaults, friction, commitment devices, and feedback loops — rather than depending on daily willpower or motivation, which are unreliable inputs.

prompts.title: Diagnose Which Motivation Driver Is Missing
prompts.description: When motivation has dropped, classify which of four drivers — clarity, energy, reward, or identity — is actually missing, using a bounded taxonomy, so the user applies the matching fix instead of generic 'just be disciplined' advice.

prompts.title: Extract Signal From a Failure Without Toxic Positivity
prompts.description: Mine a specific failure for transferable lessons and accurate self-assessment, while refusing the two distortions — toxic positivity ('it was all a gift') and total self-condemnation ('I'm a failure') — that destroy the signal.

prompts.title: Process Harsh Criticism by Separating the Sting From the Signal
prompts.description: Take a piece of harsh criticism or feedback, split delivery from content, decompose it into discrete testable claims, verdict each against a fixed truth taxonomy weighted by source credibility, and decide the one change to make — or that none is warranted.

prompts.title: Re-Enter Life After a Low Period That Is Already Lifting
prompts.description: After a rough stretch where the user went quiet and pulled back — now beginning to lift — screen that it is genuinely lifting and non-clinical, restore the physical baseline first, then sequence gentle re-contact with what they withdrew from, one low-stakes reconnection at a time, with no catch-up heroics.

prompts.title: Rebuild Grounded Confidence After a Visible Failure Through Proof-Reps
prompts.description: After a visible failure has knocked out confidence, rebuild it on evidence rather than affirmations — bound the collapse to its domain, inventory disconfirming evidence, diagnose miscalibrated-low vs. accurately-lowered confidence, and design a graded sequence of real proof-reps.

prompts.title: Rebuild Momentum After a Long Stall
prompts.description: After a project or practice has been stalled for weeks or months, rebuild momentum through a deliberate re-entry ladder — restore-state, micro-win, cadence, and visible streak — instead of attempting a heroic relaunch that collapses within days.

prompts.title: Recover From a Specific Rejection Without Reading It as a Verdict
prompts.description: After a specific rejection (job, pitch, submission, relationship), separate the no from self-worth, classify what the rejection can and cannot tell you, extract only the real signal, and produce one re-entry action.

prompts.title: Structured Recovery After a Concrete Setback
prompts.description: After a specific setback or failure, run a bounded recovery sequence — stabilize, contain the damage, extract the controllable cause, and define one re-entry action — instead of either spiraling or rushing back in pretending nothing happened.

prompts.title: Counter the Motivation Drain of Working Alone
prompts.description: Diagnose which isolation deficit is draining a solo dev's motivation — no witnesses, no feedback, or invisible progress — then engineer the minimal matching structure of social contact, feedback loops, and visible progress into the coming week.

prompts.title: Design External Accountability When No One Is Watching
prompts.description: Diagnose which accountability mechanism actually moves this specific solo dev, then design one matched external system — commitment, witness, stakes, and cadence — with a kill condition so a dead system gets replaced, not endured.

prompts.title: Design a Sustainable Weekly Operating Pace for a One-Person Business
prompts.description: Proactively design a repeatable weekly cadence for a solo business — output rhythm, recovery, and a load ceiling matched to the user's real capacity — so throughput survives past the current sprint instead of spiking then crashing.

prompts.title: Make a Consequential Decision Without a Team to Bounce Off
prompts.description: Stress-test a solo dev's important decision by constructing a synthetic 'board' of named adversarial roles, forcing each to attack the plan, then converging on one call plus the reversal condition that would change it.

prompts.title: Set a Defensible Price Anchored to Value, Not Self-Doubt
prompts.description: Diagnose whether a solo dev's price is set from delivered-value evidence or from low confidence, then produce one defensible number, the evidence behind it, and a pre-committed raise trigger.

prompts.title: Audit Where Your Credit Leaks and Design Honest Visibility
prompts.description: For someone whose real contributions are invisible or under-credited, trace exactly where credit leaks in the work-to-recognition pipeline, then design specific visibility moves that make true work legible — without self-promotion theater or claiming others' work.

prompts.title: Build a Durable Cross-Team Alliance to Get Things Done Without Authority
prompts.description: Map the interests of a peer on another team whose cooperation you need but can't command, find the genuine overlap between their goals and yours, and design one low-cost reciprocal act that opens a durable working alliance rather than a one-off favor.

prompts.title: Build a Working Model of Your Manager and Adapt How You Surface Work
prompts.description: Construct an evidence-based model of your manager's priorities, pressures, communication style, and reward triggers from real observations, then produce one specific change to how you surface work — without becoming a sycophant or losing your own judgment.

prompts.title: Diagnose and Repair or Strengthen One Manager Relationship
prompts.description: Assess the current trust level in a specific manager relationship, locate the concrete misfires that eroded or capped it, and design one relationship-building move calibrated to the actual trust state — repair when broken, deepen when merely transactional.

prompts.title: Distinguish Mentors From Sponsors and Design the Ask
prompts.description: Separate the mentor role (advises you) from the sponsor role (spends capital on you), map which real people in your network could plausibly be which, then design one specific ask and the reciprocal value you offer in return.

prompts.title: Apply Two or Three Fitting Mental Models to a Problem You're Facing
prompts.description: Take one specific problem the user is stuck on, select the 2–3 mental models that genuinely fit its structure (not a grab-bag), run the problem through each to generate a non-obvious angle, and converge on the single insight that changes the user's next move.

prompts.title: Design a Personal Decision Journal That Calibrates Your Own Judgment
prompts.description: Build a lightweight decision-journal format the user will actually keep — capturing the decision, the predicted outcome, and a confidence number — and a review cadence that later scores those predictions so the user learns where their judgment is reliable and where it isn't.

prompts.title: Surface the Load-Bearing Assumptions Under a Plan or Belief, Then Test the Weakest
prompts.description: Extract the hidden assumptions holding up a plan or belief the user is acting on, rank them by how load-bearing and how uncertain each is, identify the one whose failure would collapse the plan, and decide what the user must verify before proceeding.

prompts.title: Policy Implementation Feasibility — Deep Assessment of Whether a Policy Can Actually Be Operated
prompts.description: Assess implementation feasibility for a policy proposal at depth: legal authority, administrative capacity, funding reality, realistic timeline benchmarked against comparable efforts, dependencies, implementation failure modes (gaming, capture, evasion, under-enforcement), and the gap between proxy 'implemented' and substantive implementation. Counters the failure of policies that are sound on paper and unoperatable in practice.

prompts.title: Policy Options Memo — Compare 3–5 Policy Options on Feasibility, Cost, Equity, and Political Viability
prompts.description: Structure a policy options memo that compares 3–5 distinct policy options against a defined problem. Each option is evaluated on effectiveness, implementation feasibility, fiscal cost, equity / distributional effects, political viability, reversibility, and unintended consequences. Includes a recommendation with explicit naming of the values tradeoffs the recommendation rests on.

prompts.title: Policy Problem Framing — Define the Problem Before Generating Options
prompts.description: Frame a policy problem before anyone proposes solutions. Forces specification of who is affected (with magnitude), the measured current state, the no-action trajectory, the contested framings held by different stakeholders, root causes versus symptoms, what has already been tried, and the policy window. Counters the most common upstream failure: solving a misframed problem efficiently. Pre-condition for policy_options_memo.md.

prompts.title: Policy Stakeholder & Coalition Map — Positions, Blockers, and Swing Actors
prompts.description: Map every stakeholder around a policy proposal on position, intensity, influence, true interests, coalition affiliation, and movability — then derive the structures that determine outcomes: coalitions (who moves together), blockers (high influence + opposed), and swing actors (low intensity + medium-to-high influence, where coalition-building leverage actually lives). Counters the failure of counting headcount instead of weighing power and persuadability.
