prompts.title: Voice Clone Profile Builder
prompts.description: Analyze writing samples to build a comprehensive, reusable voice profile that enables AI to generate content authentically matching a person's writing style, tone, and rhetorical patterns

prompts.title: Content Research for Writing
prompts.description: Research a topic to prepare for writing an article, presentation, or report — gathering source-cited statistics, expert perspectives, examples, and counter-arguments, with credibility assessment and strict separation of evidence from inference.

prompts.title: Narrative Arc Builder — Three-Act Structure from a One-Line Thesis or Core Idea
prompts.description: Build a three-act narrative arc (setup / tension / resolution) from a one-line thesis or core idea, naming the central change and the through-line. Includes named application sections for general essay, product pitch, launch story, and internal memo. The canonical narrative-arc prompt for the repository.

prompts.title: Original-Expression Rewriter — Re-express Source Text in Your Own Words While Preserving Facts and Meaning
prompts.description: Rewrite a nonfiction source passage into genuinely original expression that conveys the same facts, meaning, and level of certainty — reducing copied wording and structure while preserving truthfulness. Produces a rewrite, a fidelity check, and a copying-risk audit that flags anything better handled by quotation or attribution.

prompts.title: Precision Document Edit — Tighten Prose for Clarity and Argument Strength While Preserving Voice
prompts.description: Edit a prose passage for clarity, concision, and argument strength while preserving the author's voice and meaning. Produces a markup view with reasons, a clean rewrite, and a voice-and-meaning self-audit.

prompts.title: Thesis Builder — Surface the Stakes and Forge a Defensible Essay Thesis
prompts.description: Surface the stakes underlying a loose idea, then craft graded thesis options (safe / sharp / boldest) each with three supporting sub-claims and the strongest counter-argument it must survive, plus the trade-off of each option.

prompts.title: UX Copy Tone Swap — Rewrite a UI Snippet in Three Brand Tones with Clarity and Accessibility Flags
prompts.description: Rewrite a UI-copy snippet (button, error, empty-state, onboarding line, etc.) in three distinct brand tones, justify each choice against the moment and audience, and flag any tone that risks clarity or accessibility. The canonical tone-swap prompt for the repository.

prompts.title: Unsourced-Claim Disposition — Decide KEEP / SOFTEN / REFRAME / QUOTE / CUT for Claims You Know But Can't Cite
prompts.description: For each factual claim a nonfiction author asserts from experience but has no source for, decide the honest disposition: keep it (a source was found), soften its certainty to match the evidence, reframe it as labeled professional judgment, quote-and-attribute it, or cut it. Prevents tacit expertise from being published as if it were established, cited fact.

prompts.title: Voice Print Extractor — Build a Reusable Voice Spec from a Writing Sample
prompts.description: Analyze a 500+ word writing sample to extract a compact, reusable 'voice print': sentence-length distribution, cadence, signature rhetorical moves, diction tier, punctuation habits, and 3–5 do/don't steering rules to paste into future prompts.

prompts.title: Decide Whether to Treat AI as Tool or Colleague for a Task
prompts.description: Classifies a specific task as better suited to tool-mode AI (fast, scoped, high-oversight, low-context) vs. colleague-mode AI (slower, higher-autonomy, needs context, produces work you'd review like a junior teammate's) so you pick the right mode before wasting a cycle.

prompts.title: High-Grade Intent Specification for a Delegation
prompts.description: Converts a one-line delegation request into a full intent specification that a delegated agent or teammate can execute without you — outcome, scope, out-of-scope, constraints, deliverables, success criteria, and decision rights.

prompts.title: Role-Based Delegation Plan (Who Does What, When)
prompts.description: Turns a task into a role-based plan — which parts a human does, which parts AI does, which parts require handoff between the two, and the timing of each — so nothing falls between roles and no role is over-loaded.

prompts.title: Verification Plan for Delegated Work
prompts.description: Designs a right-sized verification plan for work you delegated — what to spot-check, what to deep-check, what to accept, and how to catch the failure modes most common to the task type, without re-doing the work yourself.

prompts.title: Define Agent Authority Boundaries
prompts.description: Specify what an agent can do autonomously, what requires confirmation, and what is forbidden — as enforceable prompt rules, not aspirational language.

prompts.title: Design Agent Loop Termination Conditions
prompts.description: Define explicit, falsifiable termination conditions for an agent's main loop so it stops cleanly on success, failure, or budget exhaustion.

prompts.title: Generate a Brief for a Subagent
prompts.description: Author a self-contained brief that a sub-agent can run without seeing the parent's context, with explicit scope, return contract, and authority limits.

prompts.title: Human-in-the-Loop Handoff
prompts.description: Define when and how an agent pauses to request human input, with the format of the request and the resume protocol.

prompts.title: Idempotency Rules for Agents With Side Effects
prompts.description: Prevent duplicate side effects on retry by giving the agent rules for checking, recording, and gating actions with idempotency keys.

prompts.title: Make an Agent Trace-Friendly
prompts.description: Add prompt rules so the agent emits structured trace events around decisions, tool calls, and errors, enabling observability without log scraping.

prompts.title: Planner / Worker / Judge Three-Prompt Pattern
prompts.description: Author three prompts that form a planner-worker-judge cycle, with strict input/output contracts and a maximum revision loop.

prompts.title: Progress Report Format for Long-Running Agents
prompts.description: Define a concise structured progress report an agent emits at intervals so users and orchestrators can track without reading the full trace.

prompts.title: Self-Correction Loop for Agents
prompts.description: Wrap an agent step with detect-error → diagnose → repair logic so transient or schema errors are recovered without escalating.

prompts.title: State Summary for Context Compaction
prompts.description: Produce a compact, lossless-where-possible state summary the agent can resume from after context compaction.

prompts.title: Decide Whether to Downsize the Model
prompts.description: Diagnose whether a smaller model can serve the same prompt acceptably, with measurement-based gates and a fallback escalation rule.

prompts.title: Lossless Compression Rewrite
prompts.description: Rewrite a prompt to reduce tokens while preserving identical behavior on the regression set.

prompts.title: Lossy Compression Inside a Quality Tolerance
prompts.description: Compress a prompt past lossless, accepting bounded behavior changes that pass a tolerance check on the test set.

prompts.title: Make the System Prompt Skinnier
prompts.description: Move rules from the system prompt into just-in-time instructions, examples, or developer prompts when they are not universally needed.

prompts.title: Prune Few-Shot Examples for Token Savings
prompts.description: Remove few-shot examples that do not contribute unique signal, validated by per-example ablation against the test set.

prompts.title: Redesign a Prompt for Streaming Latency
prompts.description: Reorder the output schema so the most useful content streams first, reducing time-to-useful-token without reducing quality.

prompts.title: Restructure for Prompt-Cache Hits
prompts.description: Reorder a prompt so the longest stable prefix is at the front, maximizing cache hit length and amortizing token cost.

prompts.title: Token Audit of an Existing Prompt
prompts.description: Find the highest-cost low-value sections of a prompt and rank them for compression based on observed token weight.

prompts.title: Bisect Prompt Changes (Git-Bisect for Prompts)
prompts.description: Run a git-bisect-style binary search over a sequence of prompt revisions to find the single change that introduced a regression.

prompts.title: First-Failure Cause Isolator
prompts.description: Given a bad output, name the single primary cause from a fixed taxonomy and emit one corrective edit.

prompts.title: Input Perturbation Battery
prompts.description: Apply a fixed battery of small input perturbations (case, whitespace, length, delimiters) to surface brittleness.

prompts.title: Minimal Reproducer Isolator for Prompt Failures
prompts.description: Reduce a failing prompt + input pair to the smallest reproducer that still triggers the failure.

prompts.title: Multi-Turn Drift Diagnosis
prompts.description: Locate the turn at which a long conversation's behavior degraded (style drift, rule abandonment, persona slip, format loss).

prompts.title: Prompt Failure Mode Taxonomy Classifier
prompts.description: Classify a failed model output into one of seven failure modes from a fixed taxonomy and emit the recommended next debug step.

prompts.title: Silent Failure Detector
prompts.description: Detect outputs that look fluent and well-formed but are wrong — where surface validators pass and only deeper checks fail.

prompts.title: Temperature Sensitivity Probe
prompts.description: Run a fixed prompt at temperatures 0.0, 0.3, 0.7, 1.0 to determine whether a failure is deterministic, variance-driven, or temperature-cliff.

prompts.title: Bootstrap a Personal Instruction File from Observed Preferences
prompts.description: Build a first-draft personal instruction file (CLAUDE.md, custom-instructions block, or equivalent) from evidence — corrections the user has accumulated, rules they've compounded in-session, maps of model defaults they've pushed against — instead of from a blank page full of aspirational preferences.

prompts.title: Compound Corrections Across a Session So Preferences Stick
prompts.description: Turn a stream of ad-hoc corrections the user has made to a model during a working session into a compact, ordered rule set that makes those corrections stick — for the rest of the session and, optionally, for future sessions — so the user stops re-correcting the same defaults.

prompts.title: Map the Model's Default Position on a Topic
prompts.description: Before asking a model for analysis, opinion, or recommendation on a topic, probe and map its default position — what it would say unprompted, which views it balances against each other, what it hedges on — so you can push it off the median toward the specific view you actually want.

prompts.title: Sharpen an Instruction So the Model Cannot Default to the Median
prompts.description: Rewrite a vague instruction into a version the model cannot satisfy by producing average output — adding the user's prior, the views to suppress, the hedge phrases to forbid, the specific form the answer must take, and the test the output must pass.

prompts.title: Audit an Existing Prompt for Specification Gaps
prompts.description: Audit a prompt the user is already running in the wild against a specification-coverage checklist. Surfaces the unstated assumptions, undefined success criteria, ambiguous audience, and missing refusal conditions that let the model wander. Returns a ranked list of gaps, evidence from real outputs, and the specific prompt edits that would close each gap.

prompts.title: Build Personal 'Taste' for AI Output Quality Through Calibrated Comparison
prompts.description: A structured practice for developing reliable intuition about AI output quality on a recurring task type: blind-score 10–20 outputs against a spec, compare personal scores to the spec's objective score, find where intuition and spec disagree, and correct the mismatch by updating either the spec or the intuition. Builds taste that is calibrated, not just confident.

prompts.title: Config-Sweep Stress Harness
prompts.description: Design a pre-production stress test that varies runtime configuration — temperature, model version, context length, and concurrency/load — rather than inputs, holding a fixed challenge set constant, to surface config-sensitivity, latency cliffs, and token-cost spikes before production does. Distinct from adversarial testing (varies the input) and model robustness testing (perturbs the model or data): this varies the deployment knobs an ops team actually turns.

prompts.title: Decompose a Task Across Orthogonal AI-Difficulty Axes
prompts.description: Given a candidate task for AI, score it across orthogonal axes that actually predict AI difficulty — specification clarity, context payload, tool availability, reversibility, stakes, verification cost, ambiguity of correctness, and horizon — so the user can decide whether the task is AI-shaped, and if so, which axis is the bottleneck.

prompts.title: Design an Evaluation Set for Correctness
prompts.description: Design a production-scale evaluation set for an AI task: case coverage by category, a rubric that imports the correctness spec, a scoring protocol that two graders can apply consistently, thresholds that separate signal from noise, and an operating cadence. Output is a runnable eval, not a slideware plan. Distinct from a personal eval harness — this is for tasks where the eval itself must be auditable and rerunnable by a team.

prompts.title: Discover What 'Correct' Actually Means for a Fuzzy Request
prompts.description: Pin down an operational definition of correctness for a task the user describes loosely. Returns a correctness spec — named consumer, observable must-haves, must-nots, refusal conditions, tiebreakers — grounded in real examples the user has judged rather than in abstract quality heuristics. The output is the input to specification, evaluation, and audit prompts.

prompts.title: Force Tradeoff Clarity on Competing Quality Dimensions
prompts.description: Take a task whose quality dimensions pull against each other (brevity vs. completeness, caution vs. decisiveness, precision vs. coverage, refusal vs. best-effort) and force the user to commit to a dominance order with evidence-backed tiebreakers. Returns a tradeoff policy the downstream prompt, eval, and audit can enforce consistently.

prompts.title: Optimize a Workflow Based on Which AI-Difficulty Axes Are Hardest
prompts.description: Takes a multi-step workflow the user is running with AI and redesigns it to reduce the total difficulty along its hardest axes — moving steps, changing human-AI hand-offs, adding verification points, splitting steps, or rerouting entirely. The goal is not to 'reduce difficulty' in general but to target the specific axis that's dragging the workflow.

prompts.title: Production Monitoring for Output Correctness Drift
prompts.description: Design monitoring that catches correctness drift in a live AI system — signals grounded in the user's actual telemetry, alert thresholds that separate drift from noise, sampling strategies that keep costs tractable, and a response playbook that names who acts on what. Distinct from a pre-ship eval: monitoring runs continuously against production traffic that the eval never saw.

prompts.title: Prompt Lifecycle Assessment
prompts.description: This prompt helps diagnose your operational maturity in prompt engineering, identifies specific stage-failures, and recommends tools to level up your workflow. Based on a 6-stage lifecycle framework.

prompts.title: Repository Review & Reflection Prompt
prompts.description: A comprehensive self-reflective analysis prompt for AI agents to evaluate the Prompting-Guides repository. Use this prompt to identify improvements, gaps, inconsistencies, and opportunities across the repository's 1200+ prompts and extensive coding agent resources.

prompts.title: Run a Pre-Mortem on Correctness Before Shipping
prompts.description: Imagine the prompt or system has shipped and is producing wrong outputs three months later. Walk the user backward from plausible failure modes to the spec, prompt, or monitoring gap that would have let each failure through. Returns a ranked list of likely failures with preventive edits and detection signals, grounded in the user's actual deployment context rather than generic AI-risk catalogs.

prompts.title: Translate Vague Requirements into Testable Specifications
prompts.description: Take a requirement phrased as a quality adjective ('more professional,' 'cleaner,' 'better reasoning,' 'more rigorous') and translate it into observable, testable behaviors with pass/fail examples drawn from the user's real outputs. Returns a spec fragment that replaces the adjective with criteria a downstream prompt, rubric, or audit can enforce.

prompts.title: Data Exfiltration Probe Set
prompts.description: Generate probes that attempt to extract a model's system prompt, internal context, or user data using six extraction strategies, each with a binary pass/fail test rule.

prompts.title: Edge Case Generator
prompts.description: Produce edge inputs from a task specification across boundary, malformed, and hostile axes for exhaustive input-coverage testing.

prompts.title: Jailbreak Corpus Builder
prompts.description: Assemble a categorized jailbreak test corpus with taxonomy, severity, and reproduction metadata for evaluating system-prompt robustness.

prompts.title: Persona Attack Battery
prompts.description: Generate a graded battery of role-play and identity-override attempts against a system prompt's persona and behavioral constraints, ordered by bypass sophistication.

prompts.title: Prompt Injection Test Set
prompts.description: Generate direct and indirect prompt injection cases for tool-calling agents, RAG pipelines, and multi-turn systems with injection vector, target, and containment verification.

prompts.title: Refusal Bypass Audit
prompts.description: Generate a graded ladder of phrasings targeting a specific refusal policy, ordered by bypass sophistication, to identify whether the refusal is robust or brittle.

prompts.title: Case Inventory from Production Logs
prompts.description: Mine production logs into a structured eval test set with extraction filters, deduplication, labeling, and anonymization steps.

prompts.title: Dataset Difficulty Stratifier
prompts.description: Score and stratify eval cases by difficulty across orthogonal axes, producing a balanced distribution and identifying which strata reveal the most about model capability gaps.

prompts.title: Holdout Split Designer
prompts.description: Design train/dev/test splits that prevent data leakage, with split ratios, stratification criteria, leakage audit, and a documented rationale for each design decision.

prompts.title: Synthetic Case Generator
prompts.description: Generate synthetic eval cases with axis-based coverage guarantees and quality validation, to supplement or replace real log data when coverage gaps exist.

prompts.title: A/B Test Runner Design
prompts.description: Design a rigorous A/B experiment over two prompt variants: hypothesis, primary metric, sample size, blinding protocol, scoring rubric, and a pre-committed decision rule.

prompts.title: Canary Set Designer
prompts.description: Design a small, fast-running canary test set (5–15 cases) that catches major regressions early, with run-time targets, sensitivity requirements, and triage protocol.

prompts.title: Change Impact Estimator
prompts.description: Predict which test cases a specific prompt change is likely to affect before running them, to prioritize test execution and reduce evaluation cost.

prompts.title: Golden Set Curator
prompts.description: Build and maintain a stable golden test set with provenance tracking, freeze protocol, and update criteria for long-term regression testing.

prompts.title: Release-Gate Scorecard
prompts.description: Turn eval and stress-sweep results into a merge decision: compare a candidate run against a frozen baseline, compute per-metric deltas against noise floors, assign a traffic-light status to each metric, hard-fail on blocker thresholds, and emit a PR-ready scorecard comment. This is the 'analyse and gate releases' artifact — the thing that actually blocks or clears a prompt/model change.

prompts.title: Calibrated Rubric Anchors
prompts.description: Create concrete output examples that anchor each score point (1–5) on a rubric dimension, ensuring scorers apply scores consistently and reducing inter-rater variance.

prompts.title: Inter-Rater Agreement Protocol
prompts.description: Measure and improve agreement across human or LLM judges using kappa-based metrics, calibration sessions, disagreement diagnosis, and a documented remediation plan.

prompts.title: LLM Judge Designer
prompts.description: Design an LLM-as-judge prompt with role, rubric, chain-of-thought structure, bias controls, and a verification protocol that checks for positional, length, and self-preference bias.

prompts.title: Pairwise vs. Pointwise Scoring Decision
prompts.description: Decide between pairwise (A vs. B preference) and pointwise (absolute score) rubric modes for a specific evaluation task, then design whichever mode is selected.

prompts.title: Audit Few-Shot Examples for Contamination and Overfit
prompts.description: Detect when few-shot examples are causing the prompt to overfit to surface features that do not generalize.

prompts.title: Build an Edge-Case Few-Shot Pack
prompts.description: Curate few-shot examples that cover edge cases (boundary inputs, malformed inputs, refusal-worthy inputs) instead of typical inputs.

prompts.title: Decide When to Add a Few-Shot Example
prompts.description: Diagnose whether a task needs zero, one, or several few-shot examples, and which to add first if any.

prompts.title: Design Negative Few-Shot Examples
prompts.description: Create examples that show what the model should not do, formatted so the model does not imitate them by accident.

prompts.title: Generate Synthetic Few-Shot Examples
prompts.description: Build few-shot examples when no corpus exists, with explicit diversity targets and a quality gate.

prompts.title: Normalize the Format of Few-Shot Examples
prompts.description: Make every few-shot example share input shape, output shape, and delimiter conventions so the model imitates structure, not noise.

prompts.title: Order Few-Shot Examples
prompts.description: Decide the order in which few-shot examples appear, considering recency bias, difficulty progression, and primacy/recency effects.

prompts.title: Select Few-Shot Examples From a Corpus
prompts.description: Pick a small representative set of few-shot examples from a larger corpus, balancing coverage, diversity, difficulty, and prompt budget.

prompts.title: Diagnostic for Whether the 'Right Problem' Is Being Solved
prompts.description: Before writing a prompt or delegating a task to AI, verify that the problem the user is about to solve is the problem actually worth solving — separating the stated task from the underlying intent, surfacing assumptions about why it matters, and testing whether solving it as stated will deliver the outcome the user expects.

prompts.title: Map a Team's Current AI Use Against Misalignment Risk
prompts.description: Produce a team-level map of how AI is currently being used — by whom, for what, with what stakes and verification — and identify the specific workflows where the gap between stated goals and how the model is actually being asked to behave is large enough to create real risk.

prompts.title: Workshop for Building Constraints, Escalation Triggers, and a Value Hierarchy for Any AI Task
prompts.description: Structured session that produces three artifacts for an AI task before the model runs: the constraints the output must respect, the triggers that escalate the task out of AI back to a human, and the value hierarchy that tells the model which goal wins when goals conflict — so the user doesn't discover missing constraints in review.

prompts.title: Calibrated Uncertainty — Emit Confidence with a Calibration Rubric
prompts.description: Force the model to attach a confidence value to each claim using a fixed verbal-numeric rubric tied to evidence strength, with calibration test cases.

prompts.title: Citation-Required Pattern — Every Claim Needs a Source Token
prompts.description: Enforce a strict per-claim citation rule with a source-token format, post-hoc validator, and rejection action for unattributed claims.

prompts.title: Grounding-Only Pattern — Refuse Beyond Evidence
prompts.description: System-prompt pattern that bans any claim not present in supplied evidence and provides the exact refusal text the model must emit when asked to go beyond it.

prompts.title: Invented-Entity Audit — Find Made-Up Names, IDs, and References
prompts.description: Scan a model output for entities, identifiers, and references that do not exist in supplied evidence and tag each as invented, paraphrased, or grounded.

prompts.title: Known/Unknown Separator — Split Confident Facts From Guesses
prompts.description: Force the model to physically segregate verified claims from inferred or guessed claims into two output blocks, so downstream consumers can act on them differently.

prompts.title: Pre-Mortem for a Factual Task — Anticipate Fabrication Classes
prompts.description: Before generation, enumerate the specific fabrication classes the task is most exposed to and pick a guard for each — converting risk into prompt structure.

prompts.title: Self-Consistency Check — Sample N, Flag Disagreeing Claims
prompts.description: Generate the response N times under varied seeds or temperature, decompose each into atomic claims, and flag claims that do not agree across samples.

prompts.title: Temporal Anchoring — Pin Claims to Cutoff and Provided Dates
prompts.description: Force the model to declare its knowledge cutoff, the reference date for the current task, and tag every time-sensitive claim with its temporal anchor.

prompts.title: Compaction Techniques for Long Prompts
prompts.description: Cut a long prompt's length by ~50% while preserving every constraint, using a fixed catalogue of compaction techniques.

prompts.title: Imperative vs Declarative Instruction Converter
prompts.description: Decide whether each rule should be an imperative ('Do X') or a declarative spec ('Output is X'), and convert it into the better form.

prompts.title: Instruction Anchor Phrase Library Builder
prompts.description: Build a per-model-family library of empirically reliable anchor phrases (the wordings that change behavior most reliably for that family).

prompts.title: Instruction Conflict Taxonomy
prompts.description: Classify any pair of conflicting instructions in a prompt into one of four named conflict types and emit a resolution path.

prompts.title: Instruction Hierarchy Designer
prompts.description: Design and encode a system > developer > user precedence layer inside a prompt so the model resolves conflicts deterministically.

prompts.title: Instruction Negation Audit
prompts.description: Find every 'do not X' rule in a prompt that risks priming the model toward X, and rewrite it into a positive-form replacement.

prompts.title: Instruction Precedence Test Set Generator
prompts.description: Generate an adversarial test set that proves whether the model honors a stated SYSTEM > DEVELOPER > USER hierarchy.

prompts.title: MUST / SHOULD / MAY Classifier (RFC-2119 for Prompts)
prompts.description: Apply RFC-2119-style normative ranking (MUST / SHOULD / MAY) to a flat list of prompt rules so the model and reviewers share a precedence vocabulary.

prompts.title: Active Coaching Inside a Running Conversation to Correct Behavior
prompts.description: Mid-conversation coaching pattern that corrects a model's behavior in the current session without starting over — name the specific deviation, supply the rule that replaces the default, check adherence, and capture what should move into the system prompt for next time.

prompts.title: Build a System Prompt from Scratch Aligned with Constitutional Principles
prompts.description: Structured design session for authoring a new system prompt that cooperates with the target model's base training — starting from the task, deriving the principles that should govern it, translating them into operational rules the model can check itself against, and locking them in an ordered format the model won't average over.

prompts.title: Diagnose Why a Model's Behavior Deviates from Instructions
prompts.description: Root-cause analysis for why a specific model (Claude, GPT, Gemini) is failing to follow a specific instruction in a specific prompt — locating the deviation in the prompt, the model's base training, the context, or the interaction pattern rather than guessing.

prompts.title: Refactor a System Prompt to Align with the Model's Base Constitution
prompts.description: Take an existing system prompt that is fighting the model's base training and refactor it so instructions cooperate with — rather than contradict — the model's built-in tendencies, keeping the original intent but removing instructions that the model will either resist or over-comply with.

prompts.title: Build a Quirks Catalog for a Model
prompts.description: Catalog observed model-specific behaviors (quirks, tics, biases) with reproductions and recommended prompt-side mitigations.

prompts.title: Claude-Specific Prompting Patterns
prompts.description: Apply Claude-specific patterns (XML tags, prefill, system message conventions, extended thinking) to a prompt for measurable behavior improvements.

prompts.title: GPT-Specific Prompting Patterns
prompts.description: Apply OpenAI / GPT-family conventions (system messages, JSON mode, structured outputs, function calling) to a prompt with measurable behavior changes.

prompts.title: Haiku-Class Model Constraints and Patterns
prompts.description: Adapt prompts to small/fast models (Haiku, mini, flash) by simplifying instructions, reducing reasoning, and tightening schemas.

prompts.title: Migrate a Prompt Across Model Families
prompts.description: Translate a prompt between Claude, GPT, Gemini, or open-source families with explicit substitutions for each family's idioms.

prompts.title: Migrate a Prompt Within a Model Family
prompts.description: Move a prompt from one model version to its successor (e.g., Sonnet 4.6 → 4.7) by checking deprecated patterns, new capabilities, and behavior diffs.

prompts.title: Patterns for Thinking-Mode (Reasoning) Models
prompts.description: Adapt a prompt for reasoning-mode models (Claude extended thinking, o-series) by simplifying instructions, removing CoT scaffolding, and tuning thinking budget.

prompts.title: Probe a New Model's Capabilities
prompts.description: Run a structured capability probe against a new model: instruction following, format adherence, tool use, refusal style, reasoning, and length control.

prompts.title: Replace a Retired Model
prompts.description: Plan and execute the replacement of a retired model with a successor or alternative, including compatibility checks, prompt edits, and rollback.

prompts.title: Test a Prompt's Portability Across Models
prompts.description: Run a portability check that scores a prompt's behavior consistency across multiple models and identifies the patterns causing divergence.

prompts.title: Email / Doc / Chat Format Variants
prompts.description: Generate three format-appropriate shapes of the same content from a single prompt: email, document, and chat message.

prompts.title: Length Budget Designer
prompts.description: Define hard caps on words, tokens, and section counts with an enforcement method for each cap.

prompts.title: Markdown Contract
prompts.description: Define exact heading depth, list style, code-fence language tags, and bold/italic usage in a copy-paste system prompt block.

prompts.title: No Preamble / No Postamble
prompts.description: Eliminate opener affirmations and sign-off lines from AI responses with a system prompt block and detection patterns.

prompts.title: One-Sentence Answer Pattern
prompts.description: Enforce extreme brevity: one sentence for answerable questions, with a defined fallback structure when one sentence is impossible.

prompts.title: Quoting and Attribution Rules
prompts.description: Define verbatim vs. paraphrase quoting conventions, attribution format, and fidelity requirements for a specific output context.

prompts.title: Streaming-Friendly Output Design
prompts.description: Structure prompt output so the first 50 tokens are maximally useful when displayed incrementally in a streaming UI.

prompts.title: Table Design Prompt
prompts.description: Choose columns, sort order, and alignment for a table; decide when a table beats a list.

prompts.title: Build Input Validation Into a Prompt
prompts.description: Add an input-validation preamble that rejects malformed input with a structured error before any task work happens.

prompts.title: Build a Meta-Prompt That Emits Prompts
prompts.description: Author a meta-prompt whose output is itself a prompt, with strict structural constraints and a self-check pass.

prompts.title: Build a Prompt Pack for a Role
prompts.description: Produce a coherent set of 5–12 prompts for a single role (e.g. CSM, sales rep, recruiter) that share voice, schema, and naming.

prompts.title: Build a Prompt Using the Constraint-First Pattern
prompts.description: Author a prompt by enumerating Must / Must Not rules first, then deriving role, task, and output format from the constraint set.

prompts.title: Build a Prompt Using the Role-First Pattern
prompts.description: Author a prompt that opens with a tightly bounded role, then derives task, constraints, and format consistent with that role.

prompts.title: Build a Task Prompt From a Blank Page
prompts.description: Structured intake that converts a fuzzy goal into a first-draft, production-shaped task prompt with role, inputs, constraints, output contract, and verification.

prompts.title: Decide What Belongs in System vs User Prompt
prompts.description: Classify each rule, fact, and instruction into system, developer, or user role based on stability, sensitivity, and override behavior.

prompts.title: Decide What the Prompt Assumes When Input Is Silent
prompts.description: Define explicit default values and silence-handling rules for every optional input so behavior is predictable.

prompts.title: Design a Clarification-Before-Answer Prompt
prompts.description: Author a prompt that asks targeted questions before producing output, with budget caps and a fallback when the user refuses.

prompts.title: Design a Multi-Call Prompt Chain
prompts.description: Decompose a task into a chain of prompts with explicit handoff contracts, intermediate validation, and failure routing.

prompts.title: Design a Progressive-Disclosure Prompt
prompts.description: Build a prompt that opens minimal, expands on signal, and only loads detailed instructions when triggers fire.

prompts.title: Design a Reusable User-Prompt Template
prompts.description: Convert one-off prompts into a parameterized template with named variables, a sample fill, and a fill-validator.

prompts.title: Design the Negative Half of a Prompt
prompts.description: Produce a ranked, falsifiable Must-Not list derived from real rejected outputs and known failure patterns.

prompts.title: Induce a Prompt From Accepted Outputs
prompts.description: Reverse-engineer a prompt from 5+ accepted outputs by extracting shared structure, vocabulary, and constraints, then writing rules that produce them.

prompts.title: Produce Terse and Verbose Variants of the Same Prompt
prompts.description: Author two variants of a prompt — minimal and full — that produce equivalent outputs and let callers pick by latency or cost budget.

prompts.title: Skeleton-First Prompt Authoring
prompts.description: Lock the section structure of a prompt before writing content, then fill each slot with content derived from inputs.

prompts.title: Audit a Prompt for Brittleness
prompts.description: Identify rules in a prompt that pass on the happy path but break on edge cases, and propose hardening for each.

prompts.title: Eliminate Redundancy in a Prompt
prompts.description: Find duplicated instructions in a prompt, classify each as harmless / redundant / conflicting, and consolidate without losing intent.

prompts.title: Engineering Prompt Improver
prompts.description: Transform a vague engineering-focused prompt into a specific, well-structured one — diagnosing clarity/structure/specification gaps, applying an enhancement framework, and producing an improved prompt with explained changes, platform tips, and a verification test.

prompts.title: Explain a Prompt Diff
prompts.description: Take a before/after prompt diff and produce a structured explanation of what changed, why each change matters, and what risks each introduces.

prompts.title: Idempotent Rewrite: Improve Readability Without Changing Behavior
prompts.description: Rewrite a prompt for clarity and structure while preserving identical behavior on a regression set.

prompts.title: Minimal-Change Pass: Fix One Failure Without Regressing Others
prompts.description: Diagnose a specific failure in a prompt and propose the smallest possible change that fixes it while passing a regression set.

prompts.title: Modernize a Legacy Prompt
prompts.description: Update a prompt written for older models or older conventions to current best practice without changing intent.

prompts.title: Promote a Prompt From Prototype to Production
prompts.description: Run a prototype prompt through a fixed promotion checklist that adds validation, monitoring hooks, and refusal handling.

prompts.title: Repair the Prompt From a Bad Output
prompts.description: Given one specific bad output and the prompt that produced it, diagnose which part of the prompt failed and propose the smallest repair.

prompts.title: Resolve Conflicting Rules in a Prompt
prompts.description: Find pairs of rules that contradict, classify the conflict type, and propose a resolution that preserves the dominant intent.

prompts.title: Restack a Flat Rule List Into Layered Constraint Architecture
prompts.description: Take a flat list of `Must` / `Must Not` rules and reorganize into layered architecture (safety, scope, content, format, style) with explicit precedence.

prompts.title: Specificity Pass on an Existing Prompt
prompts.description: Identify vague verbs, abstract nouns, and unmeasurable adjectives in a prompt and replace them with operational language.

prompts.title: Prompt Optimization and Engineering
prompts.description: Systematically optimize prompts for accuracy, consistency, cost-efficiency, and maintainability through structured testing and iteration.

prompts.title: Clean Refusal When Retrieved Context Is Insufficient
prompts.description: Force the model to emit a structured 'no answer' response — naming what's missing and what was searched — instead of confabulating when retrieved passages do not support the question.

prompts.title: Compress Retrieved Passages Before Stuffing
prompts.description: Reduce retrieved chunks to question-conditioned, citation-preserving summaries that fit a token budget without dropping facts the answer will depend on.

prompts.title: Design a Citation Format for RAG Output
prompts.description: Pick and specify a citation format — inline, footnote, hover-token, per-claim or per-paragraph — given the rendering surface, audience, and verifier path.

prompts.title: Evaluation Harness for RAG Groundedness, Relevance, and Context Precision
prompts.description: Specify a test harness that scores a RAG system on faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision, and context recall — with judge prompts, datasets, and pass thresholds.

prompts.title: Follow-up Question Handler — Re-retrieve or Reuse Prior Context
prompts.description: Decision rule for whether a follow-up turn should reuse the prior turn's retrieved passages, re-retrieve with a rewritten query, or both.

prompts.title: Freshness-Aware RAG Prompt for Time-Sensitive Claims
prompts.description: Force the model to attach passage dates to claims, downgrade or refuse on stale evidence, and distinguish 'as of' answers from 'current' answers.

prompts.title: Multi-Query Expansion for Recall
prompts.description: Generate N diverse query variants from one user question to maximize the probability the relevant passage appears in the merged top-K across runs.

prompts.title: RAG Grounding Contract — Answer Only From Retrieved Passages
prompts.description: System-prompt contract that constrains the model to answer only from supplied passages, attach span IDs to every claim, and refuse when evidence is absent.

prompts.title: Resolve Conflicts Across Retrieved Sources
prompts.description: Decision rules for the model when retrieved passages disagree — apply authority, recency, specificity, or surface the conflict explicitly rather than silently picking one side.

prompts.title: Rewrite a User Question into a Retrieval-Friendly Query
prompts.description: Convert a raw user question into one or more queries optimized for vector / BM25 / hybrid retrieval, using HyDE, decomposition, and term expansion as the situation requires.

prompts.title: Decide Whether to Use Chain-of-Thought
prompts.description: Diagnose whether a task benefits from explicit reasoning steps or whether direct-answer mode performs better.

prompts.title: Decompose a Task Into Ordered Subtasks
prompts.description: Author a prompt that explicitly splits a task into ordered subtasks the model executes in sequence with intermediate outputs.

prompts.title: Design a Structured Scratchpad
prompts.description: Add a bounded scratchpad to a prompt so the model can think out loud in a fixed structure before producing the final answer.

prompts.title: Explanation-Then-Answer Split for Auditable Outputs
prompts.description: Produce an answer plus a separate, parseable explanation block when both are needed by different consumers (UI vs API vs reviewer).

prompts.title: Plan-Then-Execute Split
prompts.description: Separate a task into a planning prompt and an execution prompt so plans can be reviewed before execution and reused.

prompts.title: Premise-Check Pattern
prompts.description: Add a step that verifies input premises before reasoning, refusing or asking when the premise is false or unverifiable.

prompts.title: Self-Check Pattern: Answer, Then Verify
prompts.description: Add a self-verification pass to a prompt where the model produces an answer, then checks it against named criteria, then revises or confirms.

prompts.title: Self-Consistency Runner
prompts.description: Sample N independent answers at temperature > 0, vote or aggregate, and emit the majority answer with disagreement signal.

prompts.title: Set an Extended-Thinking Budget
prompts.description: Decide and document the thinking-token budget for reasoning models, with rules for adjusting it per input class.

prompts.title: Silent Reasoning, Visible Answer
prompts.description: Have the model reason internally and emit only the conclusion, with reliable separation between hidden reasoning and surfaced answer.

prompts.title: Tree-of-Thought Template
prompts.description: Prompt the model to branch on candidate approaches, evaluate each, prune, and proceed with the best — within a bounded budget.

prompts.title: Build a Reusable Personal Context Document
prompts.description: Produce a single, reusable context document the user pastes into new chats or loads as persistent memory — capturing role, active projects, tools, constraints, vocabulary, and the specific defaults the user doesn't want to re-type every session. Built from evidence of what the user actually explains on every chat, not from an aspirational bio.

prompts.title: Build an Eval Harness for a Personal Workflow
prompts.description: Produce a lightweight, personal-scale eval harness for a task type the user runs repeatedly with AI — 5–10 representative inputs, a rubric, a scoring protocol, and a baseline. The harness is for skill development and quality tracking, not for production CI. It makes prompt changes measurable instead of felt.

prompts.title: Deep Four-Discipline Diagnostic with a Multi-Month Development Roadmap
prompts.description: A deeper, evidence-based diagnostic across the four AI-work disciplines (prompt craft, context, intent, specification) that produces a sequenced 3–6 month development roadmap with checkpoints, artifacts to produce, and exit criteria per discipline. For users who've already run the rapid diagnostic twice and haven't moved.

prompts.title: Design a Reusable Constraint Architecture That Channels AI Output
prompts.description: Build a durable, reusable constraint architecture — a layered set of constraints (format, content, style, scope, authority, safety) the user applies across a class of tasks to reliably channel AI output into the shape the user wants. Distinct from a per-task constraint workshop; this is the library-building version, producing an asset reused for months.

prompts.title: Pre-AI Thinking Exercise Captured Off-Screen Before Opening a Chat
prompts.description: A short, structured off-screen thinking pass — done on paper, in a text file, or on a whiteboard with no model in the loop — that surfaces what you actually want, what you already know, and what decisions you've already made, before the first token is typed into a chat. Prevents the failure mode of outsourcing the thinking to the model and then relitigating the model's output for an hour.

prompts.title: Rapid Diagnostic of AI Skill Across Prompt Craft, Context, Intent, and Specification
prompts.description: A ~10-minute self-assessment that scores the user across four orthogonal disciplines of AI work — prompt craft, context management, intent clarity, and specification — and returns the single weakest discipline to work on next. Not a maturity model; a next-step locator.

prompts.title: Rewrite a Vague Conversational Ask into a Fully Self-Contained Problem Statement
prompts.description: Transforms a casual chat opener — 'help me with X,' 'can you look at this,' 'what do you think about Y' — into a self-contained problem statement the model can act on without follow-up. The rewritten version names the outcome, the inputs, the constraints, the done criteria, and the desired mode. Refuses to rewrite on synthetic examples; the user must supply a real ask.

prompts.title: Write a Specification That Fully Defines 'Done'
prompts.description: Given a task the user is handing to AI, produce a specification where 'done' is unambiguous — every criterion is observable, the set is closed (nothing important is unstated), and a stranger could pass/fail any output against it without asking the user a question. Refuses to produce specs for tasks the user can't yet describe as an outcome.

prompts.title: Dual Output Pattern: Human Prose + Machine JSON
prompts.description: Emit a user-facing message and a machine-readable payload in one call without the two contradicting each other.

prompts.title: Enum Constraint Pattern with Rejection on Unknown
prompts.description: Force a field's value into a closed set, rejecting unknown values with a structured error rather than silently coercing.

prompts.title: Field Ordering for Streaming and Short-Circuit Speed
prompts.description: Order schema fields so consumers can short-circuit on early signals and streamed output becomes useful before completion.

prompts.title: JSON Repair Pattern
prompts.description: Detect and repair malformed JSON from a model without dropping fields, hallucinating values, or silently coercing types.

prompts.title: JSON Schema → Prompt Builder
prompts.description: Convert a JSON Schema into a prompt that produces conforming output, choosing schema-in-prompt vs response_format vs tool-use strategy.

prompts.title: Markdown Section Contract for Parseable Output
prompts.description: Define heading, list, and code-block conventions so a downstream parser can reliably extract sections from markdown output.

prompts.title: Optional Field Policy: null vs Omit vs Empty String
prompts.description: Pick a single, consumer-aligned policy for absent values across a structured-output schema and document the rules.

prompts.title: Second-Pass Schema Compliance Validator
prompts.description: Grade a producer's structured output against a schema with a typed verdict, per-field findings, and a single retry instruction.

prompts.title: Streamable Table Row Emitter
prompts.description: Generate one validated row at a time so consumers can stream, paginate, and reject rows without buffering the whole table.

prompts.title: XML Tag Output Pattern (Claude-Optimized)
prompts.description: Decide when XML tags beat JSON for Claude, and define tag conventions plus a parser regex that survives nested content.

prompts.title: Anti-Voice Designer
prompts.description: Build an enforced banlist of specific voice tics—em-dashes, hedges, opener phrases—with detection patterns and repair rules.

prompts.title: Audience Adaptation Prompt
prompts.description: Rewrite the same content for multiple target audiences with per-audience vocabulary, depth, and structure adjustments.

prompts.title: Brand Guideline to Prompt Rules
prompts.description: Convert a brand style or voice guideline document into an enforceable, copy-paste-ready prompt rule block.

prompts.title: Consistency Audit Across Outputs
prompts.description: Detect voice and style drift across N outputs generated from the same prompt by comparing measurable signals.

prompts.title: Length and Density Control
prompts.description: Enforce hard caps on words-per-claim, sentences-per-paragraph, and total word count with a compliance audit table.

prompts.title: Persona Designer for Writing Tasks
prompts.description: Design a bounded writing persona—voice, sentence style, vocabulary tier—for use in writing prompts, not agent behavior.

prompts.title: Register Control
prompts.description: Rewrite or generate text at a specified formality register with banned and required linguistic forms per level.

prompts.title: Signature Phrase Kill List
prompts.description: Detect and eliminate AI-signature phrases from a corpus of outputs; produces a frequency-ranked banlist with repair patterns.

prompts.title: Voice Extraction from Corpus
prompts.description: Codify a distinctive writing voice from 5+ samples into an operational rule set reusable in prompts.

prompts.title: Voice Transfer Prompt
prompts.description: Apply a target voice specification to a source text without altering any factual claims.

prompts.title: Author a Refusal Policy
prompts.description: Specify the categories the assistant refuses, the tone of refusal, and the alternative paths offered, as concrete prompt rules.

prompts.title: Build a Persistent Rule Set for the System Prompt
prompts.description: Codify the rules that should hold across every turn of every session into a stable, ranked, conflict-free block.

prompts.title: Build the Minimal Viable System Prompt
prompts.description: Write the smallest possible system prompt that still produces acceptable outputs on a target task, then justify each surviving sentence.

prompts.title: Define the User-Input Contract
prompts.description: Specify in the system prompt what user inputs the assistant accepts, the shapes it tolerates, and how it handles malformed or out-of-scope inputs.

prompts.title: Design a Role Charter for a System Prompt
prompts.description: Author the role-defining block of a system prompt: identity, scope, expertise boundary, authority, and what this role explicitly is not.

prompts.title: Multi-Persona Router in a Single System Prompt
prompts.description: Design a system prompt that hosts multiple sub-personas behind a deterministic router so the right persona handles the right input.

prompts.title: Separate the Safety Layer From the Task Layer
prompts.description: Architect the system prompt so safety rules are independently editable, enforceable, and auditable apart from task instructions.

prompts.title: Session Memory Protocol
prompts.description: Specify what the assistant remembers across turns, what it forgets, and how it surfaces remembered facts so users can correct them.

prompts.title: System Prompt Versioning Protocol
prompts.description: Define how a system prompt is versioned, deployed, rolled back, and tracked so changes are auditable and reversible.

prompts.title: System Prompt for an Autonomous Agent
prompts.description: Compose a system prompt suited to autonomous agent loops: persistent identity, action policy, observation discipline, and stop conditions.

prompts.title: Argument Extraction From Messy User Text
prompts.description: Extract typed tool arguments from natural-language input with explicit confidence, source spans, and missing-field handling.

prompts.title: Call-Tool vs Answer-From-Knowledge Decision Prompt
prompts.description: Force a typed decision on whether to invoke a tool or answer directly, with declared confidence and freshness checks.

prompts.title: Disambiguation Before Destructive Tool Calls
prompts.description: Force a clarification turn before invoking a destructive or high-blast-radius tool when args are ambiguous.

prompts.title: Dry-Run / Propose-Confirm-Execute Pattern
prompts.description: Three-step protocol for irreversible tool calls: propose with a diff, get explicit confirmation, then execute with idempotency.

prompts.title: Multi-Tool Orchestration with Dependency Tracking
prompts.description: Plan a sequence of tool calls with explicit dependencies, parallelism, and a single retry rule per node.

prompts.title: Tool Description Writer
prompts.description: Write tool descriptions, parameter docs, and disambiguators so the model picks the right tool on first try.

prompts.title: Tool Failure Recovery Pattern
prompts.description: Classify a tool error and choose retry, fallback, or escalate using a typed decision table — no infinite retries.

prompts.title: Tool Naming Convention for Disambiguation Without Docs
prompts.description: Define a naming pattern that lets the model and humans pick the right tool from the name alone.

prompts.title: Tool Result → User-Facing Answer Interpretation
prompts.description: Turn raw tool output into a user-facing answer with field grounding, error surfacing, and zero invented numbers.

prompts.title: Tool Set Minimization for a Task Class
prompts.description: Find the smallest tool set that fully covers a task class, ranked by per-tool routing confusion and cost.

prompts.title: JSON Prompt Translator
prompts.description: A unified schema system for translating natural language briefs into structured JSON for three target types: UI/UX layouts, diagrams/flow charts, and marketing images. The translator classifies intent, runs clarification questions, and outputs validated JSON.

prompts.title: Historical Operation Case Study — Studying a Documented Campaign Without Inventing It
prompts.description: Build a rigorous case study of a documented, publicly attributed influence operation, anchored to primary sources and named investigations, with an explicit evidence-quality layer distinguishing what was established from what was alleged, reported, or assumed. Every factual specific must be sourced or bracketed, because a fabricated detail in a case study becomes someone else's citation.

prompts.title: Media Literacy Curriculum — Teaching Recognition Without Teaching Cynicism
prompts.description: Design a teaching sequence that builds durable recognition of manipulation technique while avoiding the documented failure mode of media literacy education: producing generalized distrust in which learners dismiss everything, including good sources. Emphasizes transferable checking habits, examples drawn from all political directions, and assessment that measures discrimination rather than suspicion.

prompts.title: Technique Taxonomy Mapping — Reconciling the Competing Frameworks
prompts.description: Map the named public frameworks for influence and propaganda technique against each other — which describe the same move under different names, which operate at different levels of analysis, and where each was built for a purpose that limits its transfer. Requires every framework attribution to be verified rather than recalled, since misattributed taxonomy is the characteristic error in this literature.

prompts.title: Correction Design — Replacing a False Belief Rather Than Just Denying It
prompts.description: Design a correction that actually displaces a false belief: leading with the true account, stating the falsehood once and clearly marked, explaining the manipulation, and — critically — supplying an alternative causal story, because a gap left where an explanation was tends to be refilled with the false one. Handles the continued-influence effect and the risk of amplifying by correcting.

prompts.title: Crisis Communication Integrity — Speaking Honestly While Under Attack
prompts.description: Plan communication during an active information attack without adopting the opponent's methods: what is known versus unknown, what can be said now, who decides at 3am, and which lines will not be crossed regardless of pressure. Pre-commits the integrity limits before the pressure arrives, because they are decided badly under it, and treats admitting uncertainty as a durability strategy rather than a weakness.

prompts.title: Prebunking Design — Warning People Before the Claim Arrives
prompts.description: Design advance inoculation against an expected false claim: a forewarning, a weakened exposure to the technique, and a refutation the audience can carry themselves. Targets the manipulation technique rather than the specific claim, so the protection generalizes. Includes the honesty constraint that prebunking a claim which turns out to be true is a serious failure, and the timing constraint that prebunking after arrival is just debunking.

prompts.title: Rumor Response Triage — Whether Answering Would Do More Harm Than Silence
prompts.description: Decide whether to respond to a false or hostile claim at all, weighing current reach against the reach a response would create, the audience that matters, and the cost of silence. Treats 'monitor and do not respond' as a decision with owners and tripwires rather than as inaction, and blocks the reflex to respond to everything visible to the communications team.

prompts.title: Astroturf vs Organic — Is the Grassroots Support Real
prompts.description: Assess whether a movement, campaign, or wave of public comment reflects genuine constituency or manufactured appearance, using funding transparency, participation depth, local specificity, and cost-to-participate rather than message uniformity. Built to protect real grassroots movements from dismissal, since accusing an authentic movement of astroturfing is the more common and more damaging error.

prompts.title: Attribution Confidence — How Sure Can You Honestly Be About Who Did This
prompts.description: Grade attribution claims about who is behind an influence operation, separating the three distinct questions of infrastructure, sponsorship, and direction, and applying explicit confidence language with stated basis. Treats 'unattributed' as the correct default and the most common honest outcome, and handles the fact that false-flag and imitation activity make the obvious attribution the one most worth doubting.

prompts.title: Coordination Indicators — Telling Coordinated Behavior from Organic Convergence
prompts.description: Assess whether a cluster of accounts or outlets is coordinated, using structural indicators that organic convergence does not produce: synchronized timing at implausible resolution, shared infrastructure, identical asset reuse, and unnatural amplification topology. Explicitly ranks message similarity as the weakest indicator, because people who agree say the same things. Requires an organic-explanation pass before any coordination finding.

prompts.title: Inauthentic Account Signals — Assessing Automation Without Accusing People
prompts.description: Assess behavioral signals of automation or identity misrepresentation on a set of accounts, while treating every alternative explanation — a heavy user, a scheduled feed, a non-native speaker, a marketer, a lonely person — as a live hypothesis. Built around the fact that 'bot' accusations are usually wrong and land on real people. Outputs account-level behavioral findings with confidence bands, never a person-level verdict.

prompts.title: Influence Operation Analysis — Actors, Behavior, Content, Degree, Effect
prompts.description: Assess whether observed activity constitutes a coordinated influence operation, using the ABCDE axes (actors, behavior, content, degree, effect) analyzed separately so that a striking finding on one axis cannot carry the others. Produces a confidence-graded assessment with a mandatory alternative-explanation pass, and treats 'insufficient evidence — this looks organic' as a first-class result. Counters the field's dominant failure mode: inferring a campaign from content you dislike.

prompts.title: Information Laundering Chain Map — How a Claim Becomes Citable
prompts.description: Map the hops by which an unsourced claim acquires citability: placement in a low-scrutiny outlet, citation by a marginally more credible one, aggregation, and finally reference by an institution that treats the chain as sourcing. Locates the citation loop where outlets cite each other in a circle with no original evidence, and identifies the hop where the hedge was dropped.

prompts.title: Narrative Lifecycle Tracker — Seeding, Amplification, Mainstreaming, Laundering
prompts.description: Track a narrative through its stages — origination, seeding into receptive communities, amplification, crossover to mainstream attention, and laundering into citable legitimacy — recording what changed at each transition and which actors were load-bearing. Distinguishes a pushed narrative from one that simply resonated, and identifies the stage where intervention would still have mattered.

prompts.title: Community Resilience Review — Design Against Brigading and Manufactured Consensus
prompts.description: Review a community or platform's structural resilience to brigading, manufactured consensus, and moderation capture: which mechanisms convert volume into visibility or sanction, how new-account and vote-based influence is bounded, and whether reporting can be weaponized against the people it exists to protect. Assesses design, not participants.

prompts.title: Narrative Vulnerability Assessment — Which True Things About You Are Exploitable
prompts.description: Identify the narratives about your organization that would be most damaging and most difficult to answer, sorted by whether they are true, partly true, or false — because the true ones are both the most exploitable and the only ones with a real fix. Produces remediation ownership for substantiated vulnerabilities rather than messaging, and never drafts the attacking narrative.

prompts.title: Organizational Influence Threat Model — Who Would Target Us, and What We Would Do
prompts.description: Threat-model an organization's exposure to influence and information attack: which adversaries have motive and means, which channels reach your audiences, what a plausible campaign against you would exploit, and which detection and response capabilities you actually have. Produces findings and countermeasures only — never campaign material — and treats fixing genuine underlying problems as a first-class countermeasure.

prompts.title: Personnel Targeting Exposure Review — Reducing What Can Be Used Against Your People
prompts.description: Assess how exposed key staff are to pretexting, impersonation, and targeted harassment, using only what is already publicly available, and produce reduction actions plus organizational protections. Consent-first and dignity-first: staff are participants rather than subjects, findings go to the individual, and the review never investigates private lives or produces a dossier.

prompts.title: Coercive Control Pattern Recognition — Naming a Pattern and Getting Real Help
prompts.description: Help someone recognize whether what they are living with matches documented coercive-control patterns — isolation, monitoring, financial restriction, micro-regulation of daily life, and threats — and move them toward trained support rather than toward a decision. Safety-first throughout: prioritizes not tipping off a controlling person, and treats professional support as the destination rather than an afterthought.

prompts.title: Cognitive Security Hygiene — Rules You Set Before the Pressure Arrives
prompts.description: Build a small set of pre-committed personal rules that hold under manipulation, urgency, and emotional activation — the conditions in which judgment is least available. Targets the specific states in which you are actually exploited rather than aiming at general skepticism, and keeps the rule set small enough to survive contact with a real Tuesday.

prompts.title: High-Control Group Dynamics — Assessing Structure, Not Beliefs
prompts.description: Assess a group against documented high-control structural criteria — exit cost, information control, thought-terminating language, leader accountability, and the price of dissent — while holding the group's actual beliefs entirely out of scope. Built so that an unusual belief system is never itself the finding, since the structural questions apply identically to religious, political, commercial, wellness, and workplace groups.

prompts.title: Information Diet Audit — What Is Actually Shaping What You Believe
prompts.description: Audit the real inputs forming your picture of the world: which sources, selected by whom, at what emotional intensity, with what feedback loop. Reconstructs the gap between the sources you would name and the ones actually consuming your attention, and distinguishes narrowness of viewpoint from narrowness of evidence — the second being the one that matters.

prompts.title: Manipulation Recognition — Sorting What Happened from What You Were Told Happened
prompts.description: Work through whether a specific interaction or pattern in your life involves manipulation, by separating what was actually said and done from the interpretation you were given. Organizes your own observations into evidence you can evaluate, distinguishes manipulation from ordinary conflict and from honest disagreement, and routes anything involving fear, control, or safety to qualified support. Does not diagnose anyone.

prompts.title: Pretext Recognition — Verifying Who Is Actually Contacting You
prompts.description: Assess an unexpected approach — call, message, email, or in-person — for the structure shared by social engineering attempts: a manufactured reason to be contacting you, urgency that prevents verification, and an action that must happen now. Centers on out-of-band verification through a channel you found yourself, which defeats the entire class regardless of how convincing the approach is.

prompts.title: Worried About Someone — Sorting Concern from Change, and Finding Real Help
prompts.description: Help someone worried that a person they love is being drawn into a harmful movement to separate what they have actually observed from what they fear, distinguish changed opinions from the specific indicators that warrant professional help, and reach the services that exist for exactly this. Preserves the relationship, because the connection is the single strongest protective factor. Routes any indication of planned harm to authorities immediately.

prompts.title: Emotional Manipulation Decoder — Which Feeling, Recruited for What
prompts.description: Map the emotional architecture of a message: which emotion each passage recruits, by what device, and what action or belief that emotion is being converted into. Tests whether the emotion is proportionate to the underlying facts, since appropriate emotion about real stakes is honest communication and only disproportionate or misdirected emotion is manipulation. Counters the reflex of treating all emotional appeal as illegitimate.

prompts.title: Framing and Narrative Analysis — What the Frame Makes Invisible
prompts.description: Recover the frame a message imposes: its metaphor, its cast of agents and victims, where it starts the clock, what it treats as background, and which questions it makes unaskable. Reframes the same facts two other ways to expose what the original frame does. Counters the failure of arguing inside a frame you never noticed you accepted.

prompts.title: Persuasion Pressure Audit — Compliance Mechanics and Dark Patterns in an Offer
prompts.description: Inventory the structural compliance pressure in a message, offer, interface, or pitch: manufactured urgency, artificial scarcity, reciprocity debt, commitment laddering, social proof, authority signaling, default manipulation, and friction asymmetry. Distinguishes real constraints from manufactured ones by asking what happens if the target simply waits. Counters both the failure of missing engineered pressure and the failure of treating every deadline as a trick.

prompts.title: Propaganda Technique Identification — Name the Move, Quote the Evidence
prompts.description: Dissect a single artifact — a post, ad, speech, article, or video script — into the specific persuasion and propaganda techniques it uses, each named and anchored to a quoted span. Separates technique presence from intent and from falsity, since ordinary honest communication uses many of the same moves. Counters the failure mode of labeling any disagreeable message 'propaganda' without being able to point at what in it does the work.

prompts.title: Provenance and Transmission Trace — Where Did This Actually Come From
prompts.description: Trace a claim, image, video, or document backwards through its chain of transmission toward first appearance, recording what changed at each hop: added captions, lost context, altered dates, shifted attribution, and upgraded certainty. Separates the provenance question (where did it come from) from the truth question (is it accurate), since old, recontextualized, and misattributed material is frequently authentic.

prompts.title: Rhetorical Deception Scan — Structural Bad Faith, Not Ordinary Fallacy
prompts.description: Scan an argument for the structural moves that make it unfalsifiable or unanswerable in practice: motte-and-bailey, gish gallop, just-asking-questions, false balance, concern trolling, goalpost shifting, and prebunked criticism. Distinguishes these from honest error, since the same surface can come from confusion or from design. Complements general fallacy detection by focusing on moves whose function is to exhaust or trap a responder rather than to reason badly.

prompts.title: Statistical and Visual Distortion Scan — Where the Number Stops Meaning What It Says
prompts.description: Audit a statistic, chart, or data claim for the distortions that survive technical accuracy: truncated axes, base-rate omission, relative-risk inflation, denominator swaps, cherry-picked baselines, survivorship bias, and misleading aggregation. Assumes incompetence before design, because most bad charts are made by people in a hurry. Produces the honest restatement of the same underlying data.

prompts.title: Cognitive Distortion Identifier

prompts.title: Psychoeducation Material Creator

prompts.description: Design qualitative research interview protocols with question sequencing, probing strategies, and rapport-building elements

prompts.title: Therapeutic Technique Explainer
prompts.description: Explain evidence-based therapeutic techniques for training and educational purposes with theoretical rationale and implementation steps

prompts.title: ADHD Testing Battery Design (Adult / Child, Multi-Source)
prompts.description: Design an adult or child ADHD testing battery using multi-source, multi-informant data — developmental history, rating scales, performance-test caveats, and a structured differential — without overrelying on any single instrument.

prompts.title: Assessment Battery Selection Aid
prompts.description: Translate a referral question into a defensible assessment battery — mapping referral question to constructs, candidate instruments (named only), and a battery design with time/cost/burden tradeoffs and referral thresholds.

prompts.title: Autism Assessment Battery Design (Masking-Aware, Multi-Informant)
prompts.description: Design a masking-aware, multi-informant autism assessment battery — developmental history, observational assessment, self/informant screeners, cognitive/adaptive measures, and differential — attentive to adult and female/late-identified presentations and camouflaging.

prompts.title: Decisional-Capacity Evaluation Scaffold (Medical / Financial)
prompts.description: Scaffold a decision-specific decisional-capacity evaluation using Appelbaum's four abilities — understanding, appreciation, reasoning, expressing a choice — applied on a sliding scale to decision risk, with cognitive screening and capacity-vs-competency distinction.

prompts.title: Forensic Evaluation Framing (Referral Question, Role, Limits)
prompts.description: Frame a forensic psychological evaluation before it begins — clarifying the legal referral question and retaining party, the forensic-vs-therapeutic role boundary, notification and confidentiality limits, third-party data requirements, response-style considerations, and the boundaries of opinion.

prompts.title: Integrated Assessment Report Writer
prompts.description: Write an integrated psychological assessment report from multi-source findings — synthesizing referral question, background, behavioral observations, validity considerations, results organized BY DOMAIN/QUESTION, integrated interpretation, diagnostic impressions, and tailored recommendations as a narrative integration rather than a data dump.

prompts.title: Multi-Method Personality Assessment Integration
prompts.description: Integrate multi-method personality assessment data — self-report inventories, performance-based measures, interview, and collateral — into a coherent formulation that reconciles convergent and divergent findings, weighs response style/validity, and produces an integrated description rather than a list of test scores.

prompts.title: Neuropsychological / Cognitive Screening Interpretation
prompts.description: Interpret cognitive-screening results (MoCA, MMSE, RBANS, SLUMS, Mini-Cog) into a referral-aware clinical read — distinguishing screening from full neuropsych evaluation, framing domain patterns without overcalling, and flagging when full evaluation or neurology referral is indicated.

prompts.title: Patient-Reported Outcome Measure (PROM) Selection Aid
prompts.description: Select patient-reported outcome measures matched to presentation and setting — mapping construct, population, setting, administration burden, cadence, sensitivity to change, and licensing into a measurement-based-care recommendation.

prompts.title: Therapeutic Assessment Feedback-Session Planner
prompts.description: Plan a collaborative/therapeutic-assessment feedback session (Finn's model) — organizing findings into Level 1/2/3 information, sequencing delivery, anticipating client reactions, tying findings to the client's original assessment questions, and producing usable next steps.

prompts.title: Integrated / Collaborative-Care Huddle Brief
prompts.description: Produce a concise registry-style huddle brief on shared collaborative-care panel patients for the BHCM, PCP, and consulting psychiatrist: target symptom scores, treatment-to-target status, and recommendations.

prompts.title: PCP Communication Note (Psychiatric / Medication Coordination)
prompts.description: Write a minimum-necessary note to the primary care physician conveying relevant psychiatric and medication information: diagnoses, current psychotropics and monitoring needs, labs requested, and specific coordination asks.

prompts.title: Referral Letter Generator (Specialist / Higher LOC)
prompts.description: Generate a scoped referral letter to a specialist (psychiatrist, neuropsychology, PCP, higher level of care) with a sharp referral question, ROI-bounded clinical summary, current meds/risk, and an explicit ask.

prompts.title: School-Partnership Communication (Counselor / Teacher / IEP-504 Team)
prompts.description: Draft a scope-limited communication to a school counselor, teacher, or IEP/504 team conveying only functional/classroom-relevant information and recommended accommodations, with explicit consent/assent framing and a statement of what is NOT disclosed.

prompts.title: Warm-Handoff / Transfer-of-Care Narrative
prompts.description: Produce a warm-handoff narrative for transferring a client between clinicians or levels of care: reason for transfer, treatment summary, what's working vs. not, active risk, open loops, and recommended next steps.

prompts.title: Complaint to a State Licensing Board — Draft
prompts.description: Draft a factual, chronological complaint to a state mental health licensing board — who, what, when, and which standard of conduct concerns you — and find the right board, while staying procedural and routing legal harm to an attorney.

prompts.title: Requesting Your Clinical Records — Letter Draft
prompts.description: Draft a clear HIPAA right-of-access request for your mental health records — specifying which records, format, dates, and where to send them — with a plain explanation that psychotherapy process notes may be handled differently.

prompts.title: Self-Advocacy on an Inpatient Psychiatric Unit
prompts.description: Prepare to advocate for yourself on an inpatient psychiatric unit — questions to ask the team, how to state your goals and preferences, understanding your rights and the discharge plan, and how to ask about medications — in a collaborative, respectful way.

prompts.title: Workplace Accommodations Request for Mental Health — Draft
prompts.description: Draft an ADA-style workplace accommodations request for a mental health condition — framing the functional limitation without over-disclosing your diagnosis, naming specific accommodations, and using interactive-process language — as a request structure, not legal advice.

prompts.title: Writing to a Therapist About a Concern — Message Draft
prompts.description: Draft a concise, boundaried between-session message to your therapist about a concern — naming the concern, what you need, and how urgent it is — without using the message as an emergency channel.

prompts.title: ADHD External Scaffold Designer
prompts.description: Help an adult ADHD client design external scaffolds — environmental, temporal, social, and digital — that compensate for executive-function gaps without depending on willpower.

prompts.title: Anger Time-Out Script Builder
prompts.description: Build a personalized anger time-out script — the words to say, the action to take, the duration, and the return — so anger surges don't end in damage to relationships or self.

prompts.title: Anti-Avoidance Prompt for Depression
prompts.description: Help a client surface what they've been avoiding (calls, tasks, decisions, conversations) and convert one item into the smallest possible next action without judgment.
