prompts.title: Anxiety Grounding Menu Builder
prompts.description: Build a personalized menu of grounding techniques matched to a client's specific contexts (work, public, in bed, in transit, in front of kids), so the right technique is at hand in the right moment.

prompts.title: Behavioral Activation Scheduler
prompts.description: Help a client schedule behavioral activation activities — small, specific, mood-aware activities that reverse the depression-withdrawal-flatness loop.

prompts.title: CBT-I Sleep Restriction Calculator (Client-Side)
prompts.description: Help a client implement the sleep restriction component of CBT-I (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia) — calculate sleep window, set bedtime/wake time, manage daytime sleepiness, and titrate.

prompts.title: Family Accommodation Reduction Plan (OCD)
prompts.description: Help an OCD client and their household identify family accommodations (reassurance, doing the check, avoiding triggers, washing for the person, taking on rituals) and reduce them in coordination with the ERP plan.

prompts.title: Flashback Grounding Script
prompts.description: A scripted in-the-moment grounding sequence for flashbacks (sensory, somatic, or full reliving), designed to be readable off a phone in 60 seconds when cognition is offline.

prompts.title: OCD ERP Exercise — Drafting With Your Therapist
prompts.description: Help a client draft an Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) exercise to bring to their OCD-trained clinician for review. Specifies exposure, response prevention, anticipated SUDS, success criteria, and what NOT to do.

prompts.title: Personal Panic Plan Builder
prompts.description: Build a one-page panic-attack plan covering early warning, in-the-moment steps, post-attack debrief, and the medical-rule-out checkpoint.

prompts.title: Rumination Interrupt Protocol
prompts.description: Help a client interrupt depressive rumination — repetitive, abstract, past-oriented self-focused thinking that maintains depression — using attention-redirection and concrete-thinking techniques.

prompts.title: Self-Designed Exposure (With Your Therapist) Worksheet
prompts.description: Help a client design exposure exercises to bring to their therapist for review and assignment — building a graded hierarchy and matching it to current skill level.

prompts.title: Window of Tolerance Check
prompts.description: Help a client check whether they are in their window of tolerance, hyperaroused (above), or hypoaroused (below) — and select a matched skill to come back.

prompts.title: Worry Postponement Protocol
prompts.description: Help a client implement worry postponement (a CBT-for-GAD technique): a daily 'worry window' that contains rumination instead of letting it take all day.

prompts.title: After Losing Someone to Suicide — Initial Support
prompts.description: An initial support framework for the first weeks after losing someone to suicide: validating the specific grief of suicide loss (guilt, 'why', stigma), organizing first-weeks support, deciding what to tell people, finding survivor-of-suicide-loss resources, watching your own safety, and handing off to a therapist.

prompts.title: Am I in Crisis? — Self-Triage
prompts.description: Plain-language self-triage to decide right now whether to call 911 / go to the ED, reach a crisis line, contact a clinician today, or use coping and follow up this week — based on simple decision questions, not a clinical scale.

prompts.title: First 72 Hours After ED Discharge — Personal Plan
prompts.description: Build a personal plan for the first 72 hours after leaving the emergency department for a mental-health crisis: means-safety at home, who's with me, locking in follow-up, medication continuity, warning signs to go back, and 988/ED routing — designed to hand to an outpatient clinician.

prompts.title: Supporting a Loved One in Suicidal Crisis
prompts.description: Concrete guidance for what to do when someone you love may be suicidal: how to ask directly, listen, reduce access to means, stay with them or get them to help, route to 988/911/ED, and care for yourself — without promising secrecy about safety.

prompts.title: Ambiguous Loss Framework
prompts.description: Apply Pauline Boss's ambiguous-loss framework to a living-but-lost relationship — dementia, addiction, estrangement, incarceration, brain injury — by naming the type of loss, holding both-and, finding meaning, and setting a boundary on hope.

prompts.title: Anniversary Reaction Plan
prompts.description: Pre-plan for a grief anniversary — death-day, birthday, holiday, or season — by anticipating the wave, shaping the day with or without others, deciding what to allow, and flagging when grief tips toward crisis.

prompts.title: Complicated vs. Normal Grief — Self-Reflection
prompts.description: Guide a structured self-reflection on whether grief may be crossing from normal bereavement into prolonged grief disorder — using PGD markers descriptively — with a clear clinician handoff and crisis escalation if suicidal ideation is present.

prompts.title: Continuing-Bonds Grief Journaling
prompts.description: Generate continuing-bonds journal prompts that help maintain a healthy connection with someone who died — letters, rituals, 'what would they say' — with calibration that grief is non-linear and not a set of stages to finish.

prompts.title: Pet Loss Reflection & Ritual Script
prompts.description: Validate the often-disenfranchised grief of losing a pet and produce a reflection-and-ritual script — a goodbye or memory ritual, an ongoing memory practice, and language for handling people who minimize the loss.

prompts.title: Alcohol Use Re-Evaluation
prompts.description: A non-judgmental, DrinkLess-style re-evaluation of your drinking — honest baseline (units/week, patterns, triggers, function), a decisional balance, and small experiments. Includes a required safety carve-out for physical dependence (do not stop abruptly) and a clinician handoff.

prompts.title: Exercise-as-Antidepressant Plan
prompts.description: Build a movement plan that uses exercise for its mood benefit — evidence-based dose framing (general guidance, not a prescription), a too-small-to-fail start, mood-paired tracking, and explicit overlap with behavioral activation. Includes a medical-clearance carve-out and a route to a clinician/988 if depression is severe or suicidal thoughts are present.

prompts.title: Screen Time & Phone Relationship Audit
prompts.description: An honest, shame-free look at your relationship with your phone — what it's doing FOR you (function), where it actually costs you, value-aligned changes, and friction tweaks. No detox dogma, no moralizing.

prompts.title: Sustainable Habit Designer (with Relapse Planning)
prompts.description: Design one habit you can actually keep — tiny start, a concrete anchor cue (implementation intention), friction tuning, lightweight tracking, and a relapse-is-normal recovery plan that beats all-or-nothing thinking.

prompts.title: Coming-Out Conversation Planner
prompts.description: Plan a coming-out conversation about gender, sexuality, or identity — who/when/how, the actual opening sentences, anticipated reactions and responses, a safety-first carve-out, and aftercare.

prompts.title: Divorce / Separation Emotional Plan
prompts.description: Build an emotional plan for a divorce or separation that is kept distinct from the legal and logistical track — grieving the relationship, the identity shift, co-parenting emotional load, and escalation if depression or suicidal thoughts appear.

prompts.title: Gender Identity Exploration Journal
prompts.description: A structured, non-leading journal for exploring gender identity at one's own pace — felt-sense reflection, euphoria and dysphoria mapping, social and medical questions held lightly, with no timeline pressure and an affirming-therapist handoff.

prompts.title: Post-Diagnosis Adjustment
prompts.description: Adjust to a new chronic-illness or neurodivergence diagnosis — naming the grief and the relief, integrating the diagnosis without being defined by it, reframing the past through the new lens, and seeding self-advocacy, with a therapist handoff.

prompts.title: Religious Deconstruction Support
prompts.description: Work through religious deconstruction with grief and integrity — name the losses (community, meaning, certainty), hold ambiguity, separate questions of belief from belonging, with a handoff for grief and anxiety.

prompts.title: Retirement Identity Reframe
prompts.description: Work through the identity loss that can come with retirement — naming what work provided (structure, status, purpose, social connection), reframing and rebuilding those, watching for depression, with a therapist handoff.

prompts.title: Gratitude Journal With Calibration
prompts.description: A gratitude practice that doesn't slide into toxic positivity: pairs each gratitude with the honest texture (mixed feelings, ambivalence, what's hard) and calibrates difficulty to current state.

prompts.title: Journal Prompt Generator (Anti-Toxic-Positivity)
prompts.description: Generate journaling prompts that go past gratitude-list templates without flipping into rumination — calibrated to the client's current emotional state and capacity.

prompts.title: Mood Tracking Summarizer
prompts.description: Take a stretch of mood-tracking entries (PHQ-9, GAD-7, daily mood log, sleep, energy, substance use, exercise) and produce a pattern summary the client can review or bring to a clinician.

prompts.title: Weekly Emotional Pattern Review
prompts.description: A 15-minute weekly review surfacing the week's emotional pattern: highs, lows, recurring themes, what helped, what didn't, and the one thing to carry into next week.

prompts.title: Affordable Therapy Navigator — Insurance, EAP, Sliding Scale
prompts.description: Build a step-by-step plan to find affordable therapy across insurance, EAP, sliding-scale, training clinics, and community mental health — with call scripts and the cost questions to ask.

prompts.title: Do I Need Therapy? — Self-Decision Aid
prompts.description: Weigh the signals — functioning, duration, distress, and whether self-help has hit a ceiling — into a lean toward (or away from) starting therapy, with safety escalation if it surfaces.

prompts.title: Finding a Therapist — Search Criteria & Consult Questions
prompts.description: Turn what I need into concrete search filters (specialty, modality, identity, logistics, budget) plus a consult-call question set and a list of green and red flags to read for.

prompts.title: Screening a Therapist for Cultural & Identity Fit
prompts.description: Generate identity-relevant screening questions for a prospective therapist and a guide to reading their answers — without prescribing the 'right' answers or treating identity as a single box to check.

prompts.title: Therapy Modality Fit Selector
prompts.description: Plainly describe the major therapy approaches (CBT, DBT, EMDR, psychodynamic, IFS, ACT), map my concerns to the ones most likely to fit, and produce questions to ask a prospective therapist — treating fit as collaborative, not destiny.

prompts.title: Explain My Diagnosis to Me — Plain Language
prompts.description: Give a plain-language, general explanation of a mental-health diagnosis a clinician gave me — what it commonly means, what it does not mean, typical treatment options, and questions to bring back to my clinician.

prompts.title: Questions to Ask About a Newly Prescribed Psychiatric Medication
prompts.description: Build a question checklist for a client who was just prescribed a psychotropic medication — purpose, time to work, side effects, interactions, alcohol, missed doses, stopping/taper, follow-up — with NO dosing advice and clear routing to the prescriber/pharmacist.

prompts.title: Understanding My Partner's Diagnosis — Support Without Taking It On
prompts.description: Understand a partner's (or close person's) mental-health diagnosis in general terms so I can support them without over-functioning, losing my boundaries, or making their condition my whole identity.

prompts.title: What to Expect From a Neuropsychological Evaluation
prompts.description: Explain in plain language what a neuropsychological evaluation is for, its typical multi-session structure, the general kinds of testing involved (no item content), how to prepare, and the usual timeline to results and a feedback session.

prompts.title: What to Expect at My First Psychiatry Appointment
prompts.description: Plain-language walkthrough of a first psychiatric (or psychiatric-prescriber) appointment — what they'll ask, what to bring, how long it runs, that medication may or may not be started, and questions to bring.

prompts.title: Attachment-Style Self-Reflection
prompts.description: Reflect on attachment tendencies (secure, anxious, avoidant, disorganized) as a lens rather than a fixed label — map specific behaviors to tendencies, name what they protect, and emphasize earned security and changeability.

prompts.title: Boundary-Setting Script Builder
prompts.description: Build a specific boundary-setting script — the boundary stated plainly, the actual sentences, anticipated pushback with prepared responses, and a follow-through plan for when the boundary is tested.

prompts.title: Conflict Postmortem
prompts.description: After a conflict, map what each person was protecting — the cycle, each person's underlying need and fear, the trigger, and one specific experiment to try next time.

prompts.title: Friendship-End or Hibernation Conversation Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a friendship-ending or pause/hibernation conversation — first getting clear on what you actually want (end vs pause vs fade), then the actual message options at varying directness, and how to handle the likely responses.

prompts.title: Is This Relationship Healthy? — Pattern Check
prompts.description: Pattern-check a relationship across several dimensions — respect, reciprocity, safety, repair, autonomy — with a hard safety carve-out: if abuse or control signals appear, route to DV resources / safety planning / 988 and do not 'both-sides' it.

prompts.title: Navigating Family Estrangement
prompts.description: Work through family or parental estrangement across all three stances — initiating distance, holding existing distance, or attempting repair — neutrally, with a hard safety carve-out for abuse and a 'bring this to my therapist' handoff for the grief.

prompts.title: Repair Conversation Drafter
prompts.description: Draft an apology / repair conversation that owns what's actually yours without over- or under-owning — what's mine vs not, the repair sentences, what NOT to add (defensiveness, false-equivalence, the 'but'), and a follow-up.

prompts.title: Asking My Therapist for a Change in Approach
prompts.description: Help a client articulate a request for change in their therapy: pace, modality, focus, structure, communication style, or session frequency.

prompts.title: Between-Session Homework Helper (Client-Side)
prompts.description: Help a client work with therapy homework they were assigned but are stuck on — clarify, troubleshoot, scale down, or surface what's making it hard.

prompts.title: Ending Therapy Conversation Planner (Client-Side)
prompts.description: Help a client plan the conversation about ending therapy — whether because the work is complete, because of fit, finances, life change, or because they want a break.

prompts.title: Post-Session Reflection Processor (Client-Side)
prompts.description: Help a client integrate what just happened in a therapy session: what landed, what didn't, what shifted, and what to do between now and the next session.

prompts.title: Pre-Session Agenda Drafter (Client-Side)
prompts.description: Help a client compile a focused, honest agenda for an upcoming therapy session in 10–15 minutes — what to bring up, what's been hard to say, what to revisit from last time.

prompts.title: Saying Hard Things to a Therapist — Rehearsal
prompts.description: Help a client rehearse a hard thing they want to bring to their therapist — disclosure, disagreement, ending therapy, asking about a clinical mistake, or revealing relapse / NSSI / SI they've been hiding.

prompts.title: Anxiety vs Depression vs Burnout — Self-Differentiator
prompts.description: Help a client distinguish among anxiety, depression, burnout, and grief when they're experiencing low energy, worry, or numbness — including overlap and what to do about each.

prompts.title: Hypomania Self-Check
prompts.description: Help a client think through whether a recent stretch of high energy, productivity, or elevated mood might be hypomania rather than a great week or burnout-recovery.

prompts.title: Intrusive Thoughts — Normal vs OCD Signal
prompts.description: Help a client tell the difference between ordinary intrusive thoughts (which most people have) and an OCD pattern that may benefit from specialized treatment.

prompts.title: Panic Attack vs Heart Attack — Reasoning Through It
prompts.description: Help a client think through whether what they're experiencing is panic, a cardiac event, or another medical issue — without delaying medical care when uncertain.

prompts.title: Self-Screen Score Interpreter (PHQ-9, GAD-7, PCL-5, AUDIT, ACE, MDQ)
prompts.description: Help a client interpret a self-administered screening score (PHQ-9, GAD-7, PCL-5, AUDIT, MDQ, ACE) without diagnosing — what the band means, what the limits are, and what to do with the result.

prompts.title: Trauma Response Pattern Recognizer
prompts.description: Help a client recognize whether what they're experiencing — flashbacks, hyperarousal, numbing, avoidance, dissociation — fits a trauma-response pattern, and what kinds of help are matched to it.

prompts.title: Comorbidity Mapping and Treatment Implication Planner
prompts.description: Map common comorbidity patterns across DSM-5-TR diagnostic pairs and triads, and derive sequencing and treatment-modification implications for each pattern

prompts.title: DSM-5-TR Differential Diagnosis Generator
prompts.description: Generate a ranked ICD-10-CM / DSM-5-TR differential with confirm and refute criteria per candidate diagnosis

prompts.title: Diagnostic Disclosure Conversation Planner
prompts.description: Plan and structure the conversation in which a clinician shares a formal diagnosis with a client, balancing accuracy with the client's emotional readiness and maintaining collaborative agency

prompts.title: ICD-10-CM to DSM-5-TR Crosswalk Assistant
prompts.description: Produce accurate DSM-5-TR to ICD-10-CM code crosswalk tables for billing and clinical documentation

prompts.title: Malingering vs. Genuine Distress Framework
prompts.description: Apply a forensic-aware, multi-evidence credibility framework that evaluates symptom validity without defaulting to dismissal of genuine distress

prompts.title: Normal Reaction vs. Disorder Reasoner
prompts.description: Apply structured clinical reasoning to determine when grief, acute stress, life-stage transition, or other expected human experiences cross the threshold into a diagnosable disorder

prompts.title: Personality Disorder Dimensional Formulation (DSM-5 Section III AMPD)
prompts.description: Generate a dimensional personality disorder formulation using the DSM-5 Alternative Model for Personality Disorders (Section III), rating self/interpersonal functioning and pathological trait domains

prompts.title: Provisional vs. Rule-Out vs. Deferred Diagnosis Decision Aid
prompts.description: Guide the clinician through deciding when to assign provisional, rule-out, or deferred diagnostic status rather than a confirmed diagnosis

prompts.title: AI-Augmented Practice Operations Design
prompts.description: Design AI-augmented mental-health practice operations with clinical-oversight guardrails: separate AI-appropriate operational tasks from human-only clinical decisions, and for each automated task define the human-in-the-loop checkpoint, hallucination/error risk, PHI/data-governance handling, and audit trail.

prompts.title: Asynchronous Messaging Therapy Protocol
prompts.description: Design an asynchronous text/messaging therapy protocol with risk routing: response-window SLAs, scope of what async is and is not appropriate for, session-equivalence/billing, structured message format, in-text crisis detection and escalation (async is NOT for emergencies), boundary/availability framing, documentation, and criteria for converting to synchronous care.

prompts.title: Digital Phenotyping Data Interpreter
prompts.description: Interpret passive and app-collected behavioral data (sleep, mobility/GPS, phone-use, typing dynamics, actigraphy, EMA self-report) into hypothesis-generating clinical signal requiring clinical correlation — never diagnosis — with baseline/deviation logic, false-positive sources, consent/privacy, and clinician-outreach triggers.

prompts.title: Telemental Health Program Design
prompts.description: Design a tele-mental-health program covering modality selection, HIPAA-compliant platform requirements, clinical-appropriateness screening, telehealth informed consent, per-location emergency protocols, and PSYPACT licensure compliance.

prompts.title: BIRP-Format Progress Note Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a BIRP-format (Behavior / Intervention / Response / Plan) progress note common in CMH, SUD, and case-management settings.

prompts.title: Biopsychosocial Intake Assessment Note Drafter
prompts.description: Compile a complete biopsychosocial intake assessment from clinician interview notes, including HPI, full history, MSE, formulation, provisional diagnoses, and initial plan.

prompts.title: Clinical Supervision Note Drafter
prompts.description: Document a clinical supervision session (supervisor or supervisee perspective): cases reviewed, interventions taught, parallel-process observations, supervisee competencies advanced, and plan.

prompts.title: Collateral Contact Note Drafter
prompts.description: Document a collateral contact with PCP, school, family, probation, or other party — including ROI status, purpose, content shared and received, and clinical impact.

prompts.title: DAP-Format Psychotherapy Progress Note Drafter
prompts.description: Convert raw session notes into a DAP-format (Data / Assessment / Plan) progress note with rigorous separation of objective and subjective data inside the Data block.

prompts.title: Discharge Summary Drafter
prompts.description: Draft an outpatient or program discharge summary documenting course of treatment, gains, residual concerns, aftercare plan, and prognosis.

prompts.title: GIRP-Format Progress Note Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a GIRP-format (Goal / Intervention / Response / Plan) progress note that anchors every line of the note to a numbered treatment-plan goal.

prompts.title: Group Therapy Progress Note Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a group psychotherapy progress note that documents group census, theme, individual participation per member, group process, safety, and plan, billable per-member.

prompts.title: Initial Treatment Plan Drafter (Golden-Thread)
prompts.description: Build a goal-driven initial treatment plan with explicit golden thread linking problem → goal → measurable objective → intervention → frequency → reviewer.

prompts.title: PIRP-Format Progress Note Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a PIRP-format (Problem / Intervention / Response / Plan) progress note that anchors the encounter to the presenting clinical problem rather than to a behavior or a goal.

prompts.title: SOAP-Format Psychotherapy Progress Note Drafter
prompts.description: Convert raw session notes into a clinically defensible SOAP-format individual psychotherapy progress note that supports the billed CPT code.

prompts.title: Telehealth Session Progress Note Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a telehealth-specific psychotherapy progress note covering location attestation, identity verification, environment/privacy adequacy, technology functioning, telehealth modifier/POS, and standard clinical content.

prompts.title: Therapeutic Termination Summary Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a therapeutic termination summary distinct from administrative discharge — focused on the relational arc, processing of the ending, gains internalized, and a forward-looking handoff to the client's future self.

prompts.title: Treatment Plan Update / 90-Day Review Drafter
prompts.description: Generate a treatment-plan update or 90-day review documenting progress on each objective, justifying continued care, and modifying the plan with audit-grade rationale.

prompts.title: Bowenian Three-Generation Genogram Formulation
prompts.description: Build a multigenerational genogram formulation across Bowen's eight concepts (differentiation, triangles, nuclear family emotional process, family projection, multigenerational transmission, emotional cutoff, sibling position, societal emotional process) with standard genogram symbol legend and pattern-reading guidance.

prompts.title: Discernment Counseling Protocol (Doherty, Mixed-Agenda Couples)
prompts.description: Run Bill Doherty's Discernment Counseling for mixed-agenda couples (one leaning-out, one leaning-in): a brief 1–5 session structure aimed at a confident decision among three paths, with central individual conversations, each partner's narrative and contributions, and hard contraindication screening for IPV/coercive control and undisclosed ongoing affairs.

prompts.title: EFT Couples Full-Arc Planner (Three Stages / Nine Steps)
prompts.description: Plan a complete Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) for couples treatment arc across Johnson's three stages and nine steps, anchored to negative-cycle mapping, attachment-injury identification, and EFT Tango moves.

prompts.title: Gottman Method Intervention Planner
prompts.description: Translate a Gottman assessment (Sound Relationship House, Four Horsemen, Love Maps, bids/turning, flooding/DPA, conflict typology) into a sequenced intervention plan with antidotes, friendship-building, conflict management, and physiological self-soothing.

prompts.title: IFS-Informed Couples Session Structure (Intimacy from the Inside Out)
prompts.description: Structure an IFS-informed couples session using the Intimacy from the Inside Out (Herbine-Blank) model: detect each partner's protective parts in the dynamic, run the U-turn, unblend, and facilitate courageous communication speaking-for (not speaking-from) parts with Self-energy in dialogue.

prompts.title: Structural Family Therapy Session Planner (Minuchin)
prompts.description: Plan a Structural Family Therapy session: join/accommodate, map the family structure (boundaries, subsystems, hierarchy, alignments/coalitions/triangulation), then sequence enactments, boundary-making, unbalancing, reframing, and restructuring.

prompts.title: Collateral Information Interview Protocol
prompts.description: Structured protocol for conducting a collateral informant interview at intake, with ROI scope adherence, domain-by-domain inquiry, and integration of collateral data into the clinical record.

prompts.title: Cultural Formulation Interview Drafter
prompts.description: Produce a structured Cultural Formulation Interview (CFI) narrative following DSM-5-TR supplementary module structure, with cultural identity, explanatory models, psychosocial stressors, and clinician-client relationship domains.

prompts.title: Developmental History Compiler
prompts.description: Compile a structured developmental history from prenatal through late adolescence for an adult psychiatric intake, covering milestones, adversity, learning, and psychosocial transitions.

prompts.title: Intake Screening Battery Interpreter
prompts.description: Compile and interpret an intake screening battery (PHQ-9, GAD-7, PCL-5, AUDIT, C-SSRS) into a clinician-ready summary with flag logic, score tables, and actionable clinical notes.

prompts.title: Medical History for Psychiatric Intake
prompts.description: Compile a psychiatric-relevant medical history section covering diagnoses, medications, labs, and conditions with bidirectional psychiatric-medical interaction for a 90791/90792 intake note.

prompts.title: Mental Status Exam Compiler
prompts.description: Compile a structured, fully descriptive Mental Status Exam from clinician interview observations, avoiding 'WNL' shorthand in favor of observed behavioral anchors.

prompts.title: Pediatric and Adolescent Intake with Caregiver
prompts.description: Structured biopsychosocial intake protocol for children and adolescents (ages 4–17) that manages parallel individual and caregiver inputs, developmental calibration, multi-informant integration, school functioning, and age-appropriate assent/consent, producing a CPT 90791/90792 intake note.

prompts.title: Psychiatric History Compiler
prompts.description: Compile a structured past psychiatric history covering prior diagnoses, providers, medications with response/side effects, hospitalizations, and longest period of stability for an adult intake.

prompts.title: Re-Intake After Lapse Protocol
prompts.description: Structured protocol for re-intake after a significant lapse in care — determining what to update vs. re-do, capturing the lapse interval, and re-establishing the treatment frame.

prompts.title: Substance Use History Intake Module
prompts.description: Per-substance history intake module with AUDIT and DAST-10 scoring interpretation, withdrawal risk screening, and ASAM criteria framing for level-of-care determination.

prompts.title: Telehealth-Only Practice Intake Protocol
prompts.description: Structured intake protocol for practices delivering care exclusively via telehealth, covering location attestation, platform verification, interstate licensure, safety and escalation planning, technology-fail contingency, and documentation requirements specific to synchronous audio-video encounters.

prompts.title: Trauma History Intake Module
prompts.description: Structured trauma-history intake module that elicits sufficient clinical data for formulation and treatment planning while respecting pacing, titration, and the client's chosen level of disclosure.

prompts.title: Individual ROM Trajectory Analyzer
prompts.description: Analyze one client's routine-outcome-monitoring (ROM) trajectory across sessions: response/remission status, expected-treatment-response comparison, not-on-track alerts, alliance (SRS) signal, and a session-level recommendation.

prompts.title: MBC Implementation Plan for a Practice
prompts.description: Build a measurement-based-care implementation plan for a practice or clinic (not a single client): instrument battery selection, workflow/EHR integration, staff roles, training, cadence policy, dashboards, change management, and fidelity metrics.

prompts.title: Outcome Monitoring Dashboard Interpreter
prompts.description: Interpret a panel/clinic-level outcome-monitoring dashboard (registry view): remission/response rates, average change, percent not-improved, caseload flags, equity/subgroup breakdowns, and quality-improvement actions.

prompts.title: Treatment Non-Response Decision Tree
prompts.description: A structured decision tree for when a client is not responding by the expected point: rule out measurement artifact, alliance, adherence, dose, diagnosis-fit, and comorbidity before sequencing reformulate / intensify / augment / switch modality / step up level of care / refer.

prompts.title: ACT Committed Action Planner
prompts.description: Convert a values statement into a committed-action plan with workability check, willingness check, specific behavioral steps, anticipated barriers (FEAR), and willingness graduation.

prompts.title: ACT Defusion Exercise Selector
prompts.description: Match a defusion exercise to the client's specific cognitive-fusion pattern (rule, comparison, evaluation, reason-giving, past/future) and the function fusion is currently serving.

prompts.title: ACT Group Protocol (Hexaflex-Sequenced)
prompts.description: Design a multi-session group-delivered ACT protocol sequenced across the hexaflex (acceptance, defusion, present-moment contact, self-as-context, values, committed action) plus creative hopelessness/workability, with experiential exercises and metaphors per process, group facilitation, homework, and a psychological-flexibility measurement plan.

prompts.title: ACT Matrix Session Facilitator
prompts.description: Facilitate an ACT Matrix session (Polk & Schoendorff): toward/away moves on the vertical axis, sensory experience / mental events on the horizontal axis, with workability sorting and committed-action bridge.

prompts.title: ACT Values Card Sort (Facilitated Clarification)
prompts.description: Facilitate an ACT values card sort to clarify life-domain values, sort by importance and current-living alignment, and produce a values map ready for committed-action planning.

prompts.title: Behavioral Parent Training Module (PCIT / BPT)
prompts.description: Build a behavioral parent training module anchored to PCIT (CDI/PRIDE + PDI) and the broader BPT lineage (Hanf, Kazdin PMT, Incredible Years, Triple P), producing PRIDE-skills coaching, command-quality review, an A-B-C behavior plan, and parent homework.

prompts.title: CBT Behavioral Experiment Designer
prompts.description: Design a Beckian behavioral experiment to test a specific belief (prediction or theory A vs theory B), including safety-behavior identification, outcome criteria, and post-experiment reformulation.

prompts.title: CBT End-of-Treatment Relapse Prevention Module
prompts.description: Generate a personal-manual relapse prevention module for end-of-CBT, including warning signs, personal coping toolkit, lapse vs relapse framework, booster-session plan, and self-as-own-therapist instructions.

prompts.title: CBT Thought Record Drafter (7-Column)
prompts.description: Draft a structured 7-column CBT thought record with cognitive restructuring and a balanced alternative thought, from session content or client homework.

prompts.title: CBT for Panic Disorder — Session Plan with Interoceptive Exposure
prompts.description: Generate a single-session CBT-Panic session plan (Barlow / Clark / Craske lineage) with psychoeducation, interoceptive exposure menu, cognitive work on catastrophic misinterpretation, and homework.

prompts.title: CBT for Social Anxiety — Session Plan with Video-Feedback and Safety-Behavior Dropping
prompts.description: Generate a CBT for Social Anxiety session plan (Clark & Wells / Heimberg lineage) including in-session role-play with video-feedback, dropping safety behaviors, and attention re-training.

prompts.title: Specific Phobia — One-Session Treatment (OST) Plan
prompts.description: Generate an Öst-style One-Session Treatment plan for specific phobia, including hierarchy construction, prolonged graded in-vivo exposure (up to 3 hours), and consolidation homework.

prompts.title: CPT (Cognitive Processing Therapy) Session Protocol
prompts.description: Generate a Cognitive Processing Therapy (Resick) session plan within the 12-session PTSD protocol: Impact Statement, Stuck Point Log, ABC sheets, Challenging Questions and Challenging Beliefs Worksheets, and the five themes (Safety, Trust, Power/Control, Esteem, Intimacy).

prompts.title: DBT Behavior Chain Analysis
prompts.description: Conduct a Linehan behavior chain analysis on a specific target behavior: vulnerability factors → prompting event → links (thoughts, sensations, actions, emotions) → problem behavior → consequences → solution analysis.

prompts.title: DBT Diary Card Analyzer (Weekly Review)
prompts.description: Process a week of DBT diary cards: target hierarchy review, skills use, urges/behaviors, emotion ratings, and produce a session agenda following Linehan's target hierarchy.

prompts.title: DBT Emotion Regulation Module — Lesson Plan
prompts.description: Generate a single skills-group lesson plan from Linehan's Emotion Regulation module (check the facts, opposite action, problem solving, PLEASE, building positive emotions, mindfulness of current emotion) with practice and homework.

prompts.title: DBT Skills Coaching Call Simulator
prompts.description: Simulate and structure a DBT phone-coaching call (24/7 between-session contact for skills, not therapy) within Linehan's contract: in-the-moment skill selection, brief, time-limited, not problem-solving.

prompts.title: DBT Target Hierarchy Session Organizer
prompts.description: Apply Linehan's stage-1 target hierarchy (life-threatening → therapy-interfering → quality-of-life → skills) to organize a single 50-minute DBT individual session with time blocks, agenda priority, and consultation-team flags.

prompts.title: Emotion-Focused Therapy (Individual) Session — Emotion Deepening
prompts.description: Structure an individual Emotion-Focused Therapy (Greenberg) session: classify emotions (primary adaptive / primary maladaptive / secondary reactive / instrumental), identify task markers, select chair-work or focusing interventions, and move through emotion-coaching stages to transformation.

prompts.title: EMDR AIP Case Formulation
prompts.description: Build an Adaptive Information Processing case formulation: maladaptive memory networks, present-day symptom drivers, positive networks available for linking, and treatment hypotheses ready for target sequencing.

prompts.title: EMDR Blocked Processing Troubleshooter
prompts.description: Diagnose blocked EMDR processing — looping, no SUDS movement, blocking belief, feeder memory, dissociation, or somatic block — and select a cognitive interweave, resource link, or pacing change.

prompts.title: EMDR Phase 2 Resource Development and Installation Protocol
prompts.description: Phase 2 resource development and installation (RDI) protocol: calm place, container, protector / nurturer / wise figure, adult-self, body resources, with short slow BLS for installation.

prompts.title: EMDR Target Sequence Organizer (Past / Present / Future)
prompts.description: Organize an EMDR target sequence across past contributors, present triggers, and future templates using cluster mapping and the Adaptive Information Processing (AIP) model.

prompts.title: Prolonged Exposure (PE) for PTSD — Session Plan
prompts.description: Generate a Prolonged Exposure (Foa) session plan: imaginal exposure to the trauma memory, hot-spot work, in-vivo hierarchy step, and processing — within the standard 8–15 session protocol.

prompts.title: Prolonged Grief Therapy (PGT) Session Protocol
prompts.description: Generate a Prolonged Grief Therapy / Complicated Grief Treatment (Shear) session plan within the 16-session protocol: dual loss/restoration focus (Dual Process Model), the seven core procedures, grief monitoring diary, aspirational goals, and imaginal/situational revisiting.

prompts.title: Group Therapy Curriculum Builder (Process or Psychoeducational)
prompts.description: Design a group therapy curriculum anchored to Yalom's therapeutic factors (process groups) and structured session-by-session skills design (DBT/CBT psychoeducational groups), producing a session curriculum table, group norms, and a screening/fit summary.

prompts.title: IFS Parts Mapping (Managers / Firefighters / Exiles + Self)
prompts.description: Map a client's internal-family system: protective managers, reactive firefighters, vulnerable exiles, and the Self's eight C qualities; produce a parts diagram with role, polarity, and burdens.

prompts.title: IFS Polarized Parts Resolution
prompts.description: Resolve a polarity between two parts (e.g., critic ↔ rebellious teen; caretaker ↔ resentful one) via Self-mediated dialogue, fear-disclosure, role-update, and joint commitment.

prompts.title: IFS Unburdening Session Structure (for an Exile)
prompts.description: Structure a phased IFS unburdening session for an exile: protector permission, witnessing, retrieval, unburdening (release of extreme belief / feeling), invitation of qualities, and integration.

prompts.title: MI Ambivalence Map (Two-Column + Double-Sided Reflections)
prompts.description: Map ambivalence as a structured two-column exploration with double-sided reflections that integrate sustain and change, plus a values-bridge to evoke commitment talk.

prompts.title: MI Change-Talk Coder (DARN-CAT Transcript Coding)
prompts.description: Code a session transcript or excerpt for DARN-CAT change talk vs sustain talk, with line-by-line tags, frequency tallies, MI-adherence audit, and feedback for the interviewer.

prompts.title: MI Decisional Balance Facilitator
prompts.description: Facilitate a Motivational Interviewing decisional balance exercise for an ambivalent change topic, using equipoise or change-favoring frames per Miller & Rollnick's MI-4 guidance.

prompts.title: MI OARS Response Generator
prompts.description: Generate Open question, Affirmation, Reflection (simple + complex), and Summary responses for a given client utterance, with reasoning for each and an MI-adherence note.

prompts.title: Narrative Therapy Externalizing Conversation Session
prompts.description: Structure a White & Epston narrative-therapy externalizing conversation that separates the person from the problem, maps relative influence, surfaces unique outcomes, and bridges toward a re-authored preferred story.

prompts.title: Psychodynamic Process Note (Transference / Defenses / Enactments)
prompts.description: Generate a psychodynamic process-focused session note capturing transference, countertransference, defenses, enactments, and the therapist's interventions and reasoning — distinct from a problem-oriented progress note.

prompts.title: Psychodynamic Transference-Focused Psychotherapy (TFP) Formulation
prompts.description: Build a TFP-style object-relations formulation (Kernberg / Yeomans / Clarkin): dominant object-relations dyads, self / other representations, predominant affect, primitive defenses, identity integration, and reality-testing — with treatment-frame and tactical priorities.

prompts.title: Schema Mode Mapper (Young)
prompts.description: Map active schema modes — Vulnerable Child, Angry/Impulsive Child, Punitive/Demanding Parent, Detached Protector / Self-Soother / Compliant Surrenderer / Bully-Attack, and Healthy Adult — using Young's Schema Mode Inventory framework with a session-specific mode formulation.

prompts.title: Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT) Session Structure
prompts.description: Generate a Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (de Shazer & Berg) session structure: presession change, miracle question, scaling questions, exception and coping questions, well-formed goals, the break, and an end-of-session message (compliments + bridge + task).

prompts.title: Polyvagal-Informed Stabilization & Regulation Plan
prompts.description: Build a Porges/Deb-Dana polyvagal-informed stabilization plan: a personal autonomic ladder (ventral/sympathetic/dorsal) with neuroception cues, glimmers, and per-state regulation anchors plus a daily practice plan.

prompts.title: Sensorimotor / Somatic Session Plan (Window of Tolerance)
prompts.description: Plan a Sensorimotor Psychotherapy (Ogden) / Somatic Experiencing (Levine) session organized around the Window of Tolerance (Siegel): track sensation across the three levels of processing, titrate and pendulate within the window, and complete thwarted defensive responses safely.

prompts.title: Adolescent DBT Skills Module
prompts.description: Age-adapted DBT-A skills module for teens that delivers a single skills target (mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, or Walking the Middle Path) with diary-card review and caregiver/family inclusion, producing a CPT 90853/90837 note.

prompts.title: Adolescent Intake with Developmental Lens
prompts.description: Structured biopsychosocial intake for adolescents (ages 12–17) that centers identity, peer, family, and school domains, applies validated adolescent screeners, manages confidentiality and minor consent, and produces a CPT 90791/90792 note.

prompts.title: Child Play Therapy Session Note
prompts.description: Progress note for an individual play therapy session with a child (ages 3–11) that frames play themes developmentally, links observed play content to treatment goals, and produces a CPT 90837/90834 documentation record.

prompts.title: Pediatric Anxiety Protocol Session Plan
prompts.description: Coping Cat / Cool Kids–style manualized session plan for child and adolescent anxiety that sequences psychoeducation, somatic skills, cognitive restructuring, and graded exposure with caregiver involvement, producing a CPT 90834/90837 session note.

prompts.title: Pediatric Safety Planning with Caregiver
prompts.description: Dyadic Stanley-Brown–adapted safety plan built with both the youth and caregiver, integrating Columbia C-SSRS risk stratification, developmentally calibrated warning signs and coping steps, caregiver-led means restriction, and a documented risk-reassessment loop.

prompts.title: School Collaboration: 504/IEP Mental-Health Input
prompts.description: Structured mental-health clinician input for a 504 Plan or IEP meeting that translates diagnosis and functional impairment into educational-impact language and proposes evidence-based accommodations, within the bounds of clinician scope and FERPA/release authorization.

prompts.title: Couples Therapy Intake — EFT or Gottman Frame
prompts.description: Structured conjoint and individual couples intake that mandates IPV/safety screening of each partner separately, maps the negative interaction cycle, and frames assessment and treatment planning through Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) or the Gottman Method.

prompts.title: Family Therapy Intake — Systemic (Genogram + Presenting-Problem Mapping)
prompts.description: Systemic family intake that builds a three-generation genogram, maps the presenting problem across the family system, reframes the identified patient, and assesses boundaries and subsystems, producing a CPT 90847/90846 family diagnostic record.

prompts.title: Grief Assessment — Prolonged Grief Disorder vs. Normal Grief
prompts.description: Differential assessment distinguishing DSM-5-TR/ICD-11 Prolonged Grief Disorder from normal/acute grief and from MDD, with duration-threshold logic, named grief instruments, suicide-risk screen, and a documented diagnostic determination.

prompts.title: Group Therapy Member Screening (Fit and Suitability)
prompts.description: Pre-group screening that evaluates a prospective member's fit for a process or psychoeducational group using Yalom-informed inclusion/exclusion criteria, therapeutic-factor matching, risk screen, and group informed consent, producing a placement recommendation.

prompts.title: Geriatric Depression vs. Dementia Differential (Pseudodementia Screening)
prompts.description: Structured differential framework distinguishing depression-related cognitive impairment (pseudodementia) from early neurodegenerative dementia in older adults, integrating GDS, Mini-Cog/MoCA/MMSE, Cornell scale, Wells' pseudodementia features, and an elevated late-life suicide risk screen.

prompts.title: Geriatric Grief and Late-Life Transitions
prompts.description: Assessment-and-intervention scaffold for late-life grief, cumulative and disenfranchised loss, identity and role transitions (retirement, caregiving, widowhood, relocation, functional decline), distinguishing normative grief, prolonged grief disorder, and grief-related depression while screening elevated late-life suicide risk.

prompts.title: Geriatric Intake with Polypharmacy and Falls-Risk Review
prompts.description: Structured biopsychosocial intake for older adults (65+) that integrates a medication / polypharmacy review (Beers Criteria, anticholinergic burden, STOPP/START), falls-risk assessment (Morse, TUG), functional status (Katz ADL, Lawton IADL), cognitive and late-life suicide screens, producing a CPT 90791 intake note with referral hooks.

prompts.title: Gender-Affirming Care Letter Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a behavioral-health referral/assessment letter for gender-affirming medical care structured to WPATH Standards of Care Version 8 content elements, documenting persistent gender incongruence, capacity to consent, and mental health context while leaving medical-necessity determinations to the clinician.

prompts.title: LGBTQ+ Affirmative Intake Module
prompts.description: Identity-affirmative biopsychosocial intake module that elicits sexual orientation, gender identity, and embodiment history with affirming language, applies Meyer's minority-stress framing, screens elevated suicide risk, and produces a CPT 90791 intake record.

prompts.title: Minority-Stress Case Formulation
prompts.description: Apply Meyer's minority-stress model to build a case formulation for an LGBTQ+ client — mapping distal stressors, proximal processes, resilience and community connectedness, and intersectional context to symptoms and treatment targets.

prompts.title: Adult ADHD Assessment Intake Module
prompts.description: Structured adult ADHD assessment intake that documents executive-function history, retrospective childhood onset, the DSM-5-TR criteria across inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive domains, validated rating scales (ASRS, CAARS, DIVA-5, Wender Utah), and elevated risk, producing a CPT 90791 intake record.

prompts.title: Adult Autism Assessment Intake Module
prompts.description: Masking-aware adult autism assessment intake that gathers developmental and current-functioning history, screens with RAADS-R / AQ / CAT-Q, distinguishes neurotype from co-occurring treatable conditions, and produces a CPT 90791 intake record.

prompts.title: Neurodivergent-Affirming Treatment Planning
prompts.description: A treatment-planning framework for neurodivergent adults that targets distress, co-occurring conditions, and environmental fit rather than the neurotype itself — applying the double empathy problem, identity-affirming language, accommodation over normalization, autistic-burnout recovery, and an explicit co-occurring-vs-neurotype distinction, with a golden-thread plan and elevated-risk hooks.

prompts.title: PDA (Pathological/Persistent Demand Avoidance) Framework
prompts.description: A PDA-aware clinical framework for assessing and responding to extreme demand-avoidance presentations within the autism spectrum, distinguishing PDA from ODD, oppositionality, anxiety, and trauma, and translating findings into a low-demand, accommodation-based, collaborative approach.

prompts.title: Perinatal Mood and Anxiety Screen Interpretation (EPDS / PHQ-9 / GAD-7)
prompts.description: Interpret perinatal depression and anxiety screens (EPDS, PHQ-9, GAD-7) with population-appropriate cutoffs, the EPDS item-10 self-harm flag, and a structured disposition pathway.

prompts.title: Perinatal Treatment Options Across Pregnancy and Lactation
prompts.description: Organize psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy considerations for perinatal mood/anxiety across pregnancy and lactation using a shared risk-benefit frame, with named verification resources and no fabricated drug safety ratings.

prompts.title: Postpartum Psychosis Recognition and Emergency Referral
prompts.description: Recognize postpartum psychosis as a psychiatric emergency, stratify urgency, screen infant safety, and execute same-day disposition (ED / psychiatric admission / 988) with risk-reassessment hooks.

prompts.title: Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) Engagement & Outreach Plan
prompts.description: Multidisciplinary ACT-team engagement and in-vivo outreach plan for an adult with serious mental illness who is disengaged from care or at risk of disengagement — built on ACT fidelity principles (shared caseload, low staff-to-client ratio, assertive in-community outreach, 24/7 availability), with an engagement-stage assessment, role assignments, outreach sequencing, and integrated risk-and-disengagement monitoring.

prompts.title: First-Episode Psychosis Intake with CHR/FEP Differentiation
prompts.description: Structured intake for first-episode psychosis (FEP) that differentiates clinical high risk (CHR) / attenuated psychosis syndrome from frank first-episode psychosis, estimates duration of untreated psychosis (DUP), and routes to Coordinated Specialty Care, producing a CPT 90791/90792 intake record.

prompts.title: SMI Medication Adherence Motivational Plan (MI-Based)
prompts.description: Motivational-interviewing–based adherence plan for adults on antipsychotics or mood stabilizers, mapping ambivalence about medication, eliciting and reinforcing change talk (DARN-CAT) with OARS, supporting side-effect-informed shared decision making (including LAI discussion), and producing a collaborative adherence-support plan rather than a compliance directive.

prompts.title: SMI Recovery-Oriented Treatment Plan
prompts.description: Recovery-oriented, person-centered treatment plan for adults with serious mental illness organized across SAMHSA recovery domains — health/symptom, home/housing, purpose/work-education, and community/social — integrating psychiatric rehabilitation, supported employment (IPS), WRAP, relapse-signature monitoring, and client-defined recovery goals measured with the Recovery Assessment Scale.

prompts.title: Combat Trauma Formulation with Moral Injury
prompts.description: Advanced case formulation for combat-exposed veterans that integrates PTSD symptom architecture with the moral injury construct (Litz et al.), differentiates fear-based PTSD from transgression-based moral injury, anchors index events, and maps evidence-based treatment options while maintaining a continuous suicide-risk lens.

prompts.title: Military Sexual Trauma (MST)-Aware Engagement and Treatment Planning Protocol
prompts.description: Advanced, trauma-informed protocol for engaging veterans who screen positive for Military Sexual Trauma (MST), addressing universal screening, harassment vs. assault, institutional betrayal, gender-inclusive presentation, VA free MST-related care eligibility regardless of service-connection, and continuous suicide-risk management, leading to a phased treatment plan.

prompts.title: Veteran Intake with Service History
prompts.description: Service-history-informed biopsychosocial intake for veterans and active/reserve service members that captures military service context, combat and trauma exposure, MST screening, and elevated suicide risk, producing a CPT 90791 intake note.

prompts.title: Insurance Verification (Benefits Check) Intake Protocol
prompts.description: Run a structured benefits-verification at intake — eligibility, in/out-of-network, copay/coinsurance/deductible, telehealth coverage, prior-auth and session limits, CPT-code coverage — and document plus read back the result to the client.

prompts.title: Missed-Appointment / Late-Cancellation Policy Letter Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a no-show and late-cancellation policy letter or consent clause with fee, notice window, insurance-cannot-be-billed note, telehealth applicability, and a repeated-no-show discharge pathway.

prompts.title: Records-Request Response Decision Aid
prompts.description: Decide how to respond to a request for mental-health records — distinguishing a HIPAA patient-access request, a valid third-party authorization, a subpoena (not self-executing), and a court order — with the psychotherapy-notes carve-out, minor/guardian and 42 CFR Part 2 wrinkles, and what to release, withhold, or require first.

prompts.title: Superbill Generator (Out-of-Network Claim)
prompts.description: Generate a compliant superbill for a client's out-of-network reimbursement claim — provider NPI/tax-ID, rendering vs billing provider, dates of service, CPT + modifiers + units, ICD-10 diagnosis codes, charges, payments, and the required statement language.

prompts.title: Telehealth State-of-Licensure Decision Aid
prompts.description: Decide whether you may legally see a telehealth client based on the CLIENT's physical location at session time — covering PSYPACT (E.Passport/APIT), temporary-practice exceptions, emergency carve-outs, and required documentation of client location and a local safety contact.

prompts.title: ADHD Pharmacologic Algorithm Reasoner (Stimulant / Non-Stimulant)
prompts.description: Reason through stimulant (methylphenidate vs amphetamine class) and non-stimulant (atomoxetine, viloxazine, alpha-2 agonists) selection, titration, cardiac/BP/growth monitoring, diversion-and-misuse mitigation, and comorbidity sequencing for ADHD.

prompts.title: Anxiety Pharmacologic Algorithm Reasoner (GAD / Panic / SAD)
prompts.description: Reason through pharmacologic management of generalized anxiety, panic disorder, and social anxiety disorder: SSRI/SNRI first-line, activation-aware titration, benzodiazepine role and risks, buspirone, and pregabalin/hydroxyzine/propranolol adjuncts, with CBT/exposure integration.

prompts.title: Bipolar Pharmacologic Algorithm Reasoner (Mania / Bipolar Depression / Maintenance)
prompts.description: Reason through mood-stabilizer, antipsychotic, and antidepressant decisions across bipolar phases — acute mania, bipolar depression, and maintenance — including lithium, valproate, lamotrigine, atypicals, antidepressant-switch caution, level/lab monitoring, and pregnancy considerations.

prompts.title: Controlled-Substance Treatment Agreement Drafter
prompts.description: Draft a controlled-substance treatment agreement for the chart (stimulant or benzodiazepine): single-prescriber/single-pharmacy terms, PDMP checks, lost/early-refill policy, UDS, safe storage, diversion consequences, and signatures.

prompts.title: Depression Pharmacologic Algorithm Reasoner (MDD)
prompts.description: Reason through pharmacologic management of major depressive disorder: first-line agent selection, adequate-trial definition, partial- vs non-response branching, switch/augmentation strategies, treatment-resistant options, and measurement-based anchoring.

prompts.title: Initial Psychiatric Evaluation Drafter (90792)
prompts.description: Draft an initial psychiatric diagnostic evaluation note billable as 90792 (with medical services): CC/HPI, ROS, full histories, MSE, risk, workup, DSM-5-TR formulation, initial medication plan, and informed-consent documentation.

prompts.title: Medication Management Progress Note (E&M + Psychotherapy Add-On)
prompts.description: Draft an E&M-style medication management follow-up note (99213/99214, with optional 90833 psychotherapy add-on) with interval history, target-symptom and side-effect tracking, focused MSE, MDM justification of the E&M level, and medication decisions.

prompts.title: Psychotropic Taper Plan Builder
prompts.description: Build a class-specific taper plan for SSRI/SNRI, benzodiazepine, antipsychotic, or mood stabilizer discontinuation — with per-class taper rates, crossover/bridging logic, monitoring, and abort/hold criteria.

prompts.title: Civil Commitment / Involuntary Hold Narrative
prompts.description: Draft an involuntary-hold narrative (e.g., 5150 / state equivalent) that documents danger to self / danger to others / grave disability with specific behavioral evidence and least-restrictive-alternative reasoning suitable for review by a hearing officer.

prompts.title: Columbia (C-SSRS) Suicide Risk Assessment Drafter
prompts.description: Produce a structured suicide risk assessment using the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale framework (ideation severity & intensity, behavior, lethality), integrating static / dynamic / protective factors and producing an explicit risk stratification and disposition.

prompts.title: Homicidal Ideation Triage and Documentation
prompts.description: Conduct and document a structured homicidal-ideation triage covering target identifiability, plan, means, intent, ideation type (egodystonic vs egosyntonic), risk stratification, and disposition including duty-to-protect analysis.

prompts.title: In-Session Crisis De-Escalation and Disposition Plan
prompts.description: Build a real-time, in-session crisis plan when acute risk emerges mid-encounter: rapid risk re-stratification, agreed-upon safety actions before the client leaves, contingency tree if the client refuses, and post-session follow-through.

prompts.title: Lethal Means Counseling (CALM-Style) Conversation Builder
prompts.description: Generate a CALM-style lethal-means counseling conversation covering firearms, medications, and other means, with concrete time-and-distance interventions, family involvement, and documentation.

prompts.title: Mandated Reporter Decision Walkthrough (CPS / APS)
prompts.description: Walk through a mandated-reporter decision for suspected child abuse or neglect or vulnerable-adult abuse: reasonable-suspicion threshold, jurisdictional rules, what triggers a report vs document-and-monitor, how to make the report, client conversation, and post-report therapy continuity.

prompts.title: NSSI Functional Assessment and Replacement-Skill Plan
prompts.description: Conduct a four-function analysis of non-suicidal self-injury, identify maintaining factors, and build a matched replacement-skill plan with explicit harm-reduction and safety integration.

prompts.title: Post-Attempt Re-Engagement Plan (After ED / Inpatient)
prompts.description: Build a structured re-engagement plan for clients re-entering outpatient care after a suicide attempt and ED or inpatient stay, focused on stigma-aware reconnection, narrative reconstruction, updated safety plan, means-restriction follow-through, and family loop-in.

prompts.title: Stanley-Brown Safety Planning Intervention Builder
prompts.description: Co-construct a Stanley-Brown safety plan with a client across the canonical 6 steps: warning signs, internal coping, social distractions, people for help, professionals/agencies, and means restriction.

prompts.title: Tarasoff / Duty-to-Protect Analysis
prompts.description: Walk through an identifiable-victim duty-to-protect analysis using a state-by-state aware framework: foreseeability, options (warn, hospitalize, treat differently, notify law enforcement), and documentation standards.

prompts.title: ACT for Chronic Pain — Health Psychology Session Protocol
prompts.description: Generate an ACT for chronic pain session plan across the psychological-flexibility hexaflex with values-based pacing, defusion, and acceptance — workability over pain reduction.

prompts.title: Adjustment to Chronic Illness — Intervention Plan
prompts.description: Generate an adjustment-to-chronic-illness intervention plan (Lazarus & Folkman transactional coping; Leventhal self-regulation/illness representations; ACT values) with illness-representation assessment, coping matched to controllability, adjustment-vs-MDD differentiation, and medical-team coordination.

prompts.title: Behavioral Addiction CBT — Gambling / Gaming / Behavioral-Addiction Protocol
prompts.description: Generate a CBT session/episode plan for behavioral addiction (gambling disorder, gaming disorder, problematic internet use) with functional analysis, cognitive correction of gambling-related distortions, stimulus control, and relapse prevention.

prompts.title: Bipolar Disorder IPSRT — Interpersonal & Social Rhythm Therapy Protocol
prompts.description: Generate an IPSRT session plan (Frank; social zeitgeber theory) with Social Rhythm Metric tracking, rhythm stabilization, an interpersonal problem-area focus, prodrome monitoring, and prescriber coordination.

prompts.title: CBT-I Adapted for Comorbid Pain or PTSD — Provider Protocol with Safety Carve-Outs
prompts.description: Generate a CBT-I session plan adapted for comorbid chronic pain or PTSD, with safety carve-out screening before sleep restriction, sleep-compression alternative, Imagery Rehearsal Therapy for nightmares, and prescriber coordination (e.g., prazosin).

prompts.title: CBT-I — Provider Sleep Protocol (Sleep Restriction, Stimulus Control, Titration)
prompts.description: Generate a CBT-I session plan that computes prescribed time-in-bed from sleep-diary data, applies stimulus control, and titrates by sleep efficiency.

prompts.title: Eating Disorder CBT-E — Session Protocol (Regular Eating & Weight Monitoring)
prompts.description: Generate a stage-anchored CBT-E session plan with regular eating, collaborative in-session weighing, and dietary-rule work for transdiagnostic eating disorders.

prompts.title: Family-Based Treatment (FBT) — Phase Planner for Adolescent Eating Disorders
prompts.description: Generate a phase-anchored FBT plan that mobilizes parents to refeed, externalizes the illness, and sequences phase transitions to weight restoration and adolescent autonomy.

prompts.title: Hoarding Disorder CBT — Sorting/Discarding Protocol
prompts.description: Generate a CBT session plan for hoarding disorder (Steketee & Frost) with CIR/SI-R baselining, decision-making and categorization skills, in-home sorting/non-acquisition practice, cognitive work on beliefs, and life-safety hazard screening.

prompts.title: OCD Exposure & Response Prevention (ERP) — Provider Protocol
prompts.description: Generate an inhibitory-learning ERP session plan with a SUDS hierarchy, in-vivo and imaginal exposures, full response prevention, and family-accommodation reduction.

prompts.title: Sex Therapy — Assessment and Intervention Plan (PLISSIT-Aware)
prompts.description: Generate a biopsychosocial sex-therapy assessment and PLISSIT-tiered intervention plan with sensate-focus structuring, medical rule-out, and coercion/IPV screening.

prompts.title: Somatic Symptom Disorder — Reattribution & CBT Protocol
prompts.description: Generate a CBT/reattribution session plan for somatic symptom disorder and health anxiety (Barsky; Warwick & Salkovskis) with symptom-reality validation, the feeling-understood/broaden-agenda/make-the-link structure, behavioral experiments on checking and reassurance-seeking, and medical-team coordination.

prompts.title: Board-Exam Vignette Study Tool
prompts.description: Generate board-style (EPPP / licensing / specialty) vignette items with best-answer reasoning, distractor analysis, and the principle or standard being tested — for exam preparation and supervision teaching.

prompts.title: Clinical Vignette / Teaching Case Generator
prompts.description: Generate a de-identified teaching case or vignette from a real case for didactics, supervision, or board prep — with learning objectives, discussion questions, and a HIPAA-grade de-identification checklist.

prompts.title: Countertransference Reflection Prompt
prompts.description: Structured countertransference reflection for a supervisee — triggers, somatic/affective signals, origin hypotheses, impact on the work, and a management plan that keeps the supervision/therapy boundary intact.

prompts.title: Dual-Relationship / Boundary Analyzer
prompts.description: Analyze a multiple/dual relationship under APA Standard 3.05 — distinguish boundary crossing from violation, assess risk of harm, exploitation, impairment of judgment, and foreseeability, and produce a management/mitigation plan.

prompts.title: Ethics Consultation Walkthrough
prompts.description: Work an ethical dilemma through a named decision model — problem identification, applicable ethics-code standards, stakeholders, options, principle balancing, decision, and documentation — for supervision or peer consultation.

prompts.title: Parallel Process Detector
prompts.description: Detect and name parallel-process dynamics (client → therapist → supervisor mirroring) with supporting evidence, competing hypotheses, and a supervisory intervention plan.

prompts.title: Scope-of-Practice / Boundaries-of-Competence Decision Aid
prompts.description: Analyze boundaries-of-competence ambiguity (new population, modality, or setting) under APA Standard 2.01 — with a competence-acquisition vs. refer-out decision, supervision/consultation pathway, and licensure/credential considerations.

prompts.title: Supervision Agenda Builder
prompts.description: Build a structured, time-boxed clinical-supervision agenda from a supervisee's caseload that prioritizes high-risk and high-acuity cases, mandated topics, and developmental goals.

prompts.title: Golden Thread Writer
prompts.description: Walk a single problem through the complete problem → goal → SMART objective → intervention → measurement chain to produce a self-consistent, audit-ready golden thread.

prompts.title: Measurement-Based Care Plan
prompts.description: Build a measurement-based care (MBC) plan specifying instrument selection, administration cadence, scoring interpretation, and a feedback-to-treatment-decision protocol.

prompts.title: Modality Selection Decision Aid
prompts.description: Match a clinical presentation to the best-fit evidence-based modality — CBT, DBT, ACT, EMDR, psychodynamic, or IFS — using structured decision logic.

prompts.title: Referral Decision Aid — Within Episode
prompts.description: Determine when to refer out for adjunct care (psychiatry, specialist therapy, medical, peer support) while continuing the primary treatment relationship.

prompts.title: Relapse Prevention Plan Designer
prompts.description: Design an end-of-treatment relapse prevention plan with individualized warning signs, high-risk situations, coping responses, and support contacts.

prompts.title: SMART Treatment Goal Generator
prompts.description: Convert a clinical problem statement into SMART goals with objective-level measurement criteria suitable for treatment-plan documentation.

prompts.title: Stepped Care Decision Aid
prompts.description: Determine the appropriate level of care — outpatient to inpatient — and decide when to step up, step down, or hold using LOCUS criteria and clinical indicators.

prompts.title: Treatment Resistance Reformulation
prompts.description: When the current plan is not producing meaningful change, systematically reformulate — without abandoning the client — by diagnosing the failure before changing the treatment.

prompts.title: Bias-Specific Audit — Test a Conclusion Against a Named Cognitive Bias
prompts.description: Audit a conclusion or analysis against a single named cognitive bias (confirmation, availability, anchoring, survivorship, hindsight, base-rate neglect, narrative fallacy, sunk cost, attribution error). Each bias has its own diagnostic, evidence pattern to look for, and remediation. Targeted audit beats generic 'check for bias' instruction.

prompts.title: Claim / Inference Separator — Untangle Observation, Claim, and Inference
prompts.description: Walk a passage sentence by sentence and tag each unit as pure observation (directly seen/measured), claim (an assertion the author makes), or inference (a conclusion drawn from observations and claims), surfacing where inferences are dressed as observations and where claims are smuggled inside what reads like neutral description. Counters the failure mode of accepting a confident narrative whole because the inferential leaps are hidden inside descriptive prose.

prompts.title: Disagreement Diagnosis — Empirical, Definitional, or Normative?
prompts.description: Take a stuck disagreement between two parties (or two positions in your own head) and diagnose its layers: empirical (about facts), definitional (about what words mean), normative (about what should be valued), and reference-class (about which comparable cases should anchor judgment). Most stuck disagreements have multiple layers; surfacing them ends false-deadlocks.

prompts.title: Evidence Against Yourself — Generate the Strongest Disconfirming Case for Your Own Position
prompts.description: For a position the user holds, generate the strongest empirical, theoretical, and structural evidence *against* it. Distinct from steelmanning the opponent's view: this prompt focuses on disconfirming the user's own claim, including evidence the user has not yet encountered. Used as a final adversarial check before commitment.

prompts.title: Evidence Quality Score — Rate a Piece of Evidence on a Transparent Rubric
prompts.description: Score a single piece of evidence (study, dataset, expert opinion, anecdote, news report) on a transparent multi-criterion rubric — design, sample, replication, source credibility, conflict of interest, recency, relevance — with a 1–5 score and justification per criterion, a composite with a confidence range, and a one-line statement of the load-bearing weakness. Counters the failure mode of treating all citations as equally probative and of letting a single strong-sounding source carry a conclusion it can't bear.

prompts.title: Logical Fallacy Scan — Detect Named Fallacies With Cited Evidence
prompts.description: Scan a passage against a catalog of ~15 named logical fallacies, quoting the offending sentence for each candidate and distinguishing the mere rhetorical use of a fallacy from genuine commission (where the argument's conclusion actually depends on the bad inference). Counters the failure mode of fallacy-spotting as a debate weapon — labeling without quoting, and treating every rhetorical flourish as a load-bearing logical error.

prompts.title: Motivated Reasoning Check — The Symmetry Test for Asymmetric Standards
prompts.description: Run the asymmetric-standards test: take a conclusion the user holds and the evidence supporting it, then ask, item by item, whether they would accept that same evidence if it pointed the opposite way. Surfaces where the evidentiary bar is being applied asymmetrically — accepting weak support for the favored side while demanding strong support against it. Counters the failure mode of confusing 'I have evidence for this' with 'I would believe this regardless of which way the evidence cut.'

prompts.title: Red Team Briefing — Build and Rehearse the Case Against Your Own Conclusion
prompts.description: Before shipping a thesis, memo, presentation, or position, construct the strongest opposition: the most credible critic (real or composite), their strongest argument, their strongest evidence, and their single most cutting question — then pre-draft responses to each. Distinct from surfacing disconfirming evidence; this rehearses the specific adversary's attack so the author isn't surprised in the room. Counters the failure mode of shipping a position that's only ever been pressure-tested by its author.

prompts.title: Source Credibility Triangulation — Compare Sources on Credibility, Not Content
prompts.description: Compare three or more sources on credibility dimensions — track record on this topic, methodological transparency, conflict-of-interest disclosure, citation patterns, expertise match — to surface where credibility differs and where it converges, independent of what the sources actually claim. Counters the failure mode of weighting sources by how confident or articulate they sound, and of conflating agreement-on-content with independent-credibility.

prompts.title: Uncertainty Acknowledgment Audit — Match Stated Certainty to Actual Evidence
prompts.description: Audit a draft (memo, paper, recommendation) for false certainty, flagging every claim where the certainty stated exceeds the evidence available — bare assertions that should be probabilistic, quantitative claims missing intervals, inferential leaps missing limitations, and attribution inflation ('research suggests' when it's one paper). The goal is calibrated certainty, not hedging everywhere. Counters both overconfidence and its overcorrection into mush where every sentence is buried in qualifiers.

prompts.title: Base Rate Establishment — Anchor on History Before Anchoring on Case Features
prompts.description: For a forecast about to be made, establish the historical base rate of the event class before incorporating case-specific information. Define the event class, sample comparable past cases, compute historical frequency, check stability/trend, and produce the base rate as a range. Lighter and faster than reasoning_reference_class_forecast.md; designed as a pre-step before case-specific reasoning.

prompts.title: Brier Tracker Design — Personal Forecasting Log Spec
prompts.description: Design a personal forecasting log for someone starting calibration practice. Specifies what to log per forecast, what to log at resolution, review cadence, metrics tracked (Brier, calibration curve, resolution counts), and how to act on the log. Output is a template the user can copy into a spreadsheet or notes app.

prompts.title: Calibration Self-Audit — Score Past Predictions, Surface Calibration Patterns
prompts.description: Score a log of past predictions: of forecasts you said were 70% likely, what fraction came true? Group by probability bin, compute resolution per bin, identify systematic over- or underconfidence, and identify domains where calibration is best vs worst. Output: calibration improvement plan.

prompts.title: Long Horizon, Radical Uncertainty — Posture-Based Reasoning When No Priors Exist
prompts.description: For 10–30 year forecasts, novel-domain forecasts, or civilizational-scale questions where reference classes and base rates are unavailable, build robust postures rather than predictions. Surfaces structural drivers, separates forecastable from radically uncertain, identifies near-term observables that would update the model, and accepts that point forecasts are inappropriate.

prompts.title: Probabilistic Question Design — Convert Vague Predictions into Resolvable Questions
prompts.description: Convert a fuzzy claim ('the market will turn', 'this will work out', 'X will happen soon') into 1–3 well-formed forecast questions where any informed observer would agree on resolution. Specifies who judges, by what observable, by what date, with what threshold for yes/no, and what edge cases. Calibrated to Good Judgment / Metaculus standards.

prompts.title: Scenario Probability Assignment — Probabilities Across Mutually-Exclusive Scenarios
prompts.description: Once a scenario set exists, assign probabilities to the enumerated scenarios plus a mandatory 5–10% 'other / unforeseen' reserve, together summing to 1.0; justify each via base rate or mechanism, identify the two most uncertain probabilities, stress-test by varying ±20%, and surface implications for which scenarios deserve preparation, monitoring, or can be ignored.

prompts.title: Signal vs Noise Filter — Triage New Information Against an Existing Forecast
prompts.description: Triage a stream of new information items against an existing forecast. Score each: signal or noise? Direction? Magnitude? Cumulative effect on forecast in the period? Recommended forecast adjustment (or none). Counters two failures: ignoring genuine signal and over-updating on noise.

prompts.title: Super-Forecaster Decomposition — Tetlock-Style Sub-Question Tree
prompts.description: Decompose a fuzzy forecast into a tree of sub-questions whose answers can be estimated more reliably than the parent. Combine sub-question estimates back into a parent probability with explicit aggregation logic. Improves forecast resolution by isolating estimable components from speculative ones.

prompts.title: What Would Change My Mind — Falsifiability Tripwires for a Belief or Forecast
prompts.description: Force a forecaster or believer to specify in advance what observable evidence would move their belief by stated amounts in either direction. Produces tripwires the user agrees to honor when triggered, defeats motivated reasoning ex post, and exposes beliefs that are unfalsifiable (and therefore not really forecasts).

prompts.title: Abductive Inference — Best Explanations for an Observation
